plans.title: Load-out confirm moves only the counted van stock; the packed orders' lots (sold at pack) are no longer taken from the godown a second time
plans.rootCause:
Stock leaves the godown twice for the same goods. The warehouse brief is the outlier: every other design source already says packed pieces leave once, at pack.

1) Pack takes the stock out.
- PackingService.confirm (backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/packing.service.ts:96) calls InventoryService.postPick.
- postPick (backend/libs/core/src/modules/inventory/inventory.service.ts:446-460) writes one `reason:'sale'`, `-picked` row per lot at the godown, with ref_type 'pack'.
- The class comment says so (packing.service.ts:48-66, "STOCK LEAVES EXACTLY ONCE").
- The invoice is issued from the same lot quantities.

2) Load-out takes the same lots out again.
- LoadSheetsService.confirm (backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/load-sheets.service.ts:329) builds `lots = await loadSheetLots(tx, counted)` at line 371.
- loadSheetLots (backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/warehouse.mappers.ts:466-484) merges the pack's own `sale` rows (packedLotsByOrder, :344-373) with the counted van stock.
- Lines 379-401 then post `transfer_out -qty` at `sheet.fromLocationId` and `transfer_in +qty` at the vehicle for every merged lot, packed lots included.

3) What that does, depending on the lot.
- Lot fully sold at pack: the godown balance hits `stock_balances_on_hand_nonneg` (backend/libs/database/src/schema/inventory.ts:172). applyBalance turns that into 400 "insufficient stock … would go below zero" (inventory.service.ts:740-745). The transaction rolls back, including its idempotency row (platform/idempotency.ts:56-75).
- Lot with surplus: the confirm succeeds, godown on-hand drops a second time, and the vehicle gains phantom pieces.

4) The rest of the design already assumes packed goods never move at load-out.
- docs/plans/delivery.md:17 and :84: pre-sold pieces left the ledger as `sale` at pick; returns go into the vehicle; check-in moves the counted remainder back.
- docs/plans/delivery.md:31: the load sheet confirm "posts transfer_out warehouse / transfer_in vehicle for free van stock".
- trips.service.ts:843-858 (dispatchIfPacked) dispatches a packed order at depart and posts no stock.
- trips.service.ts:740 and :860, and deliveries.service.ts:178-180: a failed stop moves no stock.
- vansales.service.ts:84 and :99 sell from the vehicle location.
- settlement.service.ts:376-404 expects the van to hold exactly its stock_balances rows, and unloads or cycle-counts against them. With packed lots transferred onto the van, check-in would expect pieces that were already delivered and write false `cycle_count` variances.
- docs/plans/00-coordination.md:407-410 (§4 item 5) only settled the reason code (`transfer_out`/`transfer_in`), not which lots move.
- docs/plans/warehouse.md:51 step (d) ("for every lot on the sheet") and :161 are stale. They date from when billing.invoices.issue did the stock half of packing.

5) Why nothing caught it.
- The demo seed models the correct semantics: confirmed sheets carry no transfer rows (seed-demo/warehouse.ts:380-400), and van stock arrives as a `van_load` pair with ref_type 'trip' (:403-436). So the 175 confirmed sheets in dos_qa have 0 `load_sheet` ledger rows, and the first real confirm is the one that failed.
- warehouse.spec.ts opens lotEarly with 240 and lotLate with 5 000, so both have surplus. Its assertions encode the double deduction (warehouse.spec.ts:1024-1030: 3 transfer_out, 3 transfer_in, lotLate 18 on the van).
- The 'lakh of goods' test (1064-1117) also double-deducts 4 800 pieces of lotB and asserts nothing about stock.
- delivery.spec.ts:643-667 confirms a van-stock-only sheet, so it never exercises packed lots.

Checked in dos_qa (SELECT only):
- Sheet 374f2089-b8fd-720e-907c-8380307948ab: draft, approved, EWB 381012345678, `van_stock []`, orders SO-0869/0871/0875/0876/0878 all `packed`, from Godown 01a0947d… to "Vehicle MH-05-AB-1234" 3bbe6b52….
- Its orders have 27 pack/sale rows over 23 distinct lots. 17 lots have godown on_hand below the packed pieces (the refusal); 6 have surplus.
- Two more approved draft sheets exist:
  - 1720dd92-c311-7860-bae2-8c80ba18ee14: 11 lots, 7 short, so it would also be refused.
  - 1e5181b6-843a-7855-a4d5-cb6451723518: 3 lots, 0 short. The current code would confirm it and silently double-deduct.
- 0 stock_ledger rows have ref_type 'load_sheet'.
- Vehicle ledger rows are only van_load/trip, sale/invoice and sale_return_saleable/credit_note.

No second contributing cause in code. The app sends `countedVanStock: []` (frontend/warehouse-app/app/load/[id].tsx:81), which is correct for this sheet. The whole defect is server-side, so it is the same on web, Android and iOS.

changes.what:
In confirm(), keep `const lots = await loadSheetLots(tx, counted)` (line 371). It still feeds the empty-sheet guard (372) and issueChallan (404-412), so the Rule 55 challan keeps one line per lot on the vehicle, packed cartons included, and the challan lines do not change.

Replace the `this.inventory.post(tx, lots.flatMap(...))` block (379-401) so it posts only the counted van stock:
- Build `const vanByLot = new Map<string, number>()` by summing `input.countedVanStock` per lotId, keeping insertion order.
- Post `[...vanByLot].flatMap(([lotId, qtyPcs]) => [...])` with the same two entry shapes as today: `transfer_out`, `-qtyPcs` at `sheet.fromLocationId`, key `load:${sheet.id}:${lotId}:out`; and `transfer_in`, `+qtyPcs` at `sheet.toLocationId`, key `load:${sheet.id}:${lotId}:in`. Both keep `refType 'load_sheet'` and `refId sheet.id`.

Why this shape:
- The per-lot sum is required. The contract does not refuse a repeated lotId (warehouse.ts:710; LoadSheetVanStockInput has `qtyPcs` positive but no uniqueness check), and the ledger keys are per lot. Without the sum, a second entry for the same lot is dropped as an idempotent no-op (`onConflictDoNothing`, inventory.service.ts:209).
- Unknown or other-tenant lots cannot reach the post: `valueVanStock(tx, input.countedVanStock)` (called before, 364; body 722-738) already throws NOT_FOUND.
- An empty list is already a no-op (inventory.service.ts:176), so no branch is needed.
- Do NOT use `lots.filter(l => l.source === 'van')`. loadSheetLots files a lot that is both packed and van stock under source 'order' with the summed quantity (warehouse.mappers.ts:476-482), so that filter would drop its van quantity.

Rewrite the class comment (114-123) and the confirm comment (316-328): the packed orders' pieces left the godown as `sale` at pack (PackingService), and only the counted van stock transfers godown → vehicle. The same keys still make a retried confirm a no-op.

Comment-only edit on ConfirmLoadSheetInput's JSDoc (697-705): 'a `transfer_out` + `transfer_in` pair per lot' becomes 'a `transfer_out` + `transfer_in` pair per counted van-stock lot (the packed orders' pieces already left as `sale` at pack)'. No Zod, route or summary change. The route summary at 937-938 ('count, move godown → vehicle, issue the challan, dispatch') is still true for van stock and stays, so `pnpm docs:readme:check` is unaffected.

Comment-only edit on the `loadSheets` JSDoc (180-182): 'Confirming the sheet posts the `transfer_out`/`transfer_in` pair godown → vehicle' becomes 'Confirming the sheet moves the counted van stock godown → vehicle as a `transfer_out`/`transfer_in` pair (packed orders' pieces already left as `sale` at pack)…'. Drizzle emits no SQL for comments, so there is no migration and no `db:generate`. This is the third place that describes the defect; the original plan missed it.

Test 1, 'confirms: stock moves godown to vehicle once, DC-0001 is issued and the orders dispatch' (989-1033): rename it with the DOS-039 prefix and correct the stock assertions.
- Before the call, read the godown on_hand of lotEarly, lotLate and lotB with `balanceOf`. Record them; do not hard-code them.
- After the call, assert: `ledgerFor(sheetId)` has exactly 2 rows, both lotB (transfer_out −12 at `godown`, transfer_in +12 at `van`), summing to 0; lotEarly and lotLate godown on_hand unchanged; lotB godown down exactly 12; `balanceOf(lotEarly, van)` and `balanceOf(lotLate, van)` both 0; `balanceOf(lotB, van)` 12.
- This replaces lines 1024-1027 (3/3 per lot) and 1030 (lotLate 18 on the van).
- Keep unchanged: every order, challan and outbox assertion, including `challan.lines toHaveLength(3)`, `DC-0001`, dispatched and the events.
- Test 1035 (retry replay) needs no change.

Test 2: add a new last `it` in the describe, after 'answers 401 with no token and hides another tenant' (1418-1425). It must stay LAST. If it failed mid-way it would leave 12 available pieces on an earlier-expiry variantB lot, and FEFO in any later test would reserve them. See tests for its body.

plans.contractChange: none. ConfirmLoadSheetInput/Output wire shapes, the route and its summary are unchanged. Only the JSDoc on ConfirmLoadSheetInput in backend/libs/contracts/src/warehouse.ts is corrected. `countedVanStock` already means 'what really goes on the van' (warehouse.ts:709), which is exactly what the fixed confirm moves.
plans.permissionsChange: none
plans.migration: none. No table, trigger, constraint or policy changes. The schema file edit is a JSDoc comment only, and Drizzle generates nothing for it. `stock_balances_on_hand_nonneg` stays as it is and still refuses van stock the godown does not have.

tests.name: DOS-039 confirms: only the counted van stock moves godown → vehicle, the packed lots stay where pack left them, DC-0001 is issued and the orders dispatch
DOS-039 sends out a sheet whose packed lot has nothing left in the godown instead of refusing 'insufficient stock'

plans.verify:
Both specs fail before the fix. Run `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/warehouse` before and after.

Test 1 before the fix:
- 6 ledger rows for the sheet (3 transfer_out).
- lotEarly godown 6 lower than recorded.
- lotEarly on the van 6, lotLate on the van 18.

Test 2 setup (all feasibility checked in code):
- asOwner: `inventory.findOrCreateLot(tx, { variantId: variantB, batchNo: `SOLDOUT-${run}`, mrpPaise: 2000, expiryDate: '2027-06-30' })`, then post `opening +12` at `godown` (key `open-${run}-soldout`).
- Why FEFO takes it: the spec creates no other variantB lot besides lotB (2029-06-30, :401-405); sellable_stock has no expiry filter (0003_force_rls_ledgers_views.sql:170-174); reserve orders by `expiry_date asc` (inventory.service.ts:343-345).
- `const id = await placeOrder([{ variantId: variantB, cases: 1 }], 'dos039')` (case override 12, :315).
- `packOrder(id, 'dos039', packer, 1)` gives 200. The pack takes the pending reservation (packing.service.ts:254-267) and posts sale −12, so `balanceOf(soldOut, godown).on_hand === 0`.
- POST /warehouse/load-sheets as packer with `{ idempotencyKey: `sheet-dos039-${run}`, id: sheet2, toLocationId: van, orderIds: [id] }` gives 200 with expectedPackages 1.
- POST …/confirm as manager (self-approving, :350-356) with `{ idempotencyKey: `confirm-dos039-${run}`, countedPackages: 1, challanId: uuidv7() }`.

Test 2 before the fix: 400, message matching /would go below zero/.

Test 2 after the fix:
- 200, status confirmed, `dispatched` equal to [id].
- `ledgerFor(sheet2)` empty.
- The sold-out lot is 0 at `godown` and 0 at `van`.
- `challan.lines` has a line with lotId = soldOut and qtyPcs 12.
- `orderState(id)` is 'dispatched'.

Also run `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/delivery`. delivery.spec.ts:643-667 confirms a van-stock-only sheet and must still show lotB 48 on the vehicle.

Running product (dos_qa; warehouse-service :3004; warehouse app :5176; dinesh.patil / Dos@1234; manager per QA/ENV.md §7):

1. Build and restart. Run `pnpm --filter @dos/core build`, then restart every service that composes WarehouseModule: owner :3001, manager :3002, warehouse :3004, delivery :3005 (core/src/service/definitions.ts:70,125,234,280), and retailer :3006, whose DeliveryModule imports WarehouseModule (delivery.module.ts:51; definitions.ts:340).

2. Take the "before" snapshot with this SQL:
```sql
select b.location_id, b.lot_id, b.on_hand from stock_balances b
 where b.location_id in ('01a0947d-7a96-723f-952d-338dd284a1b4','3bbe6b52-7dd7-7540-aad6-94ff815e8d8b')
   and (b.location_id = '3bbe6b52-7dd7-7540-aad6-94ff815e8d8b' or b.lot_id in (

```
Expected: 23 + 3 godown lots (lot 56f53711… = 0) plus the vehicle's 6 existing van_load lots.

3. Reproduce before the fix. This is safe on 374f2089: the refusal rolls back and leaves no idempotency row. Warehouse app → Home → LOAD SHEETS → 'MH-05-AB-1234 · 12 Sep · 5 orders · 38 cartons · draft' → count 35 → variance note → 'Send the vehicle out' → confirm. Result: 400 'insufficient stock: lot 56f53711… would go below zero (delta -240)', and the sheet stays draft.
   DO NOT confirm 1e5181b6 before the fix. All 3 of its lots have surplus, so the old code would double-deduct silently, and the append-only ledger cannot be undone.

4. After the fix, same steps on 374f2089: a success toast, the sheet shows confirmed with a DC-… challan, and the 5 orders are `dispatched`.
   TRIP-NEXT (72649337…) is already `active` in dos_qa because DOS-043 departed it. Confirm does not read the trip state, and the orders are still `packed`, so dispatch is legal.

5. DB checks after the fix:
   - `select status, challan_no from load_sheets where id='374f2089-b8fd-720e-907c-8380307948ab'` → confirmed, DC-….

It is approved, has 11 lots, and 7 of them would have been refused. Expect the same result as step 4. The API equivalent is POST :3004/warehouse/load-sheets/{id}/confirm with {idempotencyKey, countedPackages, varianceNote?, countedVanStock: [], challanId}.

8. Positive van-stock check. As the manager, create a sheet with vanStock [{lotId: <a godown lot with surplus>, qtyPcs: 12}] and no orders, then confirm it with countedVanStock carrying the same entry. Expect exactly one transfer_out (−12, godown) and one transfer_in (+12, vehicle) for that lot.

9. Confirms cannot be undone on dos_qa. Take a pg_dump snapshot of dos_qa before step 4, or reseed per QA/ENV.md.
plans.risk:
Low. The change is one loop inside one transaction, and it removes a movement the rest of the design never expected.

Unchanged:
- Challan lines, load value, the EWB gate, package count and variance, the approval gate (including the DB trigger from 0013), dispatch, outbox events and document render.
- Ledger key shape (`load:<sheetId>:<lotId>:out|in`), so a replay of an already-confirmed sheet still returns the stored response.

The only behaviour change: a sheet of packed orders with no counted van stock writes no stock_ledger rows at confirm. Settlement then expects only real van stock plus doorstep returns on the vehicle, which matches settlement.service.ts:376-404 and docs/plans/delivery.md:17/84.

Existing data:
- dos_qa needs no correction: 0 `load_sheet` ledger rows; vehicles hold only van_load, van sale and return rows.
- Spec databases where the old code succeeded against surplus lots keep their doubled rows. The ledger is append-only, so there is no backfill.
- Unverified: the dev `dos` database may also carry doubled rows. `pnpm smoke` confirms the newest draft sheet on every run; the op is not gated by --destructive (backend/tools/smoke-endpoints.mts:126-147, 716-724, 1640-1651). I did not query `dos`.

Adjacent, not changed: the warehouse app dialog copy 'Stock moves to the vehicle and challan paper is issued' (frontend/warehouse-app/src/strings.ts:323) stays physically true.
plans.reviewNotes:
What I changed from the submitted plan:
1. Root cause: added the evidence that this is not a new product decision. docs/plans/delivery.md:17, :31 and :84, trips.service.ts:843-858 (dispatchIfPacked moves no stock) and deliveries.service.ts:178-180 already define "pack sells, load-out moves only free van stock". docs/plans/00-coordination.md §4 item 5 only picked the reason code. The warehouse brief (warehouse.md:51(d), :161) is the stale one. Also recorded that the demo seed models the correct semantics (seed-demo/warehouse.ts:380-436), which is why 175 confirmed sheets have no ledger rows.
2. Changes: added the third comment that describes the defect, backend/libs/database/src/schema/warehouse.ts:180-182 (comment only, no migration). Added why the Map is safe: valueVanStock (load-sheets.service.ts:722-738) already rejects unknown lots, `qtyPcs` is positive in LoadSheetVanStockInput (contracts warehouse.ts:644-647), and duplicates are not refused by the contract (so the per-lot sum stays necessary).
3. Tests: checked test 2 can actually run.
   - sellable_stock has no expiry filter.
   - FEFO orders by expiry.
   - No other variantB lot exists in the spec.
   - Pack without a wave uses pending reservations.
   - The refusal is the mapped 400 from inventory.service.ts:740-745.
   - A refused confirm leaves no idempotency row (idempotency.ts runs inside the rolled-back tx).
   Made explicit that test 2 must stay the last `it`, and that test 1 reads balances before the call instead of hard-coding 234/4982.
4. Verify:
   - Named the full restart set: owner, manager, warehouse, delivery and retailer all compose WarehouseModule, directly or through DeliveryModule. The original said 'manager and owner if they mount it'.
   - dos_qa now has THREE approved draft sheets, not one. 1e5181b6 has 3 lots, all with surplus, so the current code would silently double-deduct. It must NOT be confirmed before the fix, and after the fix it is the running-product proof of the surplus half (new step 6).
   - 1720dd92 (7 of 11 lots short) is the fresh sheet for the Android repeat.
   - Added the vehicle's 6 existing van_load balances to the snapshot.
   - Noted TRIP-NEXT is already `active` (DOS-043), which does not block confirm.
5. dependsOn: the original said DOS-041 'is not in this batch's approved list'. That is wrong: DOS-041 is in the batch. There is no code dependency; it overlaps on the same raw 'insufficient stock … would go below zero' symptom, in different code (picks/pack), and in the same spec file. DOS-040 and DOS-042 will most likely append tests to warehouse.spec.ts too, so expect textual merge conflicts at the end of the describe. DOS-043 needs this fix to be verifiable, since its gate refuses depart while a sheet is draft. DOS-025 is only in the verification path (manager finds the draft). DOS-058 is a conceptual overlap on what the vehicle balance holds at settlement, with no shared lines.

Charter point for the approval gate: test 1 changes existing expected values (1024-1030). QA/CHARTER.md:70 forbids 'modifying expected values because the implementation is wrong'. Here the old values encode the defect: they contradict PackingService's documented invariant (packing.service.ts:65) and the delivery brief. The replacement assertions are stricter (godown balances of packed lots pinned, vehicle limited to lotB). The approval gate should sign this off explicitly, not let it pass silently.

Confirmed by reading or SELECT:
- Every cited line (load-sheets.service.ts:329/371/372/379-401/404; packing.service.ts:96; inventory.service.ts:176/209/343-345/446; warehouse.mappers.ts:344/466; schema inventory.ts:172; vansales.service.ts:84/99; settlement.service.ts:376-404).
- The 23/17/6 lot split for 374f2089.
- 0 `load_sheet` ledger rows; vehicle rows only van_load/sale/return.
- 3 approved draft sheets.
- ref_id is text, so the plan's `::text` casts are harmless.

Could not confirm:
- Whether dev `dos` already holds doubled rows from `pnpm smoke`. Not queried; only dos_qa was allowed.
- The finding's on-screen '25 lots' versus 23 distinct lots in the ledger (27 pack rows). Not reconciled; it does not affect the fix.
- I did not run any spec, so the before-fix failures are reasoned from code, not observed.

Residual doubts, all out of scope:
- (a) Whether a Rule 55 challan should list goods already covered by a tax invoice. Unchanged here.
- (b) Failed-stop cartons are never on the vehicle balance, so settlement neither counts nor restocks them; the order returns to `packed` and leaves again via trips.depart's dispatchIfPacked, while `onALiveSheet` (load-sheets.service.ts:740-752) keeps it off a second sheet. Consistent with the delivery brief, but untested end to end.
- (c) The warehouse app always sends `countedVanStock: []`, so drafted van stock is dropped at the gate.
- (d) docs/plans/warehouse.md:16/51/161/194 and the docs/22:117 diagram ('stock: warehouse → vehicle') still describe moving every lot. docs/22 is founder-owned (render and republish flow), so the main session decides the clarification ('van stock: warehouse → vehicle; packed orders left as sale at pack'), which restates docs/plans/delivery.md rather than making a new decision.

plans.title: A salesperson only reaches orders credited to them: another rep's order answers 404 on get, cancel, setLines, submit and device upload, and orders.list is limited to the rep's own orders
plans.rootCause:
Confirmed by re-reading every cited line. Nothing in the order aggregate checks ownership for the salesperson role. The only row-level check is for the retailer role.

1. cancel: backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts:371-382. It runs `requireRole(ORDER_ROLES)` (ORDER_ROLES = STAFF + retailer, :100; STAFF includes salesperson, warehouse and delivery, platform/authz.ts:6-14), then `lockOrder` (:537-541, a plain `where id = … for update`), then `assertRetailerOwns(order, ['draft','submitted'])` (:591-598). That check returns at :593 for every role except `retailer`. `cancelInTx` (:385-411) then runs `transition(state,'cancel')`, which is legal from `confirmed`. It releases every reservation (:397), expires pending approvals (:398-401) and records the caller as actor (:408).
2. setLines (:153-168) and submit (:232-244) have the same gap. In setLines the draft-state 409 (:160-163) is thrown before any ownership check, so it reveals another rep's order state.
3. Reads: `get` (:518-526) selects only by id. `list` → `listOrders` (orders.internals.ts:312-341) treats `salespersonId` as a filter the caller picks (:324), not a scope.
4. The offline path has the same hole. `applyOrderSync` (orders.sync.ts:54-71) rewrites the header of any existing draft, and `applyLineSync` (:102-137) re-lines any draft. Both use `findOrder` (:543-546) with no ownership check, so setLines is reachable through /sync/upload.
5. RLS cannot catch this, by design. backend/libs/database/src/schema/orders.ts:117-118 (`tenantOrOwnRetailerPolicy('sales_orders_read')` + `staffWritePolicy('sales_orders_write')`) gives every staff role tenant-wide read and write, because billing, warehouse, delivery, reporting and incentives depend on it. permissions.ts:518-525 (ANY_MEMBER) is correct per procedure: a rep needs these calls for its own orders (docs/23 line 329, S6: "`orders.list` salespersonId ✓, `orders.cancel` ✓ (up to confirmed)").
6. The product already defines a rep's orders as `salesperson_id = me`: the device pull (orders.module.ts:37-46), docs/23 line 362 ("own orders (90 d)"), and `createDraft` always stamps `salesperson_id = actor` for a rep (orders.internals.ts:105). The online endpoints never applied that rule.
7. The frontend is not a contributing cause. The sales app never shows another rep's order. Every route into `/orders/[id]` comes from pulled rows (shops/[id].tsx:338, orders/index.tsx:140), a just-confirmed AI draft (me/drafts.tsx:235) or the rep's own sync errors (orders/attention.tsx:107). No sales-app screen calls `orders.list`. The warehouse and delivery apps never call `orders.cancel/submit/setLines`.

DB facts re-checked in dos_qa:
- SO-0870 (6d53cb37-98d9-7675-bdce-c1f3ea4f1adc) has source salesperson and created_by = salesperson_id = amit.pawar. Its transitions (column `occurred_at`) are submit 10:00 and confirm 11:00 by amit.pawar, then cancel 17:49:26.667 by rahul.deshmukh, reason 'QA probe: rep cancelling another reps confirmed order'.

plans.title: payments.initiate builds its own UPI intent: the amount the shop chose, its PAY reference (in tr and tn), one upi://pay? prefix; the phone says so when no UPI app opens
plans.rootCause:
One cause produces the wrong amount, the wrong reference, the doubled prefix and the null payeeVpa. `initiatePayment` copies the invoice's stored full-URI snapshot and treats it as the intent's own query string. I re-traced every step below against the code and dos_qa.

1. **No intent is built for the payment.** `ReceivablesService.initiatePayment` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/receivables/receivables.service.ts:1192) computes `amountPaise` (:1224) and `paymentRef` (:1231). It then sorts the chosen bills newest first (:1229) and copies the newest bill's `upiQrPayload` into the reply (:1230, :1244).
   - That column is the bill's snapshot, written once at issue by `upiIntent({ amountPaise: totalPaise, reference: invoiceNo })` (billing/invoices.service.ts:1517-1522, stored at :1563). The seed writes the same shape (libs/database/src/seed-demo/sales.ts:2900).
   - So `am` is the newest chosen bill's ORIGINAL total and `tr` is its invoice number.
   - Checked in dos_qa: INV/0753 stores `am=5472.00&tr=INV-0753`. INV/0433 stores `am=10119.00&tr=INV-0433` (total 1011900; the API shows 456100 open).
   - The outbox disagrees with what the shop is asked to pay. The PaymentIntentCreated rows say 3584300 / PAY-9520ecba4571, 3584300 / PAY-13c1dede2871 and 456100 / PAY-000000000002. `retailer_outstanding_summary` for retailer 34191c43… is 3584300.

2. **The prefix is doubled.** `upiIntent()` already returns a full URI (billing/billing.internals.ts:330-345). Stored payloads that start with `upi://pay?` in dos_qa: Tarsun 840 of 856, Sai 440 of 456, Kalyan 173 of 189; the other 16 in each tenant are null. `initiatePayment` adds the prefix again (:1245), which gives `upi://pay?upi://pay?pa=…` (evidence api-01-payments-initiate.txt).

3. **`payeeVpa` is always null.** `upiField` (:1807-1814) splits on `&`, so the first key is `upi://pay?pa`, never `pa`. `pn` still parses, which is why payeeName shows "M/s. Tarsun Enterprise".

4. **The spec never saw this.** The receivables.spec.ts fixture (:171) stores `pa=tarsun@upi&pn=…&am=…`: no scheme, no `tr`, a shape billing never writes. The initiate test (:1270-1310) asserts only `payeeVpa === 'tarsun@upi'` (:1284), never am, tr or the URL.

5. **The doc comment's justification is stale (:1189-1190).** `sellerBranding()` (modules/tenancy/branding.ts:30) reads `upi_vpa` and `branding.display_name` for the retailer role through the one-statement escalation in `loadSettings` (:75-101).
   - dos_qa proves it for this exact shop: the retailer's own GET :3006/invoices/a924ae38… (QA/evidence/phase1/retailer/net-bill-0753/10-GET-…json) returned seller.upiVpa "tarsun@okhdfcbank" and displayName "Tarsun Enterprise". It also returned a signed logoUrl, even though Tarsun has `branding.logo_object_key` set.
   - `InvoicesService.upiQr` (invoices.service.ts:902-922) already rebuilds the intent from `loadSeller` for the shop's R3 sheet (retailer-app/app/dues.tsx:56-60). That is the neighbour to copy.

6. **The phone shows nothing when no UPI app opens.** pay.tsx:182-184 calls `void links.open(...)` and throws away the boolean.

plans.title: Enforce the console level (super / support / billing) on every admin.* mutation, put the level on the platform sign-in reply, keep the acting super alive through a lock, and hide what the level cannot use
plans.rootCause:
The level is stored but nothing above the database reads it. Nothing between the token and the handlers uses it. Every citation below was re-read.

1. The level exists and is seeded.
   - Enum `platform_admin_role` ('super','support','billing') at backend/libs/database/src/schema/platform-admin.ts:78. The comment at :72-77 gives the job split.
   - Column `platform_admins.role NOT NULL` at :122.
   - Seed: dos.support = 'support' (seed-demo/platform-admin.ts:76-78); dos.admin = 'super' (:168).
   - docs/18-build-log.md:2135-2136 names the jobs: super onboards, sets plans, suspends; support ASKS for access.

2. The token and the gate cannot tell levels apart.
   - `isPlatformAdmin()` (modules/auth/auth.service.ts:1046-1053) selects only `platformAdmins.id`.
   - `issuePlatformPair()` (:1097-1125) hard-codes `role: 'platform_admin'` in token and reply. The same holds for platformLogin :464, platformRefresh :501, platformMe :517.
   - `PlatformRoleSchema = z.enum(['platform_admin'])` (contracts/src/common.ts:60).
   - Every admin.* row is `PLATFORM` (contracts/src/permissions.ts:978-992).
   - `TenantGuard.admitConsole` checks only `isAllowed(permission, 'platform_admin')` (modules/tenancy/tenant.guard.ts:196-206).

3. The handler check tests "still active", never level.
   - `requireActiveAdmin()` (platform-admin/internals.ts:84-95) and `requireActiveAdminUnderSystem()` (tenants.service.ts:363-373) read `disabled_at` only.
   - They are the only check on the six mutations: tenants.create :167; suspend/reactivate via setStatus :303; subscriptions.upsert (subscriptions.service.ts:105); support.request (support.service.ts:53); support.revoke (:145); users.disable via assertActive (console.service.ts:128, :294-296).

4. Why support could lock out the super.
   - `disableUser` refuses only the actor's own id (console.service.ts:132-136).
   - It writes `users`/`auth_sessions` under withSystem (:129-158).
   - `dos_platform_admin_guard()` (migrations/0034_platform_admin_guarantees.sql:78-106) is the only level-aware DB rule, and it covers writes to `platform_admins` only.

5. A second hole the plan missed: its point (c) is false. "Self-refusal keeps a super alive" does not hold.
   - `requireActiveAdmin` never reads `users.status`.
   - TenantGuard verifies the access token with no session lookup (tenant.guard.ts:150-156).
   - `disableUser` sets `users.status='disabled'` and revokes sessions (console.service.ts:141-149) but leaves `platform_admins` alone. A locked console login therefore passes every handler check for up to one access-token lifetime (15 min).
   - Two supers A and B: A locks B → 200; B's still-valid token locks A → 200; now no super can sign in.
   - Two simultaneous disables also both pass, because neither transaction locks the actor's row.
   - With the level gate alone this stays reachable super-vs-super. The finding's own suggested fix asks for "a super may never disable the last active super".

6. The UI shows no level in two places.
   - Account screen: `t('word.platform_admin')` under "Level" (frontend/admin-app/app/settings.tsx:41).
   - Shell account label: `roleLabel: strings['word.platform_admin']` (frontend/admin-app/app/_layout.tsx:136).
   - `PlatformSession` is `{user, role}` (frontend/libs/api-client/src/session.ts:35-38).
   - No action button checks anything; the nav `can` (_layout.tsx:91-95) uses role only.

Data re-confirmed in dos_qa. `platform_audit` rows by dos.support:
- subscription.updated on Sai 82f5c562… at 19:26:19
- tenant.onboarded on 0ccdd8a0… at 19:26:19
- tenant.suspended at 19:30:27
- user.disabled on qa.probe.owner at 19:30:27
- user.disabled on dos.admin at 19:52:23

Both logins are active again (restored by SQL).

Assessment of the finding's suggested fix:
- (a) Keep the level OUT of the token. Privilege is re-read per call (auth.service.ts:1064-1067). Adding a claim would disturb TenantGuard and the PLATFORM_ROLES disjointness tests (permissions.test.ts:1466-1484).
- (b) describePermissionMatrix is the wrong harness. It is gate-only, uses synthetic tokens with no rows (testing/permission-matrix.ts:15-16, 31-35), and classifies by guard error shape (:164-180). The level × procedure matrix belongs in a contracts unit test plus the DB-backed platform-admin.spec.ts.
- (c) CORRECTED. The last-super guarantee needs the actor re-read under a row lock inside the disable transaction (point 5). No count query is needed: once the acting super is provably still active at commit, the set of active supers can never become empty through the API.

Ordering requirement: `runIdempotent` (platform/idempotency.ts:48-70) returns the stored reply without running fn. The level gate must therefore run BEFORE `platformIdempotent` in setStatus, upsert, request and revoke; otherwise a lower level replaying a super's key with an identical body gets the stored 200.

plans.contractChange:
backend/libs/contracts changes in three places.

1. **common.ts** adds `PlatformAdminLevelSchema` ('super' | 'support' | 'billing'), mirroring the database enum.
2. **permissions.ts** adds:
   - `AdminProcedurePath` (`Extract<ProcedurePath, 'admin.${string}'>`);
   - `ADMIN_LEVELS`, a console-only narrowing table keyed by exactly the 15 `admin.*` paths;
   - `levelAllows()`.

   `PERMISSIONS`, `PLATFORM_ROLES`, `ROLE_GROUPS` and `isAllowed` do not change.
3. **auth.ts**: `PlatformTokenPairOutput` and `PlatformMeOutput` each gain an additive output field, `level`.

No input schema changes.

**Why this cannot be avoided.** The level is the fact the server enforces and the admin app hides buttons by. Today it lives only in `platform_admins.role`, and neither the token role nor `AdminUserSchema.platformRole` carries it. Declaring it once in contracts keeps the app from carrying a second permission list (CLAUDE.md, "Permissions on the device").

**Consumers of the reply.**
- The frontend api-client (session store) and its tests are updated in this plan.
- The smoke tool and `QA/tools/tok.sh` read the JSON loosely and are unaffected.
plans.permissionsChange:
**PERMISSIONS is unchanged.**
- Every `admin.*` row stays `ROLE_GROUPS.PLATFORM`.
- The token role stays `platform_admin`.
- TenantGuard, PlatformTokenGuard and the `describePermissionMatrix` semantics are untouched.

**New `ADMIN_LEVELS` in permissions.ts narrows access inside the platform role:**
- **super:** all 15 procedures.
- **support:** the 8 reads (tenants.list/get, subscriptions.list/get, support.list, users.list, metrics.overview, audit.list) plus support.request and support.revoke.
- **billing:** the 8 reads plus subscriptions.upsert.

**Where it is enforced.** In the platform-admin module, by `requireAdminLevel()`:
- It runs before `platformIdempotent` in the four `withPlatform` mutations.
- In `tenants.create` it runs as a pre-check before password hashing, and again inside the withSystem transaction.
- In `users.disable` it runs as a pre-check, and then the actor is re-read under a row lock.

The admin app reads the same table through `useCan()`.

**Documentation gap.** The README/OpenAPI `x-roles` still render only `platform_admin`; see reviewNotes.

plans.risk:
1. **Contract output change on the three auth platform procedures.** A new required `level` field. Build @dos/contracts before the frontend typecheck, and run `pnpm docs:readme`.
2. **Gate moved before `platformIdempotent`.** On four mutations, a replay by a demoted or disabled admin is now refused instead of getting the stored reply. This is intended, but it is a behaviour change.
3. **Row lock in `disableUser`.** It takes `FOR UPDATE` on at most two `users` rows, in id order.
   - Two disables cannot deadlock.
   - Login and refresh update a single users row, so there is no lock cycle.
   - A disable waits for a concurrent sign-in write on the same identity: milliseconds.
4. **Extra read in `tenants.create`.** The pre-check adds one indexed read on a rare call.
5. **Sessions saved before the change.** They restore with `level: null`, so the admin app hides level-gated buttons until the boot refresh fills it in. If that refresh fails for a network reason, the buttons stay hidden until the next successful refresh. The server remains the authority.
6. **The billing mapping is a judgement call.** Reads plus subscriptions.upsert, taken from the schema comment (platform-admin.ts:72-77).
   - No billing login exists in seed or dos_qa, so no live user is affected.
   - The subscription status 'suspended' is described as paired with `tenants.status`, yet billing may not suspend. Confirm with the founder.
7. **No ordering constraint left in the spec.** All DOS-106 cases act on dedicated fixtures with a non-`p${run}.` prefix. Reusing the spec's own super or `p${run}.` usernames would break the existing identity case and cascade before the fix.
plans.reviewNotes:
**WHAT I CHANGED in the plan, and why:**

1. **Corrected point (c), the "no last-super rule needed" argument; it is false.**
   - `requireActiveAdmin` (internals.ts:84-95) never reads `users.status`.
   - TenantGuard does no session lookup (tenant.guard.ts:150-156).
   - `disableUser` leaves `platform_admins` untouched (console.service.ts:141-149).
   - So super B, locked by super A, keeps a working token for up to 15 min and can lock A back. Two simultaneous disables also both pass.
   - Added: in `disableUser`, lock the actor and target `users` rows in id order `FOR UPDATE` and re-check that the actor is active, plus a spec case that fails before the fix (B's token locks A → 200 today).
   - No count query: once the acting super is provably active at commit, the set of active supers cannot empty through the API.
2. **`tenants.create`: early level pre-check** (withPlatform + requireAdminLevel) before validatePassword/argon2. The existing pattern is console.service.ts assertActive before withSystem. A refused caller gets 403, not 400 on a weak password, and burns no hash. The in-transaction under-system check is kept and made level-aware.
3. **Spec fixtures redesigned.**
   - The plan's billing fixture and any new console usernames under `p${run}.` would break the existing 'shows one identity…' case, which asserts `platformOnly + q: p${run}.` returns exactly two ids.
   - The plan's 'lock the spec's own super, place it LAST' also relies on order. Replaced with dedicated fixtures (`l${run}.bill`, `l${run}.sup2`, `l${run}.sup3`, throwaway tenant `lvl-${run}` and victim user; phones `+918${run}N`), so pre-fix runs only mutate throwaway rows.
   - The support session uses `platformBearer`; handlers do not read the session. A real sign-in is used only for the level-in-reply case.
4. **Added an explicit idempotency-replay test and verify step** (identical body, a super's key → 403). The plan named the ordering risk but had no test that fails without it.
5. **session.ts:** changing only `isPlatformSession` would not map a missing level to null. `BaseSessionStore` passes the parsed object through (session.ts:106-120, 200). The parse lambda must build `{user, role, level}`. The frontend test now also covers the pre-change snapshot.
6. **Added frontend/admin-app/app/_layout.tsx:136**, the shell `roleLabel`, which is the other place both accounts read 'Distribution OS staff'. settings.tsx now uses the existing `useWord()` helper instead of a template-literal key.
7. **Verify:** body `id` must equal the path id (DOS-112, QA/ENV.md), or suspend 500s and disable 404s. The weak-password onboarding probe proves gate-first. Billing and super-vs-super are marked spec-only, since dos_qa has no such logins.
8. **Imports:** after the change `requireActiveAdmin` is unused in tenants.service.ts, subscriptions.service.ts and support.service.ts; remove those imports or lint fails. `AdminProcedurePath` is built on the existing `ProcedurePath` (permissions.ts:320).

**CONFIRMED by reading:**
- All cited lines of the original root cause.
- `runIdempotent` returns the stored reply without running fn.
- `isGateRefusal` classifies handler ORPCErrors as through-the-gate, so the permission-matrix suite needs no change.
- The admin-service spec's platform-token case still gets 'console account' from `requireActiveAdmin` on metrics.
- tenancy/support.spec.ts uses a support-level admin only for grants inserted directly or via tenancy, not admin.* mutations, so it is unaffected.
- The smoke tool signs in only as dos.admin.
- The dos_qa audit rows by dos.support, including user.disabled on dos.admin at 19:52:23. dos.admin and qa.probe.owner are active again.

**COULD NOT CONFIRM:**
- That DOS-073 and DOS-043 actually edit permissions.ts or permissions.test.ts; I cannot see their plans. The dependency is file overlap only, not logic.
- The live UI walk on iOS.
- The founder's intent for billing: whether it may also ask for support, or suspend, given the schema pairs subscription 'suspended' with `tenants.status`. The default here is no to both, and it needs sign-off before being written into docs/22 §8.

**RESIDUAL DOUBTS** (deliberately not widened into this fix):
- (i) A locked or disabled console login's stale token can still run suspend, upsert, request and revoke for up to 15 min. Only users.disable gets the in-transaction re-check. Also tenants.list/get, subscriptions.list/get and support.list call no admin check at all. Pre-existing and level-independent; a candidate follow-up.
- (ii) The generated README/OpenAPI `x-roles` still say `platform_admin` for every admin row, so API readers cannot see the level split. A doc-renderer follow-up.
- (iii) `auth.supportPass` stays level-blind. An admin demoted by SQL from support to billing could still mint a pass on an earlier-approved grant of their own.
- (iv) No database-level level guarantee for subscriptions and tenants writes (application gate only), unlike `platform_admins`.
- (v) The finding says '16 console procedures'; the contract has 15 `admin.*` rows (permissions.test.ts pins 15), and the 16th is presumably `auth.supportPass`.

**Must pass before merge:**
- `pnpm --filter @dos/contracts test`
- `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/platform-admin src/modules/tenancy src/modules/auth`
- `pnpm --filter @dos/admin-service test`
- `pnpm --filter @dos/auth-service test`
- `pnpm docs:readme:check`
- frontend `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm smoke` → 0 BROKEN

plans.title: Confirm order must never decide an order's pending approvals: refuse with 409 approval_required and send each decision through approvals.decide
plans.rootCause:
One cause explains both halves of DOS-020: the silent approvals and the walk through a credit stop. I re-traced the path: screen, then client, then contract, then controller, then service, then SQL.

1. **The blanket UPDATE in `confirmInTx`.** backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts:327-330 sets every pending approval on the order to `approved`, with `decidedBy` = the caller.
   - It checks no kind, and `decisionNote` stays NULL.
   - It writes no transition row for the decisions.
   - The database does not stop it. `approvals` has no trigger, and its update policy (migrations/0012_platform_gaps_expand.sql:258-266) allows owner, manager and system in WITH CHECK. The defect is purely in the service.

2. **Only the direct Confirm procedure reaches that UPDATE with approvals still pending.** `confirmInTx` has three callers:
   - `submitInTx` calls it only when `flags.length === 0` (orders.service.ts:281-286), before any approval row is inserted (:288-299).
   - `ApprovalsService.decide` calls it only after `stillPending()` is false (approvals.service.ts:108-111).
   - `OrdersService.confirm` (orders.service.ts:305-315) is behind `orders.confirm` (orders.controller.ts:39-41; contracts/src/orders.ts:314-320). It calls it with approvals still pending.
   - Paths that do not reach it:
     - ai `drafts.confirm` (ai/drafts.service.ts:167) and the delivery van sale (delivery/vansales.service.ts:87-93) reach it only through `submitInTx`.
     - Offline sync never moves an order past `draft` (orders.sync.ts:44-58).
     - No seed, worker or tool calls `OrdersService.confirm` (git grep).

3. **Every held order carries a pending approval.** The order machine allows `submitted` to go only to `confirm` or `cancel` (backend/libs/domain/src/state-machines/order.ts:39). In dos_qa, 7 of 7 `submitted` orders have pending approvals:
   - Tarsun: SO-0879, SO-0882, SO-0885 (R-0001, strict).
   - Sai Distributors: SO-0449 (SD-0016, stop; `credit_limit` f5d2ce35 + `below_floor` df049848) and SO-0452.
   - Kalyan Agencies: SO-0178 (KA-0016, stop; `credit_limit` 3925e2ca + `below_floor` e31d0945) and SO-0180.
   - Four of the seven (SO-0178, SO-0180, SO-0449, SO-0452) carry `sales_orders.approval_flags = []` although approvals are pending; the seed writes the approval rows directly. So a guard must read the `approvals` rows, never `approval_flags`.
   - The 5 pending approvals with `order_id` NULL are all `bargain` on `bargain_request` entities. An order-scoped check therefore misses no credit gate.

4. **Why it walks through a credit stop.** Confirm never looks at credit.
   - The only credit gate is the `credit_limit` approval raised at submit. `approvalFlags` (orders.internals.ts:140-156) calls `checkCredit` (receivables/credit.ts:65-102), where `breached` is true for `strict` and `stop`.
   - credit.ts:57-60 and docs/plans/receivables.md:173 say the override for that gate is an approvals-queue decision.
   - Confirm approved the gate blindly, so R-0018 (stop) was released.

5. **DB evidence, re-queried read-only.**
   - SO-0867 is `confirmed`, `confirmed_at` 2026-09-12 13:52:31.117.
   - Approvals 59eeee35 (`credit_limit`) and 5d89bf84 (`below_floor`) are `approved`, `decided_by` a1cbd424 (vikas.kadam), `decision_note` NULL.
   - `decided_at` is 13:52:31.117 on both, the same instant as the confirm.

6. **Second contributing cause: the apps.**
   - The manager order panel never renders `order.approvals`, although `orders.get` returns them for every non-retailer caller (orders.service.ts:548-550, orders.mappers.ts:108-129).
   - Confirm is enabled for any `submitted` order: frontend/manager-app/app/orders/index.tsx:523-532, and hotkey 1 at :231-233.
   - The confirm dialog prints only `m2.confirmBody` (:585-587), with no credit and no decisions.
   - The owner app has the same button at frontend/owner-app/app/orders/index.tsx:331-340.

7. **Pre-fix lock-order inversion (plausible, not observed).** `decide` locks the approval row and then the order (approvals.service.ts:75-99). `confirm` locked the order and then UPDATEd the approval rows. Removing the UPDATE removes the inversion.

8. **The existing explicit override path.** `orders.approvals.decide` (approvals.service.ts:68-113) already records `decided_by` and `decision_note`, and confirms the order when the last approval is approved. The fix routes decisions there, so the contract does not change.

9. **No founder decision behind the behaviour.** The comment at orders.service.ts:304 cites "docs/22 2026-09-05". That row (docs/22:237) only narrows the accountant's scope.

changes.what:
In `confirmInTx` (:322-369):
- Delete the blanket `tx.update(approvals).set({ status: 'approved', decidedBy: ctx.actorId, ... })` at :327-330, and the `const ctx = currentTenant()` at :323 that only it used.
- Directly after `const to = transition(order.state, 'confirm')` (:325) add the guard. This placement keeps the illegal-state 409 and its message (orders.spec.ts:581-592).
- The guard is `const waiting = await tx.select({ id: approvals.id, kind: approvals.kind }).from(approvals).where(and(eq(approvals.orderId, order.id), eq(approvals.status, 'pending'))).orderBy(asc(approvals.id))`.
- If `waiting.length > 0`, `throw new ORPCError('CONFLICT', { message: `${order.orderNo ?? order.id} is waiting on ${waiting.length} decision(s) (${waiting.map((w) => w.kind.replaceAll('_', ' ')).join(', ')}); approve or reject each in the approvals queue — the last approval confirms the order`, data: { code: 'approval_required', approvals: waiting } })`.
- That is the same untyped error-data pattern as warehouse/load-sheets.service.ts:343-346 (`code: 'approval_required'`) and delivery/vansales.service.ts:89-93. Specs already assert it via `body.data?.code` (warehouse.spec.ts:933).
- Read the `approvals` rows, never `sales_orders.approval_flags`: seeded held orders carry flags `[]` with approvals pending.
- Keep the guard in `confirmInTx`, not only in `confirm()`, so no future caller can bring back a silent decision. The cost is one indexed read (`approvals_order_idx`) on an auto-confirming submit.
- Stock reservation, the state update, `recordTransition` and `emitOrderEvent` are unchanged.
- Rewrite the docstrings at :304 and :317-321. Confirm never decides an approval; approvals are decided only through `ApprovalsService.decide`; drop the misattributed docs/22 citation.
- A refused confirm rolls back its idempotency row with the transaction (platform/idempotency.ts:56-80 runs inside `withTenant`), so a retry after the decisions is not replayed as a stored 409.

**Imports.** Add `approvals` to the `@dos/db` import. Add `and, eq` to the `drizzle-orm` import (only `sql` today). In the local `Detail` type (:67) widen `approvals` to `{ id: string; kind: string; status: string; decidedBy: string | null; decisionNote: string | null }[]`.

**Fixtures (beforeAll, :93-253).**

The users row is required because `approvals.decided_by` and `requested_by` are FKs to users (database/src/schema/orders.ts:292-297).

**New test, placed directly before 'reserves what exists…' (:656).** Name it `DOS-020: confirm on a credit-stop shop's order refuses while approvals are pending and decides none of them`.
- Rep creates and submits 1 piece of variantA for retailerC. Expect `submitted`, flags ['credit_limit'].
- Insert a second pending approval as a fixture row: `{ id: uuidv7(), tenantId, kind: 'below_floor', orderId: id, entityType: 'order', entityId: id, requestedBy: repId, status: 'pending', payload: { flag: 'below_floor' } }`. - Then the explicit path: the manager decides each approval through POST `/approvals/{id}/decide` with a note. After the first, the order is still `submitted`. **Existing test 'reserves what exists and reports the shortage instead of refusing the order' (:656-697).** It confirms through a pending strict `credit_limit` approval and asserts at :690 that confirm approved it; that assertion is the DOS-020 behaviour.

From this panel the last approval now performs the confirm and reservation, and `useQuery` holds a cached value for 30 s (api-client react/index.tsx staleTime 30_000; cache.ts:196 invalidates by prefix). Without it the panel's reservation count (['warehouse','reservations',id]) keeps reading 0 after the release.

tests.name: DOS-020: confirm on a credit-stop shop's order refuses while approvals are pending and decides none of them
reserves what exists and reports the shortage instead of refusing the order (DOS-020: gate decided before confirm)

plans.verify:
Everything below runs against a copy of `dos_batch1_template` (QA/STATE.md: tests never against dos_qa again). Point `DATABASE_URL`, the eight services and the worker at that copy before starting. Before any pnpm command: `export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; eval "$(fnm env)"; fnm use 24`.

**A. Failing spec first**
1. With the spec change only, run `DATABASE_URL=<copy> pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/orders`.
2. The DOS-020 test fails: the manager's POST `/orders/{id}/confirm` answers 200, not 409.
3. Thanks to the `finally` cancel, the shortage test stays green. If it goes red, the cleanup is wrong.
4. After the server change, the whole orders spec passes.
5. Then run `pnpm --filter @dos/core build`, and restart manager-service :3002 and owner-service :3001.

**B. API (manager-service :3002)**
1. Sign in `sanjay.bhosale` / `Dos@1234` on auth :3000 (Sai Distributors, manager).
2. `GET /orders?q=SO-0449` gives the id.
3. `GET /orders/{id}` shows `approvals` df049848 `below_floor` and f5d2ce35 `credit_limit`, both `pending`.
4. `GET /receivables/credit-check?retailerId=<SD-0016 id>&orderTotalPaise=654200` shows `creditMode` stop and `breached` true. SO-0449's total_paise is 654200, verified.
5. `POST /orders/{id}/confirm {idempotencyKey}`:
   - Before the fix: 200, and both approvals flip to `approved` with `decision_note` NULL.
   - After the fix: 409, `data.code` = 'approval_required', `data.approvals` = the two ids and kinds, and a message naming "below floor, credit limit".

**C. DB after the refused confirm**
```sql
select kind, status, decided_by, decision_note
from approvals
where order_id = (select o.id from sales_orders o join tenants t on t.id = o.tenant_id
                  where t.slug = 'sai-distributors' and o.order_no = 'SO-0449');
```
- Both approvals are `pending` with NULL `decided_by`.
- `select state from sales_orders o join tenants t on t.id = o.tenant_id where t.slug = 'sai-distributors' and o.order_no = 'SO-0449'` returns `submitted`.
- `select count(*) from reservations r join sales_order_lines l on l.id = r.order_line_id where l.order_id = <id>` returns 0.
- `select event from order_state_transitions where order_id = <id>` returns only `submit`.

**D. Manager web app :5174**
1. Sign in `sanjay.bhosale`, open Orders, filter Submitted, open SO-0449. Check at 1280×800 and at 375 px; measure, do not eyeball.
2. After the fix:
   - The panel shows "Waiting on: Below floor price · Over credit limit", each with Approve and Reject.
   - "Confirm order" is disabled with the reason text "Waiting on Below floor price · Over credit limit. Approve or reject each one first; the last approval confirms the order."
   - Key 1 does nothing.
3. Before the fix, the button was enabled and the dialog said only "Stock is reserved… no undo".
4. Approve "Over credit limit". The dialog body shows "SO-0449 · Over credit limit · Credit is blocked for this shop". Type the note "QA: owner agreed once" and approve.
   - The order stays Submitted.
   - One decision is left.
5. Approve "Below floor price" with a note.
   - The order becomes Confirmed.
   - The Reservations count in the panel updates without a reload.
6. DB after step 5:
   - Both approvals are `approved`, `decided_by` = sanjay.bhosale's user id, `decision_note` = the typed notes.
   - Reservations exist.
   - The confirm transition's actor is the manager.
7. Sign in as the accountant `nilesh.wagh`: the Waiting-on list is visible with no buttons.

**E. Owner web app :5173**
1. Sign in `sunil.tarsun`, open Orders, then SO-0879 (R-0001 strict, pending `credit_limit` 01a09586).
2. Confirm is disabled with "Waiting on Over credit limit. Decide it on Approvals; …".
3. Approving it on Approvals confirms the order; that is existing behaviour.

**F. Android (Pixel 7, `emulator -avd Pixel_7_API_36 -memory 3072`)**
1. Repeat D1-D3 on the manager app (proxy8081.mjs 5174, per QA/ENV.md §5).
2. The disabled reason renders under the button (native/controls.tsx:108-115).
3. Take screenshots with `adb exec-out screencap`.

**G. iOS (booted iPhone 16 Pro, Expo Go)**
1. Run `QA/tools/ios-login.mjs 5174 ashok.kulkarni manager`, then open SO-0178 (Kalyan Agencies, stop, two pending).
2. Check the same panel, disabled reason and a refused key path.
3. Screenshot with `xcrun simctl io booted screenshot`.
4. Reset the simulator keychain between apps (ENV.md §8).
5. Never infer iOS from Android.

**H. Regressions**
- A sales-app order for an `indicate` shop inside its limits still auto-confirms at submit (transitions submit, confirm).
- A retailer-app order for its own `indicate` shop still auto-confirms under the system role.
- A van sale with no gates still bills.
- An ai draft confirm still submits.
- `pnpm smoke` still ends 0 BROKEN; `orders.confirm` answers 409, which smoke-endpoints.mts:2181-2183 classifies EXPECTED.
- `pnpm --filter @dos/manager-service test` and `pnpm --filter @dos/owner-service test` (permission matrix) stay green.
- `pnpm docs:readme --check` shows no diff.
plans.risk:
- **Visible behaviour change.** "Confirm order" in the manager and owner apps is disabled for every held order, because 7 of 7 `submitted` orders in dos_qa carry pending approvals. Releasing a held order now means deciding each approval; the last approval confirms it (existing `approvals.decide` behaviour). This is the "confirm is refused" outcome the finding's Expected line accepts, but the founder should know the one-press release is gone.
- **`orders.confirm` becomes practically unreachable** from product flows. It succeeds only for a `submitted` order with nothing pending (seeded or legacy rows), and its `shortages` output is only observable there. The decide path computes shortages and discards them, which is pre-existing.
- **Residual, not observed and not fixed (candidate new finding).** Credit can go stale between submit and decision. A shop that passes its credit terms after submit confirms without `checkCredit` being re-run when its last non-credit approval is decided (`ApprovalsService.decide` → `confirmInTx`). Re-gating inside decide changes approvals-queue semantics, which DOS-020 did not observe.
- **Founder questions left open.** `DecideApprovalInput.note` is optional (contracts/src/orders.ts:271), and `decide` is MANAGEMENT. So the finding's suggestion "a stop needs an explicit override WITH a note" is delivered as an explicit, named decision but not as a mandatory note. Whether a stop-shop `credit_limit` needs a note, or is owner-only, is a product and permission decision.
- **Still open, outside this batch.**
  - No audit rows for confirm or decisions (DOS-028, P2).
  - An approved limit request does not change the limit (DOS-006, P2).
  - The register's "Waiting on" column is still derived from `approval_flags`, which the seed leaves `[]` (DOS-027, P2).
- **Refusal surface.** Until DOS-029 lands, a stale-screen 409 on confirm or decide closes the dialog silently. The disabled button covers the normal case.
- **Merge conflicts.**
  - Both order screens are also touched by DOS-003 (line names), DOS-004 (approval cards) and DOS-029 (error surface).
  - orders.service.ts is touched by DOS-073.
  - approvals.service.ts may be touched by DOS-005.
plans.reviewNotes:
**What I verified by reading code and read-only SQL**
- Root cause at orders.service.ts:327-330: confirmed. The three `confirmInTx` callers are exactly as stated.
- Other entry points ruled out: ai drafts (drafts.service.ts:167) and van sale (vansales.service.ts:87-93) go only through `submitInTx`; sync stops at `draft` (orders.sync.ts:44-58); no seed, tool or worker calls confirm.
- No trigger on `approvals`. Its RLS update policy allows the manager (0012:258-266), so no DB-layer co-cause.
- DB evidence for SO-0867, SO-0449, SO-0178 and SO-0879 re-queried and matches. SO-0449 total 654200 matches the verify call. Sign-in roles checked in memberships.
- Error-data pattern and its spec assertions exist (warehouse.spec.ts:933).
- smoke classifies 409 as EXPECTED (smoke-endpoints.mts ~2181). The permission matrix only asserts gate refusals.
- `disabledReason` renders on web and native.
- The illegal-transition test keeps its message given the guard's placement.

**What I changed**
1. **Invalidations.** Added ['warehouse'], ['billing'], ['reporting'] to the manager app's `decideApproval`. The plan moves the release into the panel's decide buttons, but that mutation only invalidated approvals and orders. With the 30 s cache (react/index.tsx:31) the panel's reservation count would read 0 right after the order confirms.
2. **Credit line on the decision.** For a `credit_limit` decision from the panel, `what` now carries `creditLine()`. The path that now releases held orders must itself state the credit stop, which is the finding's step 3 complaint. No new state or strings.
3. **Button gate.** Decision buttons are gated on `can('orders.approvals.decide')`, not `mayDecide` (= `can('orders.confirm')`). The accountant sees the list read-only.
4. **Spec robustness.**
   - The DOS-020 test is placed before the shortage test, with `try/finally` cancel. Otherwise the pre-fix failing run also reserves stock and breaks the reserved = 100 arithmetic, muddying the failing-test evidence.
   - It also exercises the explicit decide path end to end with notes.
   - It asserts no `OrderConfirmed` outbox row.
   - Named the needed imports (`approvals`, `and`, `eq`) and the `Detail` type widening.
   - The manager `users` row is required: `decided_by` and `requested_by` are FKs to users. The fixture approval needs `requestedBy: repId`.
   - Renamed the shortage test to carry the DOS id, as the tests schema requires.
   - Its revised :690 assertion passes before the fix too (the UPDATE only touched pending rows). It is an invariant, not the regression check.
5. **Docs note.** Added the examples.ts `x-dos-note` update for `orders.confirm`. After the fix every demo Execute is a 409 and the note would lie. It is not in any README and not pinned by examples.spec.ts, so contractChange stays none.
6. **Root cause additions.**
   - Seeded held orders carry `approval_flags = []` with approvals pending, so the guard must read `approvals` rows.
   - The 5 order-less pending approvals are all bargains, so no credit gate escapes an order-scoped guard.

changes.what:
Add next to `useMutation`, all additive; `reset()` is never called, so the idempotency key and intent are unchanged.

Types:
- `export interface WriteOutcome { readonly status: 'idle' | 'pending' | 'success' | 'error'; readonly error: ApiError | undefined }`. `UseMutationResult` satisfies it structurally.
- `export interface RefusalState { readonly scope: string | null; readonly seen: ReadonlySet<ApiError>; readonly shown: ApiError | undefined }`.

Pure functions:
- `export function refusalStart(writes, scope): RefusalState`: `seen` = every error present now, `shown` = undefined.
- `export function nextRefusal(prev, writes, scope): RefusalState`:
  1. `scope !== prev.scope` → return `refusalStart(writes, scope)`.
  2. `arrived` = current errors not in `prev.seen`; `seen'` = `prev.seen ∪ arrived`.
  3. `shown'` = undefined if any write is pending; else the last of `arrived` if there is one; else `prev.shown` while it is still one of the current errors, otherwise undefined.
  4. Return `prev` ITSELF when `arrived` is empty and `shown' === prev.shown`.

Hook:
`export function useRefusal(writes: readonly WriteOutcome[], scope: string | null = null): ApiError | undefined { const [state, setState] = useState(() => refusalStart(writes, scope)); const next = nextRefusal(state, writes, scope); if (next !== state) setState(next); return next.shown }`

This is React's guarded 'store information from previous renders' pattern; rule 4 keeps it from looping.

The rule it implements:
- an error already there when the surface mounts is not shown again;
- the LATEST refusal wins;
- pressing any write on the surface hides it;
- a new row or document (scope) resets it.

React layer list (lines 104-105): add `useRefusal(writes, scope?)`, with one sentence stating the rule (latest refusal on a surface, hidden by the next press or a scope change, never re-shown on reopen).

The DOS-029 client spec (vitest, same shape as reads.test.ts; no React renderer needed).

Add `'app.writeNoConnection': 'No connection. Check the signal, then press again.'`. It follows UX-00 §12: the next action, and no promise to send later (manager writes have no outbox).

Add `export function Refusal({ of, scope, testID }: { of: readonly WriteOutcome[]; scope?: string | null; testID?: string })`.

plans.risk:
Medium-low. The change is UI only; backend, contract, permissions and database are untouched.

Behaviour changes on purpose:
- A dialog or panel no longer closes on ANY failure; it closes only on success.
- A retry keeps the same idempotency key, because `reset()` is not called. That is safe for refusals: runIdempotent (backend/libs/core/src/platform/idempotency.ts:49-81) inserts the key in the handler's own transaction, so a thrown refusal rolls it back.
- A network failure now shows a manager-owned sentence instead of the false "This will send when the signal is back".

Other risks:
- The refusal rule relies on the guarded setState-during-render pattern. `nextRefusal` must return `prev` unchanged when nothing changed, or the hook re-renders forever; the unit spec covers this.
- Layout:
  - one brick line in dialog bodies and above submit buttons;
  - ExportButton becomes a Stack only while it is not 'ready', which touches the headers of four pages, so check 1280 and 375 px;
  - the messages registers get a line above them.
- On long surfaces (a long messages register, a document with many lines) the refusal can sit outside the viewport when the pressed row is far down. That is a residual limitation.
- On iOS, RN Modal keeps its children until the dismiss callback (Modal.js:279-282). A very fast reopen of the same dialog for the same row can still show the previous sentence; `scope` covers a different row.
- Merge conflicts are likely with the batch fixes that edit the same manager screens (see dependsOn).

Why the old rule fails:

2. Network sentence. `<Refusal>` now maps `kind === 'network'` to a new manager string, `app.writeNoConnection`. DEFAULT_MESSAGE.network promises "This will send when the signal is back", which is false for manager writes (no outbox). Keeping dialogs open would have put that promise on screen. plans.rootCause:
CONFIRMED (reviewer re-traced it). Both findings have the same cause. The same read-and-sum code was copied into two apps, and it runs against a stock read that returns one row per lot per location, 500 rows at most.

1) The client ignores nextCursor. Three screens call `inventory.stock.sellable({ limit: 500 })` once and add up whatever rows come back per item:
- frontend/sales-app/app/orders/new.tsx:98-108, read at :387 (draft line, which also feeds QtyStepper availablePieces at ~:425) and :475 (SuggestionRow chip :581-588). This is S3 order entry, DOS-074.
- frontend/sales-app/app/shops/catalog.tsx:49-59, read at :71 and :170 (S11).
- frontend/retailer-app/app/order.tsx:97-114, read at :432 and :522 (R7, DOS-097).
None of them reads `nextCursor`. No other app calls `stock.sellable` except delivery van-sale.tsx:94, which reads the vehicle location per lot and is out of scope.

2) The only stock read a rep or a shop may call is per lot per location.
- `SellableStockRowSchema` (backend/libs/contracts/src/inventory.ts:103-115) has one row per lot per location, and `limit` is capped at 500 (:121).
- `StockService.sellable` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/inventory/stock.service.ts:167-195) orders by `s.lot_id, s.location_id`. Lot ids are UUIDv7, so the order is creation time.
- Reviewer's read-only SQL on dos_qa tarsun: 793 sellable rows across 166 items; page 1 covers 157 items; 9 in-stock items are missing from page 1 and 122 are wrong on it. Godavari Cheese Slices 200 g reads 'Stock not known'. Campa Orange 1 L / Cola 200 ml / Cola 750 ml read 0 / 1 / 154 cases against 10 / 10 / 404 at the godown.

3) Paging `sellable` to the end would still be wrong.
- The `sellable_stock` view (backend/libs/database/migrations/0003_force_rls_ledgers_views.sql:170-174) covers every location kind. Summing every location overstates 24 of 166 tarsun items (6 vehicle rows, 42 damaged-bin rows).
- An order reserves from exactly ONE location: `order.fulfilFromLocationId ?? warehouseLocation(tx)` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts:331). `warehouseLocation` (orders.internals.ts:188-207) takes the FIRST active `kind='warehouse'` location ordered by id. Packing uses the same rule: `activeWarehouseLocation` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/warehouse.internals.ts:225-244). No frontend sets `fulfilFromLocationId` (git grep: none), so every rep or shop order reserves at that one godown.
- The client cannot filter by location. `SellableStockRow` carries no location kind, and `inventory.locations.list` is STAFF (permissions.ts:476), so a retailer cannot learn the godown's id.

4) An absent item may become 0 only after a complete read. 7 of 171 listed tarsun products have no godown stock. A complete per-item answer lists only items that have stock, so the screens must treat 'complete read, no row' as 0. Otherwise those 7 keep reading 'Stock not known' (retailer) or show no chip (sales).

No second server-side cause:
- RLS lets every member read locations, stock_lots and stock_balances: locations_read, stock_balances_read and stock_lots_read in migration 0012 at :228, :236 and :244.
- There are no triggers on stock_balances or stock_lots.
- The offline path is not involved (sellable_stock is not in the salesperson manifest; the hint is online-only by design).

Real fix, which is DOS-097's suggestion: one per-item availability read at the reserving godown, which the client pages through to the end.

WHAT I CHANGED
1. The godown rule. The plan summed every active kind='warehouse' location. I changed it to the SAME single location orders reserve from: the first active warehouse ordered by id.
   - That rule lives in orders' warehouseLocation() (orders.internals.ts:188-207) and warehouse's activeWarehouseLocation() (warehouse.internals.ts:225-244). No frontend sets fulfilFromLocationId (git grep: none).
   - So in a tenant with two godowns, summing would promise stock no rep or shop order can ever reserve. The finding's expected result is "the godown's sellable total".
   - It is identical in dos_qa today, where every tenant has one warehouse; I re-ran the ground-truth SQL with the subquery rule and got the same 480/9,709/249/7 and 166 items.
   - Added a second-warehouse exclusion to test 2 and a NOT TESTED note for the running product, because proving it there needs a mutation.
2. Tests.
   - The 505-lot fixture must be built in process (findOrCreateLot + one InventoryService.post inside one withTenant transaction), not through ~1,010 HTTP calls, given the 30 s test and 60 s hook timeouts.
   - The retailer actor needs its own membership; inventory.spec.ts has no retailer, so copy billing.spec.ts.
   - Added a third api-client spec: a failed page rejects the whole read. That behaviour is what the OFFLINE verify step relies on.
3. Stale comments that become false are now in scope: the contracts header, sellable's summary, the permissions.ts comment at :474-475, and the STOCK_KEEPERS comment in stock.service.ts:80.
4. Verification: added iOS steps (Appium + Expo Go per QA/ENV.md) because the plan listed ios with no steps, and rewrote the ground-truth SQL to the single-godown rule.
5. dependsOn: added DOS-023 (the same first-page-only class; if its fix is client-side it should reuse readAllPages rather than add a second helper).

WHAT I CONFIRMED (read-only)
- Every cited line in the three screens, the contract, the service, the view, reserve(), both warehouse-location helpers, and the RLS policies (0012:228/236/244).
- There are no triggers on stock_lots or stock_balances.
- DB counts: 793 rows, 166 items, 157 on page 1, 9 missing, 122 wrong, 24 overstated by summing every location, 7 of 171 listed items with no godown stock.
- All variant ids are UUIDs, so IdSchema is safe as the cursor.
- examples.spec builds examples generically, so no QUERY_FILL entry is needed.
- permissions.test has no inventory list that needs editing.
- api-client already runs vitest.
- sales-app and retailer-app have NO test script.
- switchDistributor clears the query cache.

WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM
- The ~178 KB per 500-row payload figure (I did not sign in, to avoid a write).
- Whether the S11 catalog rows are also blank on Android (DOS-077 names only the order-entry rows).
- Whether other batch fixes (DOS-003, DOS-004, DOS-034, DOS-057+DOS-099, DOS-106) change contracts; if they do, they collide on the regenerated READMEs.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS
- The backend tests fail before the fix only because the route does not exist; that is unavoidable for an additive endpoint.
- The screen wiring (absent → 0 only after a complete read) lives in two app hooks with no test runner, so it is proven only by the verify steps. If the founder wants it unit-tested, the map builder would have to move into a lib.

plans.title: The pricing engine reads 'inr' scheme thresholds as rupees, but everything that stores them uses paise, so the "2% off bills over ₹25,000" scheme never applies
plans.rootCause:
One cause: every stored `inr` trigger threshold is in paise, but the engine measures the order in rupees.

1. **The live row is stored in paise.** Scheme 6ac23a1a-ce35-76d2-a002-3a7888fc1c65 in dos_qa (tenant 01a0947d; the same row exists in 82f5c562 and 9fdfb5da) has trigger_kind=value, trigger_unit=inr, trigger_min=2500000, reward order_pct 200, scope {"all":true}, stackable=t, final=f, priority 30, valid 2026-06-14..2026-09-21. 2,500,000 paise is ₹25,000.

2. **Paise is the convention in every writer and every other reader:**
   - Seed: backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/pricing.ts:343 (2_500_000 for ₹25,000) and :537 (400_000 for ₹4,000).
   - The seed's own order pricer compares paise: seed-demo/sales.ts:704 (`gross >= s.triggerMin`) and :896 (`base < s.triggerMin`). This is why 204 seeded orders in dos_qa carry order_pct shares (tarsun 125, sai 67, kalyan 12), while none of the live QA orders SO-0879..SO-0887 does.
   - Owner app: frontend/owner-app/app/prices/index.tsx:157-166. Manager app: frontend/manager-app/app/prices/index.tsx:9 and :88-91. Both say "triggerMin is PAISE when the unit is inr" and format it with formatINR(paise(...)).
   - Retailer app: frontend/retailer-app/src/lib/offer.ts:30 and :66 call formatMoney(triggerMin), and @dos/ui formatMoney takes integer paise (frontend/libs/ui/src/money.ts:13).
   - docs/18-build-log.md:968 and backend/libs/core/src/modules/reporting/reporting.spec.ts:500 (500_000 inr) say the same.
   - The only server writer, schemes.service.ts:163, stores `input.triggerMin` unconverted.

3. **The engine alone uses rupees.**
   - backend/libs/domain/src/pricing/schemes.ts:61 documents "`inr` (rupees of gross line value)".
   - `measure()` at :462-463 returns `lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.gross, 0) / 100`.
   - `evaluateTrigger()` at :481 then runs `if (measured < scheme.triggerMin) return null`. For basket E that is 27339.32 < 2500000, so no candidate is pushed (:279-280) and orderRules stays [].
   - `measure()` is shared by three steps: 3a line-level (:253), 3b order-level (:279) and 5 cash discount (:347). So the unit is wrong for every `inr` trigger. It only shows on the order-value scheme because every live line_pct and cash_discount_pct `inr` threshold is 0.
   - The engine's own tests are written in rupees: schemes.test.ts:179 (triggerMin 30) and :213 (triggerMin 500 against a ₹340 order).

4. **Server and device are wrong in the same way.** Both pass the raw integer to the same engine:
   - Server: quote.service.ts:325 (toSchemeRule).
   - Device: frontend/sales-app/src/lib/pricing.ts:120.
   - Every server re-pricing path goes through QuoteService: orders.service.ts writeLines (:558, called at :147/:165/:214), the offline draft upload (orders.sync.ts:137), van sales (delivery/vansales.service.ts:87) and AI drafts (ai/drafts.service.ts:157), all via pricing-lines.ts:157.
   - That is why SO-0879 stored discount_paise 79442, the line schemes only.
   - There is no second contributing cause: no trigger, RLS policy or worker job touches the threshold.

5. **What allowed the drift.** The contract (backend/libs/contracts/src/pricing.ts:174, :241) and the table (backend/libs/database/src/schema/pricing.ts:166) declare triggerMin as a plain int and never state its unit, while rewardValue's unit is stated (:178).

6. **The finding's suggested fix is shallow.** scope.all and order_pct evaluation already work (the schemes.test.ts 'spreads an order_pct discount' test passes). The defect is the unit inside `measure('inr')`.

7. **Part of the finding's expectation is wrong by design.** SO-0879 and basket C contain lines under "Godavari Ghee — 6% exclusive" (2891ee90, stackable=f, final=t).
   - `lockIfFinal()` (schemes.ts:606-609) sets lockedByFinalScheme, the order-level scope drops those lines (:274), and the trigger is measured over that scope.
   - This matches docs/17 [14] ("first final rule stops the chain") and the seed's `!d.priced.exclusive` (sales.ts:890).
   - Non-exclusive gross is ₹21,297.40 for SO-0879 (verified: subtotal 2953412, exclusive 823672, rest 2129740) and ₹24,095.48 for basket C. Both are under ₹25,000, so after the fix neither earns the 2%.
   - Basket E has no exclusive line (gross ₹27,339.32) and correctly earns ₹543.57.

changes.what: In measure() (:462-463), make `case 'inr'` return integer paise, `lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.gross, 0)`, with the `/ 100` removed. This one line fixes all three callers (3a :253, 3b :279, 5 :347). Fix the SchemeRule doc comment at :60-62: triggerMin is a piece count (pcs), a whole-case count (case) or PAISE of gross in-scope line value (inr). Add a note on SchemeSlab (:34-43) that `min` is in the same unit as triggerMin (paise for inr). No other logic changes: stacking, scope, the final-line exclusion, gross-vs-net measurement, allocate(), multiples and cash discount stay as they are. Do NOT convert in the two toSchemeRule adapters instead: that would duplicate the conversion on server and device and leave the engine's 'mirrors the schemes table' contract false.

First add the failing DOS-075 tests (see tests). Then convert the rupee-valued inr fixture INPUTS to the stored unit and leave every expected value untouched. :213 must change from triggerMin 500 to 50_000: the intent is a ₹500 threshold that a ₹340 order does not reach, and left at 500 it would read as ₹5 and wrongly fire. :179 changes from 30 to 3_000 for unit consistency: 3003 paise still clears it, and it would also pass unchanged. The fixtures at :302, :531 and :617 (triggerMin 1) stay as they are, because every gross there is far above 1 paise.

Add the DB-backed DOS-075 spec after 'rejects a quote for an unpriced or unknown variant'. The owner saves a paise-threshold order_pct scheme through POST /pricing/schemes. The rep quotes shopA / v2 with an explicit pricingDate inside the scheme's own 2031 window. Call `call(app, rep, 'POST', '/pricing/quote', {...})` directly: `quoteFor` hard-codes `today`. Verified fixtures: v2 is only on the default list (₹20, no validity window, so it is valid in 2031); shopA's final override is v1 only; no approved bargain exists for shopA; the 12+1 scheme is v1-scoped and 2026-only. No other test in the file prices on a 2031 date.

Documentation only. Add a JSDoc line on `triggerMin` in schemeEconomics (:174) and UpsertSchemeInput (:241), "pieces (pcs), whole cases (case), or PAISE of gross in-scope line value (inr)", in the style of the rewardValue comment at :178. Add one on SchemeSlabSchema.min (:161), "same unit as triggerMin". No Zod change, no wire change; the README renderer reads Zod at runtime, so `pnpm docs:readme:check` stays green.
