plans.title: Quote a brand-scoped cash discount on its own lines' net, not on the whole order
plans.rootCause:
One cause, in step 5 of the pure engine `priceOrder()` (backend/libs/domain/src/pricing/schemes.ts:338-365). I read the code and re-ran the built engine to confirm it.

1. **Scope decides only eligibility.** Lines 343-345 filter the lines each `cash_discount_pct` scheme covers. That filter is used only for the trigger at 347-348.
2. **The amount is taken on the whole order.** Lines 355-356: `cashDiscountPaise = percentOf(totals.netPaise, cashDiscountBps)`. `totals.netPaise` (331-336) adds up every line, so a `{brandIds:[Too Yumm]}` scheme pays its rate on the whole bill. The `orderRules` entry (357-365) carries the same amount.
3. **The winner is picked by bps alone** (line 350, `value > cashDiscountBps`). That was only harmless while every offer used the same base.

**Reproduced** with backend/libs/domain/dist (inline node, nothing written):
- Too Yumm ₹240 + another brand ₹100, 2% scoped to Too Yumm: 680. Correct figure is 480.
- Too Yumm ₹240 at 2% + Rajwadi ₹1,000 at 1.5%: 200 bps / 2480. Correct is 150 / 1500.
- The finding's basket F: 55766 = 2% of 2,788,324.

**The money path never uses the scheme.** The second half of the suggested fix is wrong:
- An invoice copies the retailer's own term: `cashDiscountBps = i.buyer.cashDiscountBps` (billing/invoices.service.ts:1513), loaded from `retailers.cash_discount_bps` (billing/billing.internals.ts:280, 299).
- Receivables opens the condition from that term (receivables/receivables.service.ts:412-419).
- A receipt pays `percentOf(invoice total, condition bps)` (receivables/allocation.ts:249, 288, 334).
- Order lines store only per-line rules (orders/pricing-lines.ts `toStoredRules(q.appliedRules)`). There is no column for order rules or cash discount.
- Claims skips `cash_discount_pct` (claims/build.service.ts:357).
- dos_qa agrees:
  - 1,497 of 1,503 invoices carry exactly the retailer's term.
  - `cash_discount_conditions` holds only 200 and 250 bps.
  - The finding's own db-11 query of bills without Too Yumm or Rajwadi shows 169 at 200 bps and 23 at 250.

**Where the wrong figure shows up. The planner missed a shop-facing screen:**
- **Retailer app, R7 order screen:** frontend/retailer-app/app/order.tsx:458-472 (testID `r7-cash-discount`) prints `quote.data.cashDiscountPaise` as "Paying early takes ₹X off" or "Pay within {days} days and ₹X comes off" (src/strings.ts:109-110). plans.title: Android order entry: catalog rows show only "Add a case" because the full-width kit Button squeezes the item-name column to 0 dp
plans.rootCause:
Confirmed by reviewer. This is a layout bug on one screen: the text is laid out at 0 dp. It is not a List/FlatList renderer bug, the text is not lost, and no data is missing.

1. Where the rows come from. frontend/sales-app/app/orders/new.tsx:470-481 maps `suggestions` into `<SuggestionRow>` inside a kit `<Group>`, inside `Screen`'s ScrollView. No kit `List`/FlatList is used and no row has a fixed height, so the finding's "Suggested fix" points at the wrong code.

2. How the row is built (new.tsx:549-594).
   - Outer `<Row gap={3} align="center" justify="between" padY={2} padX={3}>` (561-569), not `wrap`.
   - Child 1: `<Stack gap={1} grow>` with the name (`numberOfLines={2}`) and the "brand · N pc case" line (570-579).
   - Child 2: a trailing `<Row gap={2} align="center">` (580) holding the StatusChip and `<Button label={t('s3.addOneCase')} variant="secondary" onPress={onAdd} />` (590). The Button has no `fullWidth` prop.

3. The native kit behaviour.
   - Button defaults to `fullWidth = true` (frontend/libs/ui/src/native/controls.tsx:34) and wraps itself in `<View style={{ width: '100%', flexShrink: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>` (controls.tsx:77).
   - Native `grow` is flexGrow 1 / flexShrink 1 / flexBasis 0 (native/layout.tsx:120-122).
   - The trailing Row has no grow, so its basis is auto and RN's default flexShrink is 0 (layout.tsx:168-187).

4. What Yoga does with that.
   - The inner Row is measured fit-content against the outer Row's content width.
   - The wrapper's `width:'100%'` resolves against that same width, so the inner Row's basis is the whole row, and it does not shrink.
   - The Stack's basis is 0 and it meets negative free space, so it stays 0 dp. Name and brand draw nothing.
   - The same collapse happens if the Button is a direct child next to a grow column: shrink is weighted by basis, and the Stack's basis is 0.

5. The screenshot matches (reviewer re-measured e-02 at 900-px display ×1.2; Pixel 7 = 411 dp).
   - Button left edge: 90 display px = 108 px = 41 dp. That is gutter 16 + Group border 1 + padX 12 + a 0-dp text column + gap 12.
   - Button right edge: 862 display px = 1034 px = 394 dp. That is the Group's inner edge, so the inner Row is 353 dp (the whole row content width) and overflows the 12 dp right padding by exactly the gap.
   - The rounded right corner is drawn, so the button is not clipped. The screenshot shows "Updated just now" (online) but no chip on these rows. Chip or not, the cause is the same.

6. Why web is fine.
   - The web Button also uses `width:100%` at phone width (web/controls.tsx:42,56, `fullWidth ?? !isDesk`).
   - In CSS a percentage width inside an auto-width flex item is treated as auto for intrinsic sizing. `.dos-btn` is `white-space: nowrap` (web/css.ts:60), so the wrapper cannot shrink below its label.
   - The web `grow` column is `flex 1 1 0; min-width 0` (web/layout.tsx:114-117) and takes the rest. p-03-order-entry.txt:13-31 at 390 px shows name, "Campa · 24 pc case", "18 cs available", "Add a case".

7. Scope of the trap (reviewer's own scan: a tag-stack parse of all 147 .tsx files under frontend/*-app/app and src).
   - It looked for any Button without `fullWidth` whose non-wrap Row ancestor has a `grow` child in another branch, including direct children.
   - Only new.tsx:590 matched.
   - Kit ListRow trailing slots in the apps hold chips, not Buttons (e.g. sales-app/app/orders/attention.tsx:85). The Buttons there sit in a `wrap` Row (attention.tsx:87).
   - The Panel head Row is `wrap` (sales-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:66), so its action button wraps below instead of collapsing anything.
   - The existing opt-out pattern is warehouse-app/app/pick/index.tsx:166-190 (`fullWidth={false}`, with a comment explaining why).

8. Data is fine. dos_qa, reviewer SELECT: SO-0884 | confirmed | salesperson | Campa Cola 500 ml | 1 | case | 24.

9. Not causes.
   - The inverted uiautomator bounds [467,710][675,184] are a harness quirk: their centre x of 571 px equals (108+1034)/2. ENV.md:204 records the same inversion for the working retailer steppers.
   - "171 buttons" is the catalog count ("On this phone: 171 items"). The list renders at most 12 rows with an empty query (new.tsx:147) and 30 with a query (new.tsx:155).
   - d-04's "nothing drawn below Add items" is just the fold: the bottom bar starts right under the heading's hairline.
   - No server, contract, sync, RLS or worker path is involved. `onAdd` → `setQty` (new.tsx:476-479) adds the right variant.

plans.title: Retailer order screen shows the pre-GST net as "You pay": make pricing.quote carry the order's own GST and payable total, have orders take GST from it, and show it on R7 (and on R8 lines)
plans.rootCause:
The planner's analysis is right; every citation below was re-read, and the DB figures were re-queried in dos_qa. The finding's suggested fix is wrong on one point: `pricing.quote` does not return GST, and that missing tax is the root cause.

1. R7 labels the pre-GST net as the payable amount.
   - frontend/retailer-app/app/order.tsx:361-364: the bottom bar shows `totals?.netPaise` under t('r7.net') = "You pay" (strings.ts:108).
   - order.tsx:449-457: the totals panel has only Before offers, Offers, and net as "You pay".
   - order.tsx:725: the row rate uses t('r7.perPiece') = '{rate} per piece' (strings.ts:96), which is the ex-GST `ratePaise`.
   - order.tsx:740: the row money is `quoted?.lineNetPaise`, also ex-GST.
   - The ask-for-a-better-rate sheet on the same screen is also unlabelled. order.tsx:563 shows 'r7.askListRate' = "Today's rate is {rate}" and :566 shows 'r7.askRate' = "The rate you want, per piece" (strings.ts:124-125). Both are ex-GST figures. A shop that types a GST-inclusive rate asks for more than list, and the engine silently drops that bargain (`if (rate < 0 || rate >= line.baseRate) continue`, backend/libs/domain/src/pricing/schemes.ts ~:300).

2. The screen's only price source carries no tax.
   - backend/libs/contracts/src/pricing.ts:304-325: `QuotedLineSchema` ends at `lineNetPaise`.
   - pricing.ts:327-342: `QuoteOutput.totals` (:336-341) ends at `netPaise`.
   - backend/libs/core/src/modules/pricing/quote.service.ts:105-127 maps only the `priceOrder()` result.
   - `loadVariants` (:162-190) does not select `hsnCode`.

3. GST is added only when the order is written.
   - backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/pricing-lines.ts: `loadGstBps` (:99-129), the lookup (:164), `gstBps` (:172), `taxPaise = percentOf(lineNet, gstBps)` (:176), `lineTotalPaise = taxable + tax` (:197), and `roundToRupee(subtotal - discount + tax)` (:205).
   - Callers: `OrdersService.writeLines` (orders.service.ts:560), used by create, setLines, submit, repeatLast and sync.
   - The van-sale path uses it too: `delivery/vansales.service.ts:79-87` calls `orders.insertDraft` and then `writeLines`.
   - Confirmed in dos_qa:
     - SO-0885: subtotal 547488, discount 23720 (net 523768 = the ₹5,237.68 on screen), tax 61705, round_off 27, total 585500.
     - SO-0885 lines: 192 pcs @754 −4343, gst 1800, tax 25277, line total 165702 (HSN 1905); 24 @13456 −19377, gst 1200, tax 36428, total 339995 (HSN 0405); 24 @3324, gst 0, total 79776 (HSN 0401).
     - SO-0887: 96 @754, tax 13029, 85413 rounded to 85400 (round_off −13).

4. R8 detail hides the tax as well. frontend/retailer-app/app/orders/[id].tsx:184-187 prints "qty · rate · −discount" beside the GST-inclusive `lineTotalPaise`.

5. What the fix can and cannot guarantee.
   - The bill does NOT copy the order's GST. `InvoicesService.issueForPack` (billing/invoices.service.ts:340) reloads GST and cess from `hsn_rates` at the INVOICE date (`loadHsnRates`, billing.internals.ts:218-253).
   - So, with this fix, screen = order by construction for the tax arithmetic.
   - Screen = bill only when no dated rate change falls between order and invoice, there is no cess (DOS-079, P2, not in batch), and the pack equals the order.

For contrast, the sales app labels its footer "before GST" on purpose (sales-app/app/orders/new.tsx:271-280), because HSN rates are not on the device. The retailer app is online-only and prices through `pricing.quote`, so the fix belongs in the quote.

changes.what: `QuotedLineSchema` (:304-325) gains three fields: `gstBps: BpsSchema`, `taxPaise: PaiseSchema`, `lineTotalPaise: PaiseSchema` (= lineNetPaise + taxPaise). `QuoteOutput.totals` (:336-341) gains `taxPaise`, `roundOffPaise` (signed; PaiseSchema allows negatives, common.ts:7) and `totalPaise` (rupee-rounded payable). Doc comment: GST at the HSN rate dated to `pricingDate`, the same figures the order will store; cess is not included (DOS-079). Output-only and additive. `QuotedLineSchema` is used only by `QuoteOutput`.

(a) `QuoteVariant` gets `hsnCode: string`; `loadVariants` (:169-174) selects `hsnCode: productVariants.hsnCode` (NOT NULL, catalog.ts:119). `bargains.service.ts` also calls `loadVariants`; the extra field is harmless there. (b) Move `loadGstBps` VERBATIM from orders/pricing-lines.ts:98-129: same `desc(effectiveFrom)` first-wins, same 400 message 'No GST rate for HSN … on …; add an hsn_rates row' and same `data: { hsnCodes, on }`. Never a silent 0%. (c) In `quote()`, AFTER `priceOrder` (:83-104), so the error order stays unknown variant → no price → no GST rate, and inside the same `withTenant` tx: `const gst = await loadGstBps(tx, [...new Set([...variants.values()].map(v => v.hsnCode))], result.pricingDate)`. Per line: `gstBps = gst.get(hsn)`, `taxPaise = percentOf(paise(l.lineNetPaise), gstBps)`, `lineTotalPaise = l.lineNetPaise + taxPaise`. Totals: `taxPaise = Σ line tax`, `{ rounded, roundOff } = roundToRupee(paise(result.totals.netPaise + taxPaise))`, spread as `taxPaise`, `roundOffPaise: roundOff`, `totalPaise: rounded`. (d) New imports only: `gte` (drizzle-orm), `hsnRates` (@dos/db), `paise`, `percentOf`, `roundToRupee` (@dos/domain). (e) Class doc comment (:58-62): the quote now carries GST. `hsn_rates_read` is `USING (true)` for app_rw (migration 0002:2361), so every role can read it.

Take GST from the quote instead of recomputing it. (a) Delete `loadGstBps` (:98-129) and the lookup at :164. (c) Drop `hsnCode` from the `entered` mapping (:154), and from `VariantPack` and the `loadVariantPacks` select (:55, :71, :81), since it becomes unused. (d) Remove the now-unused imports `hsnRates`, `percentOf`, `desc`, `gte`, `isNull`, `lte`, `or`. Keep `and`, `eq`, `inArray`, `sql`, `paise`, `roundToRupee`. (e) The header stays a plain sum plus `roundToRupee` (:166-215) and equals `quote.totals` by construction (engine `netPaise = Σ lineNetPaise`, schemes.ts:327-336). (f) Update the file comment (:13-17): GST arrives with the quote. (g) The missing-HSN 400 keeps its status, message and data; it is now raised inside `quotes.quote()`. plans.title: Warehouse picking sheet: add a "Start picking" step for an open wave, lock picks until the device knows the wave has started, and word the device refusal "start it before picking"
plans.rootCause:
Two faults, one on each side. The server's rule itself is correct. I re-read every cited line; all hold.

1) THE WAREHOUSE APP NEVER CALLS `warehouse.picklists.start`.
- frontend/warehouse-app/app/pick/[id].tsx:60-65 reads the device's local `picklists`/`pick_lines`. It writes only through `useRecordPick()` (frontend/warehouse-app/src/lib/queue.ts:53-80, an outbox PUT on `pick_lines`). `useRecordPick` has exactly one caller ([id].tsx:65), so this sheet is the only device pick path.
- Nothing on the sheet checks `sheet.status` before a pick:
  - `pickInFull` (:81-88), `saveShort` (:90-101) and `scan` (:104-118) all queue a pick.
  - The bottom bar (:147-176) offers only Scan and "Take it to packing".
  - `PickLineCard` (:364-381) always shows Picked/Short.
- No file in frontend/warehouse-app calls `picklists.start`. Only the manager desk does (frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/index.tsx:96-100, button :354-364).
- The step was specified and never wired:
  - docs/23-app-screens-and-api-gaps.md:393 says W5 calls `warehouse.picklists.get/start/pick`.
  - frontend/warehouse-app/src/strings.ts:241 'w5.start', :242 'w5.startFailed' and :258 'w5.notStarted' exist, unused.
- Both routes onto the sheet land on an `open` wave:
  - app/pick/index.tsx:84-98 creates a wave, then `router.push('/pick/{id}')`.
  - app/index.tsx:52-56 and :194-206 list `status: 'open'` waves and open the same sheet.

2) THE DEVICE REFUSAL WORDS AN `open` WAVE WRONGLY.
- backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/warehouse.sync.ts:59-64 rejects every status other than `picking` with code `picklist_closed` and "Picklist X is ${status}; it is no longer being picked". A wave that has not started yet gets that same sentence.
- The online path already says it right: `applyPicks` (picklists.service.ts:530-535) says 'start it before picking' when the status is `open`.

WHY THE SERVER RULE STAYS:
- The offline handler is stricter on purpose (picklists.service.ts:525-529).
- `start` is an online state-machine step. picklists.service.ts:331-366 moves each order confirmed→picking through `OrdersService.applyFulfilmentEvent('start_picking')`, which writes the transition row and the outbox event.
- `start` cannot be undone: `cancel` works only while `open` (:394-406).
- warehouse.module.ts:45 registers only `pick_lines` for devices.
- Starting the wave automatically from a queued device op would silently take away the manager's cancel for a wave that may have been meant for cancelling.

WHY THE SCREEN COUNTS A REFUSED PICK AS PICKED:
- `enqueue` writes the optimistic row (queue.ts:59).
- On a rejection, frontend/libs/offline/src/engine.ts:736-748 only sets `_pending='rejected'`.
- frontend/warehouse-app/src/lib/local.ts:244-250 works out the row state from `picked_qty_pcs` alone, and [id].tsx:73 counts it.
- DOS-040 removes this cause for unstarted waves by never letting a pick be queued before the device knows the wave has started. The general "count a rejected op as not picked" is DOS-042.

A GAP IN THE ORIGINAL FIX, FOUND ON REVIEW:
- The sheet row and its lines are separate local tables (`useLocalPicklist` local.ts:172-181, `useLocalPickLines` :187+).
- The server pull uses one cursor with `perTable = limit / tables` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/sync/sync.service.ts:278). On a cold pull where `picklists` is saturated, a wave's `pick_lines` rows can land a page before its `picklists` row.
- Locking only on `status === 'open'` leaves Picked/Short live while `sheet === null`, which is the same defect. The lock must also cover an unknown status.

EVIDENCE:
- QA/evidence/phase1/warehouse/db-03-pick-first-line.txt:43: sync_ops 01a094eb…, `picklist_closed` "Picklist PICK-0079 is open; it is no longer being picked".
- api-start-pick-0079.txt: POST /warehouse/picklists/{id}/start as warehouse → 200 `picking`.
- dos_qa now (SELECT): sync_errors on pick_lines has 2 × `picklist_closed` and 1 × `pick_rejected`. picklists: 1 open, 4 picking, 4 picked, 163 packed. SO-0881, SO-0883 and SO-0884 are `confirmed` and on no picklist.

NO PERMISSION GAP:
- permissions.ts:612 gives 'warehouse.picklists.start' to STOCK_KEEPERS = owner, manager, warehouse (:52).
- WAREHOUSE_DESK includes warehouse (warehouse.internals.ts:35).

The chip and lock read the mutation result (guarded by picklist id) until the pull lands, so an early-returning pull (engine.ts:287) cannot leave the sheet locked after a successful start. If the page is reloaded before the pull lands, the local row may still read `open`; tapping Start again is a safe replay.
- DEVICES THAT ALREADY HOLD A REJECTED PICK against an open wave keep their optimistic "Picked in full" row after Start. That is DOS-042 (counting) and DOS-046 (retry replays the stored rejection).
- NO SERVER RULE IS RELAXED: the offline handler still accepts only `picking`.
plans.reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED IN THE PLAN
1) The lock now also covers an unknown status: `locked = liveStatus === undefined || liveStatus === 'open'`. The original locked only on `'open'`, so Picked/Short stayed live while `sheet === null`. That can happen: the device pull uses one cursor with `perTable = limit / tables` (sync.service.ts:278), so on a cold pull with a saturated `picklists` table a wave's `pick_lines` can land a page before its sheet row. A tap then queues a pick against an open wave, which is the same defect.
2) `start.data` is used only when `start.data.item.id === picklistId`. The root layout renders through `<Slot>` (warehouse-app/app/_layout.tsx). If expo-router reuses the `[id]` instance when only the param changes, sheet A's `picking` would carry onto open sheet B and unlock picks.
3) While not started, the bottom bar shows ONLY Start. Scan is hidden, not disabled with `w5.notStarted`. The original would print "This sheet has not been started" twice on a phone screen (the kit prints `disabledReason` under disabled buttons, web/controls.tsx:65, native/controls.tsx:108-116) and would fight the existing `w.scanUnavailable` reason. This is the plan's own reason for hiding the row actions.
4) `invalidates` is `[['picklists']]` only. `['queue']` is dropped: W4 reads `state:'confirmed', unpicklistedOnly:true` (pick/index.tsx:53-62), which already excludes a waved order, and start does not change it.
5) Added a guard test pinning `picklist_closed` on a cancelled wave. After line 1229 changes, nothing in the repo asserts that code (git grep), so the unchanged branch would lose its only coverage. This is what proves "only the open branch changed".
6) Verify changes:
   - Android now follows the QA route (debug APK + proxy8081.mjs + android-login.sh, QA/ENV.md), not "a dev build".
   - Added the iOS step (platforms lists ios; ios-login.mjs 5176 dinesh.patil warehouse).
   - The after-fix web walk runs in a fresh profile, so the before-fix rejection cannot pollute it.
   - Every step to check is listed.
7) Small citation fixes: the offline test ends at spec:1264 (1266 is the separator); the rejection branch is engine.ts:736-748; the state computation is local.ts:244-250.

WHAT I CONFIRMED BY READING
- Every root-cause cite.
- `useRecordPick` has a single caller, so the lock closes every device pick path.
- The manager M5 app does call start (manager-app fulfilment/index.tsx:96-100); the "never called" claim is correct for the warehouse app.
- `applyPicks` already has the right open wording (picklists.service.ts:530-535).
- `useMutation` keeps the idempotency key per input (api-client react/index.tsx:377-387), and `mutate(picklistId)` matches its signature.
- The api-client's network message is "No connection. This will send when the signal is back." (errors.ts:77), so a Start-specific offline reason is justified.
- The engine's `reachable` starts true (engine.ts:102), so Start is enabled on a fresh open.
- strings.ts is English-only, one map.
- Fixture stock is enough for two more 1-case waves (spec:432-437).
- The cancel route and input are `POST /warehouse/picklists/{id}/cancel {idempotencyKey, reason}` (contracts warehouse.ts:585-588, :864-871; spec:861-866).
- dos_qa: SO-0881/0883/0884 are confirmed and on no picklist; 2 × picklist_closed rows exist.
- I agree the finding's "start on first pick" route is wrong. `start` is online-only, not a registered sync table (warehouse.module.ts:45), and cannot be undone. An auto-start from a queued op would silently take away the manager's cancel.

WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM (read-only; nothing was run)
- The red/green of the spec.
- Whether `<Slot>` really reuses the `[id]` instance; the guard is defensive either way.
- How the warehouse app wires `setNetworkHint` on web and native, i.e. whether Start disables on the offline event or only after the next failed call.
- How often the sheet-row-after-lines ordering happens in practice.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS
- A sibling gap in another app: manager M20 (manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:110-112) lists `open` sheets as active and posts `picklists.pick` online, with no Start on that screen. The server answers 409 with the correct "start it before picking", and nothing is silently miscounted. This is not DOS-040 (different role, online path); flag it separately if wanted.
- The offline lock on a stale local `open` (see risk).
- No frontend unit test is possible: warehouse-app/package.json has no test script, and frontend `pnpm test` covers only libs. The UI half is proven by the web, Android and iOS walks.
- Run `pnpm format` in both workspaces, then backend lint, typecheck and the warehouse core specs, then frontend lint and typecheck.

plans.title: Refuse a pick above its own batch row's ask (server, HTTP and offline), make the manager's M20 pick update the row it shows, and stop the Short sheet saving more than the ask
plans.rootCause:
The server only limits picks per ORDER LINE. One lot row can take more than it asks for as long as the line total stays under. Two clients can do this: the warehouse app W5, and the manager app's M20 pick screen, which the plan missed.

1. **Where each row's ask comes from.** The wave spreads each order line's ask across lot rows: `requestedQtyPcs: allocation.qtyPcs` (picklists.service.ts:246), taken from `suggestLots` (:701-728). That share is the lot's hold, or what `sellable_stock` still had.
   - In dos_qa, PICK-0079 row 01a094c0-82f2-7556-a83b-b1e619c2c0a1 (lot 3a6e7f22, batch RCP20260717) asks 6 and holds picked 20, 'Damaged carton'.
   - That lot's stock_balances: on_hand 6, reserved 0. I confirmed both with SELECTs.

2. **The pick is written with no check against the row's own ask.** `PicklistsService.applyPicks` loops at :556-618 and sets `pickedQtyPcs: pick.pickedQtyPcs` at :581.
   - A pick with a new id is inserted as a split row with `requestedQtyPcs: 0` (:596-611, pinned by warehouse.spec.ts:582-603).

3. **The only quantity rule.** `assertNotOverPicked` (:772-779, called at :620) compares Σ requested with Σ picked per order line, through `perLineTotals` (:750-770). It runs on EVERY pick, so the finding's "only when the last lot is picked" is wrong.
   - Order line 199afd5f asks 240 over 9 rows (confirmed).
   - When the 20 was keyed (sync_ops 01a094f0-08ae, `{"ok": true}`, 14:55:54, confirmed), the line held 5 (RCP20260710 at 14:55:37) + 20 = 25 ≤ 240.
   - Correction to the draft: db-04-after-picks.txt's '121 | 750' is the SHEET's total at 14:57:22. It is not the line's total when the 20 was keyed.
   - The later 246 > 240 refusal is DOS-042 step 1.

4. **Offline uses the same rules.** `applyPickLineSync` (warehouse.sync.ts:66-81) calls the same `applyPicks`. BAD_REQUEST becomes `pick_rejected` (:77-79, :85-88), inside a savepoint (sync.service.ts:121-129).

5. **Why the pack fails.** `whatLeftTheRack` (packing.service.ts:236-280) totals picked per (order line, lot). `InventoryService.postPick` (inventory.service.ts:446-460) then posts −20 on lot 3a6e7f22 against on_hand 6.
   - `stock_balances_on_hand_nonneg` turns into 400 'insufficient stock' (inventory.service.ts:741-745).
   - The pack transaction rolls back, so SO-0877 stays `picking` with 0 pack_confirmations (confirmed).

6. **W5 (warehouse app), where the finding was made.** The Short sheet's `<NumberPad>` has no ceiling:
   - `onChange={setShortPieces}` ([id].tsx:270-278); `saveShort` sends the typed value (:90-101).
   - `useRecordPick` only applies `Math.max(0, trunc)` (queue.ts:72).
   - `NumberPadProps` has no max (ui/src/types.ts:123-134).
   - Both renderers build their digits from the controlled `value` (web money.tsx:286-296, native money.tsx:143-154).

7. **Second client, missed by the draft: M20 (manager app).** `frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:86-95` sends `id: uuidv7()` for every line it records. The screen edits the wave's own rows (`pieces={counts[line.id] ?? line.pickedQtyPcs}`, :236-245), yet every manager pick is INSERTED as a new ask-0 row on the same lot (picklists.service.ts:596-611).
   - A per-row cap keyed on the stored row id (`byId.get(pick.id)`) never sees these rows.
   - So the manager can still record, say, 24 (one case step, `stepByCase`, ui/src/qty.ts:67-70) on a 6-pc row, and the pack fails the same way.
   - The finding says "server accepts it, so all platforms". Without an M20 change the server fix is bypassed by our own manager app.

8. **Design rule the draft's keypad fix conflicts with.** UX-00 §6.3 and UX-02 §4.2 say "No silent clamping": over a bound the value is accepted and the screen says what happens. A pad that silently ignores a key is that kind of clamp.
   - It can also save a wrong figure: keying 1,2 on a 6-pc row would leave "1" on the pad, and Short would save 1.
   - The kit already has the 'blocked with a reason' pattern (qty.ts:72-76).

changes.what:
**Per-row rule in `applyPicks`.** Place it after the variant check (line 568-571) and before `isFefoOverride` (line 572):

`const asked = byId.get(pick.id)?.requestedQtyPcs ?? 0; if (asked > 0 && pick.pickedQtyPcs > asked) throw new ORPCError('BAD_REQUEST', { message: `batch ${lot.batchNo || pick.lotId} on ${sheet.picklistNo ?? sheet.id} asks for ${asked} pcs; ${pick.pickedQtyPcs} were picked` })`

- Read the STORED row (`byId`), never `template` or `working`. For a new id, `template` is another row that has an ask.
- Rows with ask 0 (splits) are skipped. They stay bounded by `assertNotOverPicked`.
- BAD_REQUEST, so warehouse.sync.ts `isBusinessFault` returns `pick_rejected`.
- The message still contains 'asks for N', so warehouse.spec.ts:567-580 (/asks for 24/) keeps passing.
- JSDoc (lines 509-518): add a bullet after the per-line one: 'a row the wave created (requested > 0) may not take more than its own ask (400); extra pieces from another batch go on a split row'.

Short sheet only. No kit change, no react-native or react-dom import. Follows UX-00 §6.3: accept the value, explain it, and refuse the save.

1. **Derive state.** In the component: `const ask = shortFor?.line.requested_qty_pcs ?? 0` and `const overAsk = shortFor !== null && ask > 0 && (shortPieces ?? 0) > ask`. Split rows (ask 0) are not capped, matching the server.
2. **`<NumberPad>`.** Keep `onChange={setShortPieces}`. Add `expected={ask > 0 ? ask : null}` and `expectedLabel={t('w5.bin', { pieces: ask })}`. `w5.bin` is 'Requested {pieces} pc' (strings.ts:262), currently unused. check-in.tsx:171 already prints a label next to its figure the same way.
3. **Reason line.** Directly under the pad, inside the same `<Stack>`: `{overAsk ? <Txt field="body" desk="body" color={colors.status.brick.fg} testID="w5-short-over">{t('w5.overAsk', { pieces: ask })}</Txt> : null}`. This is the same brick-line pattern as pack/[orderId].tsx:289.
4. **`saveShort`.** First line after the null check: `if (overAsk) { haptics.error(); return }`. The sheet stays open with the reason visible, and nothing is queued.
5. **Pre-fill (`onShort`, line 228) is NOT changed.** Short is only offered on `todo` rows, and local.ts:245-249 makes a row `todo` only when picked < requested or requested = 0. The draft's `Math.min` pre-fill was dead code.

Add one key next to `w5.enterPieces` (line 263): `'w5.overAsk': 'This batch asks for {pieces} pc. Count again — more cannot be saved on this line.'` (The file is English-only for the pilot, per its header.)

**M20 updates the row it shows, so the per-row rule covers the manager role too.**

- In the `recordPick` mutation (lines 78-97), add `id: string` to the line type and send `id: line.id` instead of `id: uuidv7()` (line 90).
- In `commit` (lines 130-134), map `id: line.id`.
- Remove the now-unused `import { uuidv7 } from '@dos/domain'` (line 18) so lint passes.
- No other change: no stepper cap and no new string.
- **Why:** the contract says an id already on the sheet updates that row (contracts warehouse.ts:555-558), and this screen edits `line.id`'s own count. A fresh id both bypasses the new rule and leaves the displayed row at its old count.
- The manager SEEING the 400 is DOS-029 (this app swallows refusals).

Comment only. Extend the `RecordPickInput` JSDoc (lines 565-570): 'and a row the wave created may not take more than its own requestedQtyPcs (400)'. No schema, route or summary change, so `pnpm docs:readme` output stays identical.

Line 43, the `warehouse.picklists.pick` behaviour cell: next to 'Σ picked_qty_pcs per order line may not exceed requested_qty_pcs (400)', add 'and a row the wave created may not take more than its own requested_qty_pcs (400); split rows ask 0 and are bounded by the line total'.

Add the two DOS-041 specs right after 'accepts a pick from a device and never answers 4xx' (it ends at line 1264), before the `// roles:` comment (line 1267). No other spec uses variantB after line 1198, so the new lot cannot change an earlier FEFO assertion.

**Fixture** (inside the first spec; file-level `let dos041Picklist = ''`, `dos041Order`, `tinyLot`, `tinyRow`, `bRow`):
- `const inventory = app.get(InventoryService)`.
- `await asOwner(async (tx) => { const tiny = await inventory.findOrCreateLot(tx, { variantId: variantB, batchNo: `TINY-${run}`, mrpPaise: 2000, expiryDate: '2027-03-31' }); tinyLot = tiny.lot.id; await inventory.post(tx, [{ lotId: tinyLot, locationId: godown, qtyDelta: 6, reason: 'opening', idempotencyKey: `open-${run}-tiny` }]) })`.
  - `findOrCreateLot` takes `tx` and returns `{ lot, created }`; the draft omitted both.
- `dos041Order = await placeOrder([{ variantId: variantB, cases: 2 }], 'dos041')` gives 24 pcs. `reserve` orders by `expiry_date asc` (inventory.service.ts:341-373), so the holds are TINY 6 and lotB 18.

plans.risk:
Low to medium.

- **Substituting stock beyond a row's ask is now refused on that row.** Extra pieces from another batch must go on a split row (new id), which the API supports. W5 never re-points or splits (queue.ts:57-76 always PUTs the existing id). After this change M20 no longer creates split rows either.
- **M20 gets stricter, and a gap already there becomes visible.** Its QtyStepper only steps by whole cases (qty.ts:67-70), and no `onOpenPieces` is passed. A manager therefore cannot key a part-case ask (e.g. 6 pc in a case of 24) at all.
  - Today the manager records 24, which is accepted and can break the pack. After the fix it is refused.
  - This is correct for DOS-041. Loose-piece entry on M20 is a separate, unreported issue and is not fixed here.
  - Until DOS-029 lands, the manager's refusal is invisible.
- **Devices with an over-ask pick already queued** will see `pick_rejected` in the attention tray instead of a silent accept. This is intended.
- **Still open, out of scope:**
  - An API-only split row can still take more from a batch than that batch holds.
  - Re-pointing an asking row onto a thin lot can still overdraw it.
  - A FEFO row suggested from unreserved `sellable_stock` can lose that stock to another order before pack.
  - Pack stays the stock guarantee in all three cases.
- **Existing bad rows are not repaired,** and are only re-checked when a request touches them.
plans.reviewNotes:
**What I changed from the draft**

1. **Added the M20 manager-app client.**
   - frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:90 sends `id: uuidv7()` on every line. Every manager pick is therefore inserted as an ask-0 split row, which the draft's `byId.get(pick.id)` check skips by design.
   - Without `id: line.id`, the manager role still reproduces DOS-041 (and adds a duplicate row each time).
   - I checked for an existing finding on this: none in QA/findings/02 or 08.
2. **Replaced the keypad key-refusal with accept + explain + refuse-to-save,** per UX-00 §6.3 and UX-02 §4.2 ('No silent clamping').
   - A silently refused key can leave a wrong figure on the pad (1 instead of 12), which Short would then save.
   - This adds one string key, `w5.overAsk`, and uses `haptics.error()`, which exists on web and native.
3. **Dropped the draft's `Math.min` pre-fill.** Short is only shown on `todo` rows, and local.ts:245-249 never makes a row with picked ≥ requested > 0 `todo`, so it was dead code.
4. **Mirrored the server's `requested > 0` exemption in the app.** The draft's guard would have refused every non-zero key on an ask-0 split row.
5. **Corrected the evidence in rootCause.** db-04's 121 is the sheet's total at 14:57:22. The line held 25 of 240 when the 20 was keyed at 14:55:54 (sync_ops 01a094f0-08ae, `{"ok": true}`).
6. **Corrected the spec fixture.**
   - `findOrCreateLot(tx, …)` returns `{ lot }`, and `inventory.post` needs `idempotencyKey`.
   - Rows must be found by `lotId`, because wave rows come from `[...held].reverse()`.

plans.title: Close a picking wave only when every short line has had every lot row it was asked on recorded
plans.rootCause:
The wave closes early because completion is judged on the order-line total, never on each lot row. A short on one lot therefore "explains" lot rows nobody touched. The DOS-041 over-pick only caused the rejected upload; it did not close the wave. I re-read every citation below.

1. **The completion rule** (`backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/picklists.service.ts:781-793`, `refreshCompletion`):
   - It works on `perLineTotals(working)` (:750-770), which sums requested and picked over every row of an order line (:764-765) and keeps the first non-null `shortReason` (:766).
   - `done` is `t.picked >= t.requested || (t.picked > 0 && t.shortReason !== null)` (:790). A row's own `pickedAt` is never consulted.
   - `create` inserts every row with `pickedAt` NULL (:236-251). `applyPicks` stamps `pickedAt: now` on every row it records (:585-586).
   - Result: once any lot of a line is shorted with a reason and the line has picked anything, the line counts as done. Its untouched rows are ignored, and the wave flips to `picked` as soon as the other lines finish (:791-792).

2. **Proof in dos_qa (PICK-0079)**, re-queried 2026-09-12:
   - `status=picked`, `completed_at` 14:58:35.095. That is the `picked_at` (14:58:35.094) of the last row recorded (RCP20260822, line f3c97559).
   - Line 199afd5f already had reasons from 14:55:37 (RCP20260710 5/12, RCP20260717 20/6, RCP20260529 0/1).
   - Its B20260902 row is requested 80, picked 0, `short_reason` NULL, `picked_at` NULL, `updated_at` 14:03:59 (wave creation).
   - The line stood at 166/240 with a reason, so it counted as done.

3. **Why the picker could not correct it.** This follows from the early close:
   - The offline handler accepts ops only on `picking` waves (`warehouse.sync.ts:59-64`), deliberately (`picklists.service.ts:526-529`).
   - Nobody can cancel a started wave: `cancel` is PIN_HOLDERS (owner, manager) and only while `open` (:396, :403). The warehouse role is not a PIN holder at all.
   - So the later short is rejected as `picklist_closed`. The finding's first Expected ("stays picking until every line has a pick or a short") removes the dead end. Letting devices reopen `picked` waves would reverse a recorded design choice, so it is not part of this fix.

4. **The three counts on the screen** (a second, client-side cause):
   - `frontend/warehouse-app/src/lib/local.ts:244-249` works out each row's state from the values the device wrote optimistically, even when the engine marked the row `_pending='rejected'` (`frontend/libs/offline/src/engine.ts` `setPending(..., 'rejected')`). So "24 of 24".
   - A pull only holds back `queued`/`sending` rows (`pendingKeys`, `engine.ts` ~:484-488). The next pull or reload replaces the row with the server copy, so "23 of 24".
   - The badge is the server status, wrongly `picked`.
   - `app/pick/[id].tsx:73,78,166` counts rows and enables "Take it to packing" from that local state.

5. **What the original plan got wrong: a second writer records picks ONLY as split rows.**
   - The manager app's M20 screen (`frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:84-95`) sends every counted row as `id: uuidv7()`.
   - `applyPicks` therefore INSERTS a new row with `requestedQtyPcs: 0` (:553, :594-610) and never stamps `pickedAt` on the wave's own row.
   - The path is live: manager-service :3002 serves `POST /warehouse/picklists/{id}/pick` (checked in its /docs/openapi.json), `warehouse.picklists.pick` is STOCK_KEEPERS (permissions.ts:613), and M20 is in the manager nav (`src/nav.ts:67`).
   - The documented contract also allows it: "an id not on the sheet creates an extra row … which is how a lot split is recorded" (docs/plans/warehouse.md:43).
   - A global rule "every row that asks for pieces has pickedAt" would stop a wave picked in full from M20 from ever reaching `picked`. M20's Pack view lists only `status === 'picked'` sheets (`pack.tsx:117`), so the manager could no longer pack from that screen.
   - The defect in the finding only exists on a SHORT line: a line whose picked total reaches its ask has no missing pieces, whichever rows carried them.
   - So the right rule is per line: a line is done when it is fully picked, OR when it has picked > 0 with a short reason AND none of its asking rows (`requestedQtyPcs > 0`) still has `pickedAt` NULL.

changes.what:
In `refreshCompletion` (:781-793), first collect the order lines that still have an unrecorded ask: `const unrecorded = new Set<string>(); for (const row of working.values()) if (row.requestedQtyPcs > 0 && row.pickedAt === null) unrecorded.add(row.orderLineId)`. Then iterate `[...this.perLineTotals(working)]` as `[orderLineId, t]` pairs: `done = totals.length > 0 && totals.every(([orderLineId, t]) => t.picked >= t.requested || (t.picked > 0 && t.shortReason !== null && !unrecorded.has(orderLineId)))`.

What stays unchanged:

plans.risk:
Low. The change only makes the `picking → picked` flip stricter, and only for short lines.

**Waves that now stay `picking` longer:**
- A short line with an asking row not yet recorded. That is the fix itself.
- A short line with a lot-less row. `queue.ts:57` drops device picks on those rows, so it closes once the row is recorded through the API with a lot, or once the order is packed.
- A mixed case: a device shorts one lot of a line, and a manager records the rest from M20, which always writes new rows. M20 can then close that wave only by counting the line in full. This does not undo the fix; it is flagged in notes as an M20 follow-up.

**Downstream effects:**
- The warehouse app's Pack tab lists orders by order state `picking` (`app/pack/index.tsx:29-30`), and `packs.confirm` never checks wave status. `markPackedIfComplete` (:849) accepts `picking`, so the warehouse flow is not blocked.
- M20's Pack view DOES filter on `status === 'picked'` (`manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:117`). That is why the rule is per short line and not per wave: M20's own full-count picks still close the sheet, and the guard test and verify C prove it.
- The old plan's claim that "nothing downstream is blocked" was wrong for M20.

**Seeded and dos_qa waves:** PICK-0039/0052/0078 are already `picking` with unrecorded rows; nothing changes for them until they are picked.

**Frontend:** only rows whose upload was refused change; they show as still to do.
plans.reviewNotes:
**What I changed in the plan**

1. **The completion rule.**
   - The original plan's rule was wave-wide: every row with `requestedQtyPcs > 0` must have `pickedAt`, plus the line rule.
   - That breaks a live client. The manager app's M20 (`manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:84-95`) records every pick under `id: uuidv7()`, so `applyPicks` inserts split rows asking 0 (:594-610) and never stamps the wave's own rows. M20 is served on :3002 (checked /docs/openapi.json), allowed to managers (permissions.ts:613, WAREHOUSE_DESK includes manager) and in the manager nav (nav.ts:67).
   - Under that rule a wave picked in full from M20 never reaches `picked`, and M20's Pack view lists only `picked` sheets (pack.tsx:117).
   - It would also contradict the documented split semantics (docs/plans/warehouse.md:43), for example a lot substitution recorded under a new id.
   - The amended rule adds the row check only to the short-line branch. The defect needs a short line; a line picked in full has no missing pieces.
2. **A third test** (a guard, which passes today) pins the M20 pattern so a future tightening cannot silently break the manager's pack flow.
3. **The existing tests are made robust.** Strictly descending lot expiries per test make FEFO pick each test's own lot even if an earlier test failed partway, and rows are looked up by lotId.
4. **Verify.**
   - Each scenario now uses its own order; the old plan reused SO-0867 for the rejected-op scenario and Android. SO-0868 and SO-0867 still qualified, and SO-0884/0883/0881 were added from a fresh query.
   - Added the M20 check (vikas.kadam :5174).
   - Added billing spec and manager smoke.
   - Restart manager-service as well as warehouse-service, since both mount the rule.
5. **Corrected facts.** The warehouse role cannot cancel any wave (`cancel` is PIN_HOLDERS and open-only), not merely a started one. The risk section's "packing does not require picked" holds for the warehouse app, but not for M20's Pack list.

**What I confirmed by reading or SQL**
- Every citation in the root cause.
- The PICK-0079 rows and timestamps.
- `queue.ts:57` drops lot-less rows, and the device always PUTs the row's own id with its own lot, so the device never creates split rows.
- The engine holds back only queued/sending rows on pull.
- W6 uses `picked_qty_pcs`, not `state`.
- No other module reads picklist `picked` or `completed_at`.
- No contract description states the rule.
- The smoke pick uses the row's own id at full quantity with no status assertion.
- billing.spec's short pick uses the row's own id.

**What I could not confirm**
- I ran no tests (read-only), so "fails before, passes after" rests on reading the code.
- Whether owner-service mounts the warehouse module.
- That SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` resets `_pending` to NULL. The column is not in the server row, so it should fall back to its default.
- The DOS-040 and DOS-041 plan texts themselves; I read only their findings.

**Residual doubts**
- `picked > 0` is kept, so a short line whose every row is shorted to 0 never completes. That was already so before this fix, and pack still works.
- The sync handler reads the wave with `findPicklist`, not `lockPicklist` (warehouse.sync.ts:52). Two devices finishing the last two rows at the same moment can miss the close; they can never close early, because `pickedAt` only goes from NULL to set.
- DOS-041 must not add a per-row cap that refuses pieces on split rows asking 0. That would break M20 and the existing split test.

2. **M20 records every pick as a new split row** (`manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:90`, `id: uuidv7()`).

**What I verified.** Every root-cause citation was re-read and holds (line offsets within ±3), including:
- the RLS policy texts: deliveries_read, load_sheets_read, audit_log_insert and trips_update
- the app_rw grants on audit_log
- the dos_qa evidence: trip 72649337 active, 5 orders packed, sheet 374f2089 draft, outbox TripLoading/TripDeparted 36 s apart, 0 trip audit rows
- the absence of any founder decision in docs/22 that lets the godown depart
- that no offline sync op, worker job or other spec calls depart; only delivery.spec.ts and smoke do.

The plan's direction is right, and I could not refute the core fix.

**What I changed:**
1. Two more stale comments in the change list:
   - confirmedForTrip's JSDoc says it is "the ONLY thing delivery asks the warehouse" (load-sheets.service.ts:594-598)
   - the contracts/delivery.ts header says the same.
   The plan only added a JSDoc on the new method, which would have left both contradicting it.
2. The smoke sweep comment at smoke-endpoints.mts:2605-2607 ("the godown plans and departs") becomes false. Added as a comment-only change. I checked that smoke logic needs nothing else: classify turns the refused 403 into EXPECTED, and addStop still admits a desk role on a `loading` trip.
3. W10 dialog detail:
   - `asking` must be cleared on success and on error, or a refused call leaves the dialog open over the error text.
   - `useState` must be imported from react.
   - The audit `after` must carry ISO strings, not Date objects.
4. Core spec step 7: CancelLoadSheetInput requires `id` as well as `reason` (contracts/warehouse.ts:728-731). Step 6 now also asserts no TripDeparted in the outbox.
5. Verification:
   - The BEFORE walk no longer runs on dos_qa. Plan v1 offered Sai's TRIP-NEXT there, which would put a second tenant into the defect state and contradicts QA/STATE.md.
   - Both walks run on template copies, ids looked up by trip_no and slug.
   - Warning added: never open a session on dos_batch1_template itself.
   - iOS step added; the plan listed ios as a platform with no iOS step.
   - Note added that the AFTER depart gives sachin.dalvi two active trips (DOS-061's symptom, not a regression).
6. Citation fixes:
   - The DepartTripInput JSDoc is at ~707-713, not 699-707 (699 is StartLoadingInput).
   - The retailer-service README also carries a depart row (:165).
   - dispatchIfPacked starts at :842.

**What I could not confirm:**
- `delivery.mappers.ts:590` (not opened).
- Whether dos_batch1_template holds the same trip ids as dos_qa (deliberately not queried, see above).
- What the other batch plans actually touch. The dependsOn list is kept as the planner's file-overlap estimate:
  - DOS-039: hard, same file, and the happy path needs count-out to work.
  - DOS-040/041/042: warehouse strings.ts.
  - DOS-056/058: delivery.spec.ts.
  - DOS-061: the driver side of the same scenario.
  - DOS-025: the manager must see the draft sheet.
  Any batch fix that changes a contract (e.g. DOS-106 or DOS-073, if theirs touch permissions or contracts) will also regenerate the same READMEs: resolve by re-running `pnpm docs:readme` after merging, never by hand-merging.

**Residual doubts, for the approval gate:**
- (a) Keeping start-loading open to the godown without a sheet gate follows the documented design (JSDoc, docs/plans/delivery.md, the state machine) but rejects the finding's literal Expected. The founder should confirm it.
- (b) There is no trip-date gate. A crew can still depart a trip dated two days ahead once its sheet is counted out or absent. The date rule is a founder question, and the "two active trips" symptom belongs to DOS-061.
- (c) Removing a role from a procedure is a product change under charter A.6. It needs explicit approval, then a docs/22 §8 row plus render, and a QA/13-change-log.md entry. docs/plans/delivery.md:32 and docs/plans/00-coordination.md:619 still list warehouse on depart; they are historical briefs and docs/22 wins.

plans.title: Picking sheets list is newest first by server creation time, and the manager's Pick & pack asks the server for live sheets by status
plans.rootCause:
Two contributing causes, both confirmed. The server sorts on the client id. The Pick & pack screen also filters a capped page on the client. Each one alone hides live sheets.

1. The server sorts on the client-generated id.
   - `PicklistsService.list()` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/picklists.service.ts:275-315) orders by `desc(picklists.id)` (line 292) and pages with `lt(picklists.id, input.cursor)` (line 286).
   - The route promises "Picklists, newest first" (backend/libs/contracts/src/warehouse.ts:836).
   - The real creation time is `created_at`, stamped by the server (`timestamps.createdAt … defaultNow()`, backend/libs/database/src/schema/columns.ts:9). `insertPicklist` never sets it (picklists.service.ts:797-812).
   - The contract file's header comment even states the convention: "pages on the last row's id descending" (warehouse.ts:81-82).

2. On demo data, id order is random.
   - `scopedDemoId()` (backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/ids.ts:74-86) is sha1 with the version nibble forced to 7, so it has no timestamp bits. Seed picklists use `demoId('picklist', day)` (seed-demo/warehouse.ts:144).
   - A real `uuidv7()` starts with Date.now(), so a sheet made today begins `01a0…` and sorts below nearly every seeded row.
   - Re-checked on dos_qa, tenant tarsun, 79 sheets, `ORDER BY id DESC`: PICK-0047, PICK-0077, PICK-0009, PICK-0071, PICK-0019. This is exactly the screen order in QA/evidence/phase1/manager/18-wave-made.txt:122-174.
   - In id order PICK-0078 (`picking`) is row 65 and PICK-0079 is row 79, both past the 50-row page.
   - `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` gives PICK-0079 (14:03:59.495365), 0078, 0077, 0076.
   - Current state differs from the finding: PICK-0079 is now `picked` (the warehouse walk picked it). Statuses: packed 76, picked 2, picking 1.

3. The screens.
   - Waves: frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/index.tsx:75-77 reads one unfiltered `{ limit: 50 }` page and renders it as-is (284-297). The new sheet is off the page, before and after a reload. manager-service.log shows `GET /warehouse/picklists?limit=50` right after the POST.
   - Pick & pack: frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/pack.tsx:66-68 reads the same unfiltered page, then filters it on the client for open/picking (110-112) and picked (117). This is an independent cause, not a "latent" one: PICK-0078 is the only `picking` sheet, so a server read with `status: 'picking'` would have returned it even under the broken id order. Filtering on the client dropped it, and the tab says "Nothing to pick or pack" (strings.ts:347; evidence 22-pick-pack.txt).
   - The warehouse home already asks the server by status (frontend/warehouse-app/app/index.tsx:47-56).

4. "Sheet rows are not clickable": NOT CONFIRMED, and the planner's explanation is refuted.
   - The rows are wired. index.tsx:293-295 `onSelect` sets `setOpenSheet`. The web Register renders `<tr onClick={() => onSelect?.(row)}>` (frontend/libs/ui/src/web/list.tsx:575-584); native wires `onSelect` at frontend/libs/ui/src/native/list.tsx:433-436.
   - The overlay theory does not fit the timing:
     - The only uncaught ApiError in ~/.dos-qa-logs/logs/manager-app.log (line 95) is DOS-031's docint review, at walk step 32. DOS-023's steps are 15-19b.
     - DOS-024's 409 (walk step 21, POST req-52) is caught by `createWave.mutateAsync(...).then(ok, done)` (index.tsx:186). It cannot raise Expo's `#error-overlay`.
   - The logs show no successful sheet-row click:
     - manager-service.log has NO `GET /warehouse/picklists/{id}` at any point in the walk.
     - The same Register → onSelect → `enabled` useQuery pattern on load-out.tsx:84 did produce `GET /warehouse/load-sheets/fc53d591…` (evidence 26-load-sheet-open).
   - So either no sheet row was ever clicked, or the click was intercepted by something unrecorded. The claim is in the finding's Actual, so verify step 8 is a gate, not a formality.

5. "Assigned to a picker": out of scope.
   - docs/23-app-screens-and-api-gaps.md:223 specifies M5 as create picklist, watch progress, cancel an unstarted wave.
   - `start` accepts `assignedTo` (picklists.service.ts:344,354), but no manager UI chooses a picker. That would be a new feature; record it, do not build it here.

6. Why not a client sort, and why not a seed change.
   - Sorting 50 rows in the browser cannot bring back rows the server left off the page.
   - Time-ordered demo ids would break ids.ts:30-33 (byte-identical ids quoted by /docs examples, `pnpm smoke` and specs). The seed is idempotent by id, and QA/STATE.md:10 says "no more seed work".
   - Ordering by a client id is also wrong in production: device clock skew.

Same class of defect: load-sheets.service.ts:222-238 (`desc(loadSheets.id)`) is DOS-025.

Not a pattern to copy: platform-admin/console.service.ts:260 orders by `createdAt desc, id desc` but pages with `id < cursor`. That is an inconsistent keyset, recorded as adjacent.

plans.rootCause:
The defect is in the manager-app screen only. The backend, contract, permissions, RLS and triggers all behave. I checked each claim below against the code or the database.

1. The screen never asks for the approval queue.
   - `frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/load-out.tsx:79-81` makes one unfiltered read: `api.api.warehouse.loadSheets.list({ limit: 100 })`. It ignores `nextCursor`.
   - Lines 123 and 202-216 put every row into one `<Register>` in server order. The chip label (lines 137-147) is the only sign that a row needs the manager.
   - The contract already has `status` (`backend/libs/contracts/src/warehouse.ts:669-676`). The warehouse home already reads drafts this way (`frontend/warehouse-app/app/index.tsx:62-66`). M7 does not.

2. The server's order buries a draft.
   - `backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/load-sheets.service.ts:228` sorts by `desc(loadSheets.id)`, with keyset paging `lt(id, cursor)` at line 222.
   - Seeded ids are sha1 hashes: `demoId('load-sheet', …)` at `backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/warehouse.ts:311`, built at `seed-demo/ids.ts:74-86`. So the seeded order is effectively random.
   - dos_qa, Tarsun (tenant 01a0947d-7a79-75d2-bfff-97e499a58d49): 83 sheets, 82 confirmed and 1 draft. 61 ids sort above draft 374f2089, so it is row 62. The evidence agrees: the 12 Sep row is at `QA/evidence/phase1/manager/23-load-out.txt:822-825`, and the footer at line 1107 reads "83 rows".
   - A UUIDv7 minted today (prefix 01a09679…) sorts below 81 of the 83 seeded ids. A new sheet would be row 82 of 84, not row 84 as the plan said.
   - In production, where every id is a real UUIDv7, `desc(id)` puts the newest sheets first, so a draft built just now usually shows near the top. What production actually lacks:
     - a separate place for the approval queue;
     - any way to see a draft that sits below a sheet created after it (van 1's waiting draft under van 2's confirmed sheet);
     - any way to see a draft older than the newest 100 sheets, which is never fetched.

3. The finding's facts need correcting.
   - The draft was on the page (83 rows, not 82).
   - It was already approved. The seed writes `approvedBy` / `approvedAt` on every row, today's draft included (`seed-demo/warehouse.ts:344-345`), and `occurred()` (`seed-demo/util.ts:109-113`) never returns null. SQL: approved_by a1cbd424 (vikas.kadam), approved_at 12 Sep 12:10 IST.

plans.title: Offline doorstep delivery: the server keeps the queued photo, Expo's native fetch failure counts as no signal, the app saves to the outbox when the office never answered, and the tray drops the Zod JSON and the dead "Send it again"
plans.rootCause:
Four separate defects. The web loss and the Android loss have different causes, and both must be fixed.

1) WEB: the office refuses a correctly queued delivery. The server's device mapper drops the photo.
- The app queues one `deliveries` PUT. The photo rides in it as `pod[].inline = {mimeType, contentBase64}` (frontend/delivery-app/src/lib/queue.ts:181-197; the offline pod is built at app/stop/[id]/deliver.tsx:322-329).
- `applyDeliverySync` maps the proof with `podFromDevice` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/delivery/delivery.sync.ts:135). `podFromDevice` (:218-228) copies id, kind, object_key, payload, lat, lng and captured_at. It never reads `p.inline`.
- The photo therefore reaches `RecordDeliveryInput` with neither `objectKey` nor `inline`. The `PodEvidenceInput` refine fails (backend/libs/contracts/src/delivery.ts:576-593), and `parsed()` throws `SyncRejection('row_invalid', …)` (delivery.sync.ts:43-49).
- The stale veto is not involved. `vetoIfStale` (sync/sync.registry.ts:510-532) does apply to `deliveries` (database/src/sync-tables.ts:99, key ['id']), but it passed: the op reached the handler.
- dos_qa confirms it:
  - `sync_errors` row: op 01a0955f-3b8d-7122-8b4f-7e03d1950ef9, device 01a0952a-33e7-76de-83e8-bb6650c9cf2c, code row_invalid, 16:58:19, unresolved.
  - TRIP-ACTIVE stop 8 (Laxmi Narayan Stores, POST_FULFILLMENT): still arrived, outcome NULL, 0 pods.

2) The tray shows Zod JSON. `parsed()` uses `result.error.message` (delivery.sync.ts:48), which in Zod 4 is the JSON issues array; attention.tsx:127-129 prints it verbatim. It is the only sync handler that does this (docint.sync.ts writes its own sentences).

3) ANDROID (and iOS): the planner's mechanism is wrong. The native network failure is classified `unknown`, not `network`.
- Expo SDK 57.0.20 replaces the global `fetch` on native with expo/fetch (frontend/node_modules/expo/src/winter/runtime.native.ts:41-52). No app sets `EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_RN_FETCH`.
- A refused, unreachable or aborted request rejects with `FetchError extends Error`. Its message is always "fetch failed: …" and its `name` stays 'Error' (expo/src/winter/fetch/FetchErrors.ts:1-11; fetch.ts:78 and :88-93).
- `toApiError` (frontend/libs/api-client/src/errors.ts:130-161) recognises only ApiError, ORPCError, the AbortError/TimeoutError names and TypeError. So it returns kind 'unknown' with "Something could not be completed. Try again." DOS-068's Android evidence shows exactly that: trip history "· unknown", where delivery-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:176-181 renders the kind as the detail.

That one misclassification causes both halves of the symptom:
- (a) `status.online` stays true. The engine's `call()` sets `reachable = false` only when `isNetworkFailure` is true (engine.ts:996-1005, 1137-1149). For `ApiError{kind:'unknown', message:'Something could not…'}` it is false.
  - The planner's explanation, that `setNetworkHint(true)` resets `reachable`, does not apply on native. The only hint wiring listens for `globalThis` online/offline events (offline/src/react.tsx:118-139), which React Native does not have, and delivery-app never calls `setNetworkHint`.
  - Screenshot a-42d confirms the result: green dot, "1 waiting to send", button "Record the delivery".
- (b) `commit()` takes the online branch (deliver.tsx:289, :360). `files.uploadUrl` rejects with kind 'unknown'. The catch (:388-390) only calls `setError`, so `d4-error` shows "Something could not be completed. Try again." below the fold. That is not errors.ts:77 as the plan says. Nothing reaches `queueDelivery`, and the delivery is lost.
- Consequence for the plan: a fallback keyed on `toApiError(e).kind === 'network'` would never fire on a phone. The P1 loss would remain on exactly the platform where it was observed.
- The photo PUT (`platformFiles.upload`, ui/src/platform/files.native.ts:35-47 and files.web.ts:49-61) is a plain global fetch outside the api-client: no deadline and raw errors.
- dos_qa: TRIP-NEXT stop 1 (City Light Provision, POST_FULFILLMENT) is arrived at 16:48:54.785 with outcome NULL, 0 pods and `arrived_lat` NULL.

4) "Send it again" sends nothing.
- The web tray entry was mirrored from the server by `pullErrors` (engine.ts:370-410) after a page load emptied the memory store:
  - d-50: Waiting 0, Refused 1, "Held in memory only".
  - api-08: the offline run starts with /auth/refresh, i.e. a page load.
- `retry()` returns silently when there is no outbox row (engine.ts:771-778). `needsAttention` gives such an entry `op: null`.
- For an op the phone does still hold, "Send it again" re-sends the same opId by design (docs/27 §4 line 71). `SyncService.upload` then replays the stored refusal (sync.service.ts:93-106). So in the held case the button can never succeed either; that part is a protocol decision (see notes).

Shared cause? No. (1) is a backend mapper bug. (3) is a frontend error-classification bug plus a control-flow gap. (2) and (4) are how those failures surface.

Design conflict the plan glosses over:
- The code already sends photo bytes inline through the outbox when there is no signal (proof.ts:10-13, queue.ts:141-149).
- docs/27 §15 (lines 207-209) instead describes photos uploaded through signed URLs BEFORE the op is enqueued, with the op held as "photo not uploaded yet".
- The contract comment (contracts/src/delivery.ts, the PROOF OF DELIVERY paragraph) allows inline bytes only when `files.uploadUrl` answers inline, citing docs/20 rule 15: "nothing binary passes through a service". The plan cites "rule 3", which is the bounded-work rule.
- The server fix turns the inline path on in every environment, so it needs a founder confirmation and a docs/27 §15 line.

changes.what:
Two changes.

plans.risk:
1. **Lost response after the server committed.** When the record call hits the 20 s deadline after a commit, the fallback queues a second op. The planner said it is refused `conflict`; more likely it is `stale`. `vetoIfStale` runs first (sync.registry.ts:510-532), `deliveries` is a pull table keyed on id, and the op carries `baseUpdatedAt`; the conflict at `STOP_TERMINAL` only fires if the online record left `deliveries.updated_at` unchanged. No double delivery either way, but the tray shows a refusal the driver throws away.
2. **Classifier breadth (new).** Any Error whose message starts with 'fetch failed' becomes `network` on every platform and app.
   - That is correct for Expo's connection, TLS, DNS and abort failures, and it changes native behaviour app-wide.
   - The engine now marks itself unreachable after a failed call on phones, so screens that branch on `status.online` flip to their offline mode whenever the API is unreachable: delivery collect, van-sale, day and expenses; sales orders/new, shops/[id], me/drafts and local.ts; warehouse pick/[id].
   - This is the honest behaviour DOS-068 asks for, but those screens need the regression pass in verify.
3. **Binary through a service.** On the no-answer path, photo bytes (≤ 700 KB each) now really travel through `/sync/upload`. That contradicts docs/20 rule 15 and docs/27 §15 unless the founder confirms the exception.
   - The body limit is 26 MB (service/bootstrap.ts:55). A backlog whose batch exceeds it gets a 413, which the api-client classifies `business`. `flushInternal` releases the batch and backs off, so it retries without end.
   - The planner's 50-op batch figure was not verified here.
4. **The PUT has no deadline.** `platformFiles.upload` has no deadline on either platform. In a dead spot that accepts TCP and never answers, the fallback waits for the OS socket timeout, not 20 s. Not changed, because a fix would change the `@dos/ui/platform` signature.
5. **Web reload.** A reload on web, where the store is memory-only, before reconnecting still loses a queued write. That is the existing honest limit.
6. **Refusals from before the fix stay refused.** "Send it again" on a held op replays the stored outcome from `sync_ops`, so those deliveries must be recorded again (in dos_qa: TRIP-ACTIVE stop 8).
7. **Blast radius.** Backend: one mapper and one message format in the delivery sync handlers. Frontend: one classifier branch in api-client, the D4 commit path and one tray condition.
plans.reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED
1. **Android root cause corrected, and the fix extended to `@dos/api-client`.**
   - On native the global fetch is expo/fetch: expo/src/winter/runtime.native.ts:41-52, SDK 57.0.20; no `EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_RN_FETCH` anywhere in frontend.
   - It rejects with `FetchError` ('fetch failed: …', name 'Error'; FetchErrors.ts, fetch.ts:78/88-93). `toApiError` (errors.ts:130-161) maps that to 'unknown'.
   - DOS-068's a-39 shows "· unknown", which is `failed.error.kind` rendered by delivery-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:179.
   - Consequence: the planner's `noSignal = kind === 'network'` never fires on Android or iOS, and the delivery would still be lost there. I added the classifier fix and its DOS-056 test.
2. **Why `online` stays true on native, corrected.**
   - The cause is not `setNetworkHint(true)`: native has no hint wiring at all (react.tsx:118-139 needs `globalThis.addEventListener`; delivery-app never calls it).
   - The cause is `isNetworkFailure` (engine.ts:1137-1149) not recognising `ApiError{kind:'unknown'}`, so `call()` never sets `reachable=false`.
   - The Android `d4-error` text was "Something could not be completed. Try again.", not errors.ts:77.
3. **`save()` reuses the objectKey.** When the PUT already landed, the queued op carries the `objectKey` instead of re-sending bytes. This follows docs/20 rule 15 and avoids an orphan pending `file_objects` row.
4. **`parsed()` keeps field paths.** The refine sentence stays exact, but non-custom issues keep their path, so a type error still names the field.
5. **Test 1 made concrete and closer to the device.**
   - Uses the planned delivery id from `trips.get` and sends `baseUpdatedAt`, which exercises the stale veto the real phone hits.
   - Confirmed: tag a3 is unused; retailerA is POST_FULFILLMENT by default; trips 1 and 2 are settled / settled_with_variance before the last test; depart needs no load sheet (trip 2).
6. **Verification fixed.**
   - Web step 5 relied on the old refusal, which only mirrors to device 01a0952a-33e7-76de-83e8-bb6650c9cf2c; replaced with a two-tab plus reload sequence.
   - The dead-spot block must exclude `/sync/*`.
   - Android must keep `adb reverse tcp:8081`, and now has an offline-branch and a fallback-branch variant.
   - DB geo expectation: TRIP-NEXT stop 1 has `arrived_lat` NULL, so geo = 0 there.
7. **Added `ios` to platforms**: same code, same expo/fetch. Not headless-testable.
8. **Risk 1 corrected** from `conflict` to likely `stale` (`vetoIfStale` runs first).
9. **Citation fixed**: docs/20 rule 15, not rule 3.
10. **docs/27 §15 edit added**, conditional on the founder.

CONFIRMED FROM CODE, DB AND EVIDENCE
- `podFromDevice` drops `inline` (delivery.sync.ts:218-228). The refine sentence is at contracts delivery.ts:576-593.
- dos_qa `sync_errors` row: op 01a0955f…, row_invalid, unresolved.
- Stop 8 and TRIP-NEXT stop 1 are both arrived with outcome NULL, 0 pods, POST_FULFILLMENT.
- a-42d shows "Record the delivery" with a green dot.
- d-50 shows Waiting 0 / Refused 1 / "Held in memory only", and api-08 shows a page load (/auth/refresh) before the offline run.
- `retry()` returns silently with no row (engine.ts:771-778).
- `sync_ops` replays a stored rejection (sync.service.ts:93-106), as docs/27 §4 line 71 intends.
- Only delivery.sync.ts emits Zod JSON.
- CI's frontend job runs no tests.

COULD NOT CONFIRM (read-only; emulator not driven)
- The exact runtime message of the Android failure. The diagnosis rests on Expo source plus DOS-068's 'unknown' plus a-42d.
- Whether online `deliveries.record` bumps `deliveries.updated_at` (stale vs conflict).
- The engine's default upload batch size.
- That vitest starts cleanly inside an Expo app package; no app has done it.

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE MERGE (founder)
- The offline inline-photo path contradicts docs/27 §15 (signed URL before enqueue; op held "photo not uploaded yet"), the contract comment and docs/20 rule 15.
- The client already chose it (proof.ts:10-13, queue.ts:141-149); the server fix turns it on in every environment.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS

plans.rootCause:
PAIRING: confirmed, partly. The two findings share one cause for Open and Print and for the broken WhatsApp text. DOS-057 also has three causes that DOS-099 does not share.

SHARED CAUSE (DOS-057 steps 2, 4, 5 and all of DOS-099)
1. The local storage driver signs URLs relative to the service, on purpose.
   - backend/libs/core/src/platform/object-storage.ts:17-20 documents it.
   - :322 sets `base = OBJECT_STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL ?? ''`.
   - :338 returns `${base}/storage/${path}?expires=…&signature=…`.
2. documentRender() (platform/documents.ts:80-111) passes that URL through unchanged. files.readUrl does the same (files.service.ts:187).
3. The frontend rule is to call absoluteUrl() before using such a URL.
   - It is written in frontend/libs/app-template/src/config.ts:35-45.
   - The same function is in the owner, manager, sales, warehouse, delivery and retailer apps' src/config.ts (checked with diff).
4. Every other place that opens a document already follows the rule:
   - owner-app billing/index.tsx:184, reports/exports.tsx:83, src/lib/ui.tsx:454
   - manager-app billing/index.tsx:221, money/index.tsx:274, fulfilment/load-out.tsx:348, registers/tally.tsx:121, src/lib/ui.tsx:500
   - warehouse-app pack/[orderId].tsx:126, load/[id].tsx:103
   - delivery-app src/lib/proof.ts:111
5. Three screens skip it (confirmed with grep; there are no other offenders):
   - retailer-app/app/bills/[id].tsx:78 passes `pdf.data?.url` to documents.open (:154) and documents.print (:163).
   - retailer-app/app/receipts.tsx:59 passes `document.data?.url` to documents.open (:143).
   - delivery-app/app/share/[invoiceId].tsx:74 uses `pdf.data?.url` for open (:79), print (:83) and the share url (:91).
6. What each platform does with the relative URL:
   - Web: documents.web.ts:13 calls window.open(relative), which resolves against the Metro origin. Evidence: api-05-share-buttons.txt shows the popup at http://localhost:5177/storage/….
   - Android: documents.native.ts:22 calls File.downloadFileAsync(relative) and fails with "URI is not absolute" (a-26-open-logcat.txt, 16:33:50).
   - WhatsApp: share.native.ts:11 joins the message and the path into plain text.

WHAT I CHECKED AND DID NOT FIND
There is no second server-side cause.
- CORS is registered for every route, /storage included (bootstrap.ts:45 `app.enableCors(corsOptions(env))`, options at :81-104).
- StorageController GET serves `content-type` and `content-disposition: inline`, and answers 403 once the link expires (storage.controller.ts:40-66).
- Permissions let delivery and retailer read the papers: receivables.receipts.document is MONEY_READERS, permissions.ts:113-119 and :539. billing.creditNotes.get (:589) and files.readUrl (:400) are ANY_MEMBER.
- files.service mayRead (:195-229) calls documentVisible (:232-246), which checks the credit_note or receipt row under RLS.
- delivery-service mounts Receivables, Billing and Files and lists their contract keys (definitions.ts:265-316).
- The render-at-issue pattern works. In dos_qa, CN/9003's render row was written at 16:09:00.560 and the note was issued at 16:09:00.667 (credit-notes.service.ts:443). Invoices show the same pattern at invoices.service.ts:1608.
- The seeded OPEN/… invoices and the seeded credit notes have no PDF because the seed wrote them directly. That is not a code defect.

Why the finding's suggested server-side absolute URL is wrong here:
- The service cannot know which origin the device used to reach it: adb reverse to 127.0.0.1, a LAN IP, or the all-in-one path prefix.
- The S3 driver already returns absolute URLs.
- The app-side absoluteUrl() is the documented rule.

CAUSES THAT BELONG TO DOS-057 ONLY
(b) Recording a receipt never queues its PDF.
   - platform/documents.ts:148-151 and worker/src/jobs/pdf-render.ts:17-22 both say receipts are queued "at issue". docs/23 line 651 says the same.
   - ReceivablesService.recordReceipt (receivables.service.ts:584-697) never calls requestDocumentRender. The insert is at :601, the replay early-return at :591 and the ReceiptRecorded emitEvent at :672-679.
   - Only the on-demand receiptDocument (:760-775) queues a render.
   - recordReceipt is the one core used by all three receipt paths: the desk (createReceipt, :705), the doorstep and van-sale collections (delivery/collections.service.ts:124,127) and offline replay (receivables.sync.ts:60).
   - The other insert, the reversal mirror row (:1697), has no paper.
   - dos_qa data: 1 of 1177 receipts has pdf_object_key. That one is RCPT-0687; its render row is `receipt:700d45c2…:a5:original` at 18:59, queued because R13 asked for it. RCPT-0698 and RCPT-0699 (ganesh.more, 16:05 and 16:29) have no key and no render row.
(c) D9 never offers the receipt or credit-note paper.
   - share/[invoiceId].tsx:169-176 (credit-note rows) and :191-198 (receipt rows) have no onPress, so they render inert (d-27, d-28 evidence).
   - InvoiceCreditNoteRefSchema (contracts/billing.ts:241-248) carries no pdfObjectKey. The documented path is CreditNote.pdfObjectKey (billing.ts:335-336) followed by files.readUrl.

plans.risk:
1. Web Share with files needs recent user activation. The amended share() probes canShare synchronously first, so desk browsers never await before opening the tab. When sharing is supported, the PDF fetch still sits between the tap and navigator.share. On a slow network Safari can throw NotAllowedError; that path falls back to openTab, which may itself be popup-blocked after the await. The result is honest (false, "Nothing was sent") but shows nothing.
2. Every receipt now writes one outbox row and one A5 PDF of about 20 KB, the same load invoices and credit notes already carry. renderPending drains 100 rows per minute globally, oldest first (pdf-render.ts:84-115), plus the outbox relay path. It also stops the batch on any error other than DocumentNotFound. That head-of-line behaviour is pre-existing, but receipts are the most frequent document, so one failing row now delays more papers.
3. Existing receivables.spec.ts:1184 asserts `pdfObjectKey` is null on an older receipt. If a dev worker runs against the same database as the specs (backend/.env → dos), it may render the new A5 row first, and that assertion becomes racy. billing.spec.ts:1048 already carries the same race for invoices. Do not change the assertion; run specs with no worker attached to the spec database.
4. Credit notes have no on-demand render procedure (billing.ts:848 has only invoices.pdf). A credit note whose render was never queued (the seeded ones: 131 of 132 in dos_qa) shows "still making this PDF" on D9 indefinitely. In the product flow the render is queued at issue (credit-notes.service.ts:443).
5. In production on S3, the web share fetch needs bucket CORS that allows the app origins. Without it the fetch fails and share falls back to the tab. This is a deployment note for docs/26, not code.
6. The guard reads source text at file level. A file with one correctly absolutised `url` and a second, raw `url` in another scope would pass. The root turbo `test` task hashes only @dos/ui's own files (frontend/turbo.json `test: {}`), so a cached pass can hide an app regression locally; CI on a clean runner is unaffected.
7. Web Print stays a new-tab fallback for a cross-origin PDF, by design.
8. absoluteUrl ignores API_PREFIX in the all-in-one deployment. This is pre-existing and shared by the twelve compliant call sites.
9. Links opened on web and text shares still expire after 15 minutes. Only file shares (phone, and browsers that share files) survive to the evening.
10. The 1177 seeded receipts get no PDF after the fact. They render on first request.

WHAT I CHANGED

When file sharing is unsupported (every desk Chrome), open the tab inside the tap with no fetch. The original fetched first, then opened the tab after an await, which popup blockers can refuse. An AbortError (sheet dismissed) now returns false without opening a tab. Added a third web test for that case and reworded the second ("without fetching").
2. Core spec: before the replay, the test marks the first render row published. Without that, requestRender's unpublished-row dedupe (documents.ts:171-184) would hide a replay that re-queued, so "a replay queues nothing more" could pass for the wrong reason.
3. Added a second backend test, DOS-057 in delivery.spec.ts, through POST /delivery/collections. That is the path that produced RCPT-0698 and RCPT-0699. recordReceipt is shared today; the test pins it.

The backend SQL check now compares queued_at with the receipt's created_at to prove the same transaction, and falls back to pdf_object_key when published rows are pruned.
