plans.title: A return marked Damaged or Past its date must go to the damaged bin: one reason control in D4, and the server refuses returnedSaleable:true with reason damaged|expired
plans.rootCause:
Confirmed by reading the code. Two defects add up to the bug: the screen can send two answers that contradict each other, and the server never checks that they agree.

1. APP. frontend/delivery-app/app/stop/[id]/deliver.tsx has two independent chip rows.
   - :550-562 is the disposition row (`d4-saleable-*`). Its value is `entry.returnedSaleable`, which defaults to true (initial entry :147-153, `set()` fallback :504).
   - :564-573 is the reason row (`LINE_REASONS.slice(0,3)` = refused/damaged/expired). Its onChange at :572 is only `set({ reason })`, so tapping "Damaged" or "Past its date" leaves `returnedSaleable: true`.
   - Choosing "Can be sold again" at :558-561 keeps an earlier 'damaged' reason.
   - `setAll('none')` (:266-267) keeps the old `returnedSaleable` while defaulting the reason.
   - The payload at :353, and the outbox op at src/lib/queue.ts:178, send exactly what QA/evidence/phase1/delivery/api-04-partial-delivery-stop5.txt shows: `returnedSaleable:true, reason:"damaged"`.
   - docs/23 §5.1 only asks for "per-line qty and reason on partial", so a single control matches the screen inventory.

2. CONTRACT. backend/libs/contracts/src/delivery.ts:913-920 (`DeliveryLineInput`) declares `returnedSaleable: z.boolean().default(true)` and `reason: DeliveryLineReasonSchema.optional()` as unrelated fields.

3. SERVER. backend/libs/core/src/modules/delivery/deliveries.service.ts `checkLines` (:312-367) checks three things: the line belongs to the bill, it is not listed twice, and delivered+returned=billed (:338-343). Nothing checks the reason against the disposition. It runs at :127, before `assertPodPolicy` (:129) and before any write (:132). From there:
   - The credit-note header reason depends only on `returnedSaleable` (:185-190).
   - `saleable: l.returnedSaleable` goes to `CreditNotesService.raiseForDelivery` (:191-205), with `restockLocationId` = the vehicle.
   - billing/credit-notes.service.ts `restock()` (:452-490) posts saleable lines as `sale_return_saleable` into that location.
   - The offline path is the same: delivery.sync.ts:132 (`returned_saleable ?? true`) → `recordInTx` (:138) → `checkLines`.
   - A 4xx ORPCError thrown there becomes a readable 2xx sync rejection (sync.service.ts:137-146).

4. KNOCK-ON. claims/build.service.ts:481 only takes credit-note lines whose HEADER reason is `return_damaged`, so this case never reaches the damage claim.

WHERE EXPIRED GOODS BELONG. The bin is created by tenant-bootstrap.ts:200 as 'Damaged / expiry bin' (kind damaged), and docs/plans/delivery.md:43/:84 routes non-saleable returns to the `damaged` location.

plans.title: Money NumberPad enters rupees (paise only after "."), matching the web RupeeInput, on every native money field
plans.rootCause:
Confirmed by reading the code. The defect is only in the shared kit's NumberPad money mode. Nothing on the server, the offline path or any single screen contributes.

1. The native pad appends every tap as a paise digit. In frontend/libs/ui/src/native/money.tsx:
   - :127 the key list (1-9, clear, 0, back) has no '.' key.
   - :143 builds `digits` from the integer paise value.
   - :151-153 appends the tapped digit and calls `onChange(Number(next))`. So 4-7-5-6 emits 4756 paise.
   - :189 previews `formatMoney(value ?? 0)`, which prints ₹47.56 (QA/evidence/phase1/delivery/android/a-18-keypad-4756.png exists).
   - Money and count modes share this one reducer.
   - The header comment at :4-5 states the rule outright: "The pad appends DIGITS (1 2 3 4 -> ₹12.34)".

2. Every native money field goes through it. Native `RupeeInput` opens `<NumberPad mode="money" value={value} onChange={onChange}>` whenever `theme.density === 'field'` (:302-312, :350-368).
   - buildTheme (frontend/libs/ui/src/theme.tsx, the declaredDensity/density lines) makes a phone viewport field density even for the desk apps.
   - delivery and retailer are declared field in src/config.ts:22.
   - Native consumers: delivery `app/stop/[id]/collect.tsx:289` (this finding), `app/trip/start.tsx:263`, `app/expenses.tsx:251`; retailer `app/pay.tsx:133`, `app/order.tsx:565`; owner, manager and admin RupeeInputs on a phone.
   - The sales app has no RupeeInput.
   - Its other money entries are rupee text fields, e.g. sales-app/app/orders/new.tsx:663. Those have no paise-append defect.

3. Web already takes rupees, so the platforms disagree. Web `RupeeInput` (web/money.tsx:198-218) is a text input parsed by `parseRupees` (money.ts:63-74). "7856" becomes 785600, as api-02-record-cash-collection.txt shows.

4. The web NumberPad has the same reducer: web/money.tsx:264 (keys), :286-296 (press), :325 (preview). No app renders it in money mode. The manager gate and 7 warehouse pads all pass `mode="count"`, and the gallery uses count too. It must still match its native twin.

5. The paise-append rule was written into the kit's own docs, against the design spec:
   - types.ts:119-122: "in `money` mode `1 2 3 4` is 1234 paise"
   - frontend/libs/ui/README.md:118-119
   - The spec, docs/design/UX-00-design-system.md:346-349, says the field "accepts `1234`, `1,234`, `1234.5` → emits paise", which is rupee-first.
   - UX-01 D6 (UX-01-field-reality.md:198) only requires a number pad with the expected amount above it.
   - No founder decision in docs/22, docs/15, docs/17 or docs/18 records paise-first entry. The fix re-decides nothing.

6. There is no second cause. The trace:
   - collect.tsx:289-299 passes `onChange={setAmountPaise}`.
   - The online path sends `amountPaise` to `delivery.collections.record`, which validates it with `PaiseSchema.positive()` (backend/libs/contracts/src/delivery.ts:990 etc.; common.ts:7 `z.number().int().safe()`).
   - The offline path (delivery-app/src/lib/queue.ts:213,253) writes `amount_paise: input.amountPaise` unchanged.
   - The server stores exactly what the pad emitted.

7. dos_qa confirms it (SELECT only):
   - RCPT-0699 is upi, 475600, on TRIP-ACTIVE, Nakshatra Kirana (stop 7, planned_collection_paise 475600). It is the QA workaround of typing 475600.
   - 9 of 1503 invoices and 48 of 1177 receipts carry non-zero paise, so the pad must still reach paise. Hence the finding's main suggestion: rupees by default, paise after an explicit '.'.

changes.what:
Add pure pad helpers that both renderers call. This is the pattern qty.ts uses for `stepByCase`/`qtyState`. They are exported through shared.ts's existing `export * from './money.js'`.

Keys:
- `export const MONEY_PAD_KEYS = ['1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8','9','.','0','back'] as const` and `export type MoneyPadKey = (typeof MONEY_PAD_KEYS)[number] | 'clear'`.

Converting between entry and paise:
- `padEntryFromPaise(value: number | null): string`:
  - null gives ''.
  - Otherwise use the absolute value, the same `Math.abs` today's pad applies (there is no minus key).
  - Whole rupees give `String(abs / 100)` ('4756'); anything else gives `toEditableRupees(abs)` ('35843.12').
- `paiseFromPadEntry(entry: string): number | null`: through the existing `parseRupees`, which accepts '12.', never uses a float and returns null for empty.

Key presses:
- `pressMoneyPadKey(entry, key): string`:
  - 'clear' gives ''.
  - 'back' drops the last character.
  - '.' is ignored if the entry already has one; on an empty entry it gives '0.'.
  - A digit is ignored once two decimals are typed, or once the integer part has 10 digits. That is ₹99,99,99,999.99, the same ceiling as today's 12-digit paise cap.
  - A lone leading '0' is replaced ('0' then '5' gives '5').

Keeping the preview honest:
- `reconcilePadEntry(entry, value): string` returns `paiseFromPadEntry(entry) === value ? entry : padEntryFromPaise(value)`.
- It is the one place that decides what the pad shows. A pending '4756.' survives the parent storing 475600. When the parent overrides the value (retailer pay.tsx `amount ?? owed`, trip/start.tsx `cashPaise ?? detail.openingCashPaise`), the pad shows the parent's value, exactly as today's fully controlled pad does. The preview can never disagree with the value that will be committed.

Preview text:
- `formatPadEntry(entry): string` shows the amount exactly as typed, with ₹ and Indian grouping of the integer part via `formatMoney(Number(int) * 100).slice(0, -3)`.
- '' is '₹0', '4756' is '₹4,756', '4756.' is '₹4,756.', '4756.5' is '₹4,756.5'.

NumberPad (:127-241).

Count mode stays byte-identical in behaviour: `KEYS`, `digits`, the append `press`, the `String(value ?? 0)` preview and the full-width Done. It serves the warehouse gate, pick, pack, load, check-in and cycle-count pads, and the manager gate.

Money mode:
- Render `MONEY_PAD_KEYS` in the same four rows of three.
- `const [entry, setEntry] = useState(() => padEntryFromPaise(value))`.
- `const current = reconcilePadEntry(entry, value)` is derived during render. Do NOT add a `useEffect` re-seed:
  - An effect on `[value]` never fires when a parent falls back to the same number. Clear on retailer Pay would then preview ₹0 while the value is still the owed amount.
  - An effect that reads `entry` needs `entry` in its deps.
  - The derived form has neither problem.
- A tap runs `const next = pressMoneyPadKey(current, key); setEntry(next); onChange(paiseFromPadEntry(next))`.
- The preview at :189 shows `formatPadEntry(current)` with `accessibilityLabel={speakMoney(paiseFromPadEntry(current) ?? 0, theme.t)}` (native Txt already takes accessibilityLabel, base.tsx:40).
- Clear leaves the grid. WHAT I CHANGED

1. Verification target: stop 8 instead of stop 7.
   - Stop 7 is `delivered` and already carries RCPT-0699 (upi, 475600, TRIP-ACTIVE).
   - Recording ₹4,756 there again would book an unwanted second receipt against settled dues.
   - Stop 8 Laxmi Narayan Stores is `arrived` with planned ₹22,508 (2250800). The DB query now filters by trip and sequence 8 and expects 2250800.
   - The web parity and iOS steps no longer record anything.
   - Tool invocations are corrected: `android-login.sh <app> <port> <user> <TitleWord>`; iOS is `ios-login.mjs` plus Appium (there is no `ios-*.sh` login); the ⌫ key is matched with `ui.py text back`.

2. Re-seed design: the plan's `useEffect` on `value` is replaced with a render-time `reconcilePadEntry(entry, value)`.
   - An effect keyed on `[value]` never fires when a parent falls back to the same number. On retailer pay.tsx (`value={amount ?? owed}`), Clear would preview ₹0 while the committed value stays the owed amount: the pad would show a figure that is not what gets recorded.
   - An effect that reads `entry` would need `entry` in its deps.
   - The derived form keeps a pending '4756.', matches today's snap-back exactly (which makes the plan's own "same as today" note true), needs no effect, and is unit-testable. A new test covers it.

3. New test in parity.test.ts. It reads both renderer files, the pattern that file already uses because react-native cannot be imported under vitest. It asserts both NumberPads use the shared helpers. Without it, nothing automated touches the native half, which is where the defect was seen. render.test.tsx is static (renderToStaticMarkup), and no jsdom or testing-library is installed, so a render test cannot press keys.

4. `MONEY_PAD_KEYS` is exported from money.ts so both renderers draw one key list and a test pins it. `padEntryFromPaise` uses the absolute value, matching today's `Math.abs`.

5. The README file-table row for money.ts (:30) is updated too.

6. dependsOn now includes DOS-041, a conditional file overlap. Its suggested fix caps the pick keypad, which is `<NumberPad mode="count">` at warehouse-app/app/pick/[id].tsx:270. If that plan adds a `max` prop in the kit, it collides with this change in types.ts, both money.tsx files, the README and render.test.tsx. Land DOS-060 first and rebase DOS-041 onto the split money/count branches. I could not see the DOS-041 plan.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
- Every cited line is correct: native money.tsx :127, :143-154, :189, :302-312, :350-368; web money.tsx :264, :286-296, :325; types.ts :119-122; README :118-119; UX-00 :346-349.

WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM (read-only)

- I did not verify that Appium can tap the pad keys by label on iOS.
- I assumed RN `Modal` unmounts its children when hidden, which re-seeds `entry` on each open. The render-time reconcile makes this matter less.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS
- The preview while editing ('₹4,756', no '.00') is a calculator convention UX-00 does not spell out. It is low risk; the field shows ₹4,756.00 after Done.
- Pre-existing and out of scope, but it should be logged as a new QA finding rather than left in notes. pay.tsx `amount ?? owed` and trip/start.tsx `cashPaise ?? openingCashPaise` make Clear snap back. A phone retailer can then only type amounts sharing the owed amount's leading digits, or pick bills. Today's pad has the same limit; this fix neither causes nor cures it.

plans.rootCause:
One cause: how the delivery app picks a trip and routes to it on the phone. The backend accepts expenses and GPS points on any active trip of the crew and takes the trip id the app sends, so the server is not a second cause. The phone already holds the right rows.

1. WRONG TRIP. `frontend/delivery-app/src/lib/local.ts:235-241` `pickCurrentTrip()` ranks by `OPEN_STATES.indexOf(state)`.
   - The constant at :208 is `['active', 'loading', 'planned', 'closing']`, so the rank is active 0, loading 1, planned 2, closing 3.
   - The doc comment at :210-218 says "active first, then closing, then loading or planned". It has disagreed with the code since commit 2f8a5a5. The code is what shipped and what the gates walked.
   - Within one state the tie-break `(a.trip_date < b.trip_date ? 1 : -1)` (:238) sorts trip_date DESC, never looks at today, and never returns 0, so it is not a valid comparator.
   - dos_qa (SELECT, IST today 2026-09-12), both trips of ganesh.more are `active`:
     - TRIP-ACTIVE dda35990…: dated 12 Sep; stops 7 delivered, 1 partial, 1 failed, 1 arrived, so 9/10.
     - TRIP-NEXT 72649337…: dated 14 Sep, departed 12 Sep 15:08; 4 pending and 1 arrived, so 0/5.
     - DESC therefore returns TRIP-NEXT.
   - Every trip-bound screen uses this pick:
     - D1 `app/index.tsx:74`
     - D7 `app/expenses.tsx:58`, sent as `tripId` at :91. The ₹500 diesel (50000 paise, 16:15:49 IST) is on TRIP-NEXT.
     - D8 without a param, `app/day.tsx:78-82`
     - D2 without a param, `app/trip/start.tsx:64`
     - The GPS tracker, `app/_layout.tsx:332-343` (posts only while the pick is `active`).
   - No other screen picks a trip: the stop and van-sale screens take the trip from the stop.

2. DEAD END. Every row under "Your other trips" (`app/index.tsx:431-441`) pushes `/trip/start?tripId=…` (:439), whatever its state.
   - D2 enables depart only for `loading` (`start.tsx:159`). Any other state gets `d2.mustLoadFirst` (`start.tsx:186-187`, `strings.ts:143`), so an active trip lands on a disabled button with a false reason.
   - D2 also still shows the odometer and float form (`start.tsx:252-277`), which can never be sent for that trip.
   - D8 is the existing "open that trip" pattern: D11 rows push `/day?tripId=` (`app/trips.tsx:135-137`). The same D2 dead end is reachable from Me → "Agree" (`settings.tsx:167`, no tripId). That button renders only while consent is not granted.

3. "ON BOARD" FOR A SHEET THAT IS NOT LOADED. `app/index.tsx:340-344` prints `pl(t, 'd1.packages', expected_packages)` ("{count} cartons on board", `strings.ts:103-104`) for every sheet.
   - The panel heading is `d1.load` "Load on board" (`index.tsx:308`, `strings.ts:98`), whatever the sheets' status.
   - `load_sheet_status` is `draft | confirmed | cancelled` (`backend/libs/database/src/schema/warehouse.ts:54-55`, `backend/libs/contracts/src/warehouse.ts:103`). Draft means "built but nothing has moved".
   - The D1 query (`index.tsx:83-94`) reads sheets of every status. So a draft sheet, and also a cancelled one, is called "on board".
   - dos_qa: TRIP-NEXT's sheet is draft, 38 packages, no challan, `confirmed_at` NULL. TRIP-ACTIVE's sheet is DC-0081, confirmed 11 Sep 12:15 IST, 64 packages.

4. OFFLINE follows from 1 and 2; the data is already on the phone.
   - Delivery-role pulls: `trips` are the crew's trips created in the last 14 days, any state (`backend/libs/core/src/modules/delivery/delivery.module.ts:84-94`). `load_sheets` cover 30 days (`backend/libs/core/src/modules/warehouse/warehouse.module.ts:51-69`).
   - Both trips were created 11-12 Sep, and D1 already draws TRIP-ACTIVE from SQLite under "Your other trips".
   - The real trip is simply not the home, and its row leads to a screen that needs the network. No sync, contract or schema change is needed.

plans.title: Receipt numbers can repeat: add a unique receipt number per series and FY (keyed the same way as the counter), turn a collision into a 409 or a sync rejection, and fix the seed's lagging RCPT counter
plans.rootCause:
CONFIRMED. Both ids have one root cause. DOS-032 is the desk path (manager and accountant, POST /receipts). DOS-059 is the field path. The finding's own steps went through the ONLINE POST /delivery/collections (delivery-app app/stop/[id]/collect.tsx:109-139 calls delivery.collections.record; the response carries receipt.receiptNo). The offline /sync/upload path has the same defect. Two parts combine.

1. PRODUCT: nothing enforces a unique receipt number.
- `receipts` has only the pkey, `receipts_idempotency_idx` and `receipts_device_client_no_idx` (schema/receivables.ts:206-220; pg_indexes on dos_qa confirms).
- Invoices and credit notes carry `series_code` + `fy` plus a unique index (billing.ts:115-117; billing.ts:222-224 and 254-256).
- `nextDocumentNumber` (platform/numbering.ts:27-52) returns whatever the counter holds.
- Both insert sites write that number unchecked: `recordReceipt` (receivables.service.ts:596, insert at 601-621) and `undoReceipt` (:1696, insert at 1697-1712).
- Callers that inherit this: createReceipt; delivery `collectInTx` (collections.service.ts:127/130), which van sales also use; and the offline handler (receivables.sync.ts:60).
- The finding's index cannot be built as written: receipts has no series_code or fy column.
- An index on (tenant_id, receipt_no) alone would be wrong. The counter is keyed per tenant+series+FY and a new FY row starts at 1 (numbering.ts:33-45). The RCPT prefix has no FY (tenant-bootstrap.ts:65). So every tenant's RCPT-0001 would be refused on 1 April.
- A raw 23505 is also the wrong failure on the device path. sync.service.ts:147 rethrows anything that is not a 4xx ORPCError as a 5xx, so the device retries the whole batch forever. Only a 4xx ORPCError becomes a 2xx rejection (:138-146).

2. FIXTURE: the seed leaves the RCPT counter behind the receipts it wrote.
- The renumber pass (seed-demo/sales.ts:2912-2929) numbers every non-reversal row 1..N. That includes the part-payment residual receipts pushed at :2534, which never do `receiptSeq += 1` (only :2430 and :2640 do).
- RESIDUAL_MODES has exactly 4 entries (sales.ts:1893-1898), yet the counter is bumped to `receiptSeq + 1` (:3037). So it lags by 4 in every tenant.
- dos_qa matches: tarsun counter was 696 with RCPT-0699 seeded; kalyan-agencies 102 with 0105; sai-distributors 277 with 0280.
- Separately, seedBilling writes RCPT-9001..9004 (billing.ts:296). Its step 9 reconciles only INV and CN (:1252-1255; reconcileSeries :1423-1434 knows only those two tables).
- Seed order is sales (index.ts:268), then billing (:275), then receivables (:286). Both bumpSeries helpers use GREATEST.

No second product cause:
- The apps only display the server's number.
- The worker never inserts receipts.
- Receipts has two triggers: `receipts_touch_updated_at` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE) and `receipts_tombstone` (AFTER DELETE). Neither checks numbers.
- RLS plays no part.

One latent cause the fix must not turn into an outage. numbering.ts:3/33 takes the FY from @dos/db `financialYear`, which uses process-local getMonth (tenant-bootstrap.ts:20-24). @dos/domain `financialYear` is IST (calendar.ts:31-35). Stamping the new `fy` column with the domain function, as the original plan did, can file a number under a different FY than the counter that issued it (see changes).

DB facts (dos_qa, read-only):
- tarsun has 4 duplicate pairs: RCPT-0696 (desk), RCPT-0697 (accountant), RCPT-0698 (ganesh.more collection), RCPT-0699 (UPI).
- Current RCPT counters: tarsun 700, kalyan-agencies 102, sai-distributors 277. All three tenants hold RCPT-9001..9004.
- There are no null receipt_no values.
- Other seeded shapes (RCPT-OA-, -CHQ-, -FLD-, -VAN-, -ERR-, -NNNN-R) are unique and cannot be produced by the counter.
- A spec tenant (a-0bb6e38a, RCPT-0bb6e38a-1/-2/-D) shows rls.test.ts was once run against dos_qa. Those rows are distinct, so they do not trip the duplicate check.

1. BACKEND DEPOSIT AND BOUNCE EXIST AND ARE PERMITTED (checked)

- The unfiltered receipts.list({status:'collected'}) (:85-87) lists UPI (posted to UPI, receivables.service.ts:272-273), bank transfer (posted to BANK, :274-275), adjustment, and 2 legacy rows with mode 'credit_note', which is outside ReceiptModeSchema (receivables.ts:71-72).

- Excluding UPI and bank transfer is right.

plans.title: Retailer statement reads only the first page (50) of the ledger and prints the whole-window closing balance under it
plans.rootCause:
The planner's diagnosis holds: the bug is in the retailer screen. The backend is correct for the retailer path, and the reviewer found no second cause.

**1. The screen reads one page.**
- frontend/retailer-app/app/statement.tsx:37-46 makes a single call, `api.api.receivables.ledger.get({ retailerId, from, to })`, with no `limit` and no `cursor`.
- So the contract default of 50 applies (backend/libs/contracts/src/receivables.ts:63-66, `CursorInput.limit ... max(200).default(50)`).
- statement.tsx:47 renders that one page. :71 prints `openingPaise`. :146 prints `closingPaise` without checking `nextCursor` (RetailerLedgerOutput, receivables.ts:620-625).

**2. The backend pages correctly.** `retailerLedger` is at backend/libs/core/src/modules/receivables/receivables.queries.ts:328-387.
- Keyset on `(d::text, ref_id)` (:350), ordered `d asc, ref_id asc limit n+1` (:352-356).
- `priorResult` carries the running balance into later pages (:358-362).
- `closingPaise` sums the whole window, `d <= to` (:379-384). `nextCursor` is set only when a row exists past the page (:386).
- The service caps the window at 400 days (receivables.service.ts:182, :1140-1147). The app's longest range, 'fy', is at most 366 days (frontend/retailer-app/src/lib/dates.ts rangeOf).

**3. No second cause.** Checked by the reviewer:
- **Unique keys on the retailer's path.** The retailer uses the document path (`documentLedgerSource`, queries.ts:410-440). Its `ref_id` is the row id of an invoice, credit note or receipt. A write-off names exactly one `invoiceId` (contracts receivables.ts:653-659), so each `write_off_id` has one allocation; dos_qa holds 7 allocations for 7 write-offs. A receipt reversal is its own contra receipts row with its own id (receivables.spec.ts:618-647). No `(d, ref_id)` ties exist, so following the cursor cannot skip a row.
- **No other layer involved.** No RLS policy or trigger is involved. The statement is an online `useQuery`; there is no `@dos/offline` path.
- **Distributor switch is safe.** QueryCache drops a response from an older generation (frontend/libs/api-client/src/cache.ts:64-68, :145-148), so switching distributor mid-read cannot paint the old tenant's pages.

**4. Data re-checked read-only in dos_qa** (tenant 01a0947d-7a79-75d2-bfff-97e499a58d49, retailer 34191c43-f0bc-70ab-a39d-fcbe8f94ae36, window 2026-06-15..2026-09-12):

| Row | Entry | Running balance (paise) |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | RCPT-0659 | 6,353,500 |
| 51 | RCPT-0668 | 5,135,500 |
| 54 | RCPT-0687 | 3,584,300 (= closingPaise) |

- The shop has no entries before 2026-06-15.
- Evidence QA/evidence/phase1/retailer/net-statement/11-GET-…ledger….json: 50 items, nextCursor "MjAyNi0wOS0xMAAz…", openingPaise 0, closingPaise 3,584,300.

**5. No other screen has this defect.**
- No screen in any app sends a `cursor`.
- The only other ledger caller, manager-app/app/shops/index.tsx:95 (limit 30), renders a 12-row preview (:305). It never prints `closingPaise`, so it does not have this defect.

**The fix.** Follow `nextCursor` to the end inside the bounded window at the contract's maximum page size. Never print the closing figure unless the whole window has been read.

changes.what:
New pure helper: no React, no oRPC import. Types and signature: - `export interface CursorPage { readonly items: readonly unknown[]; readonly nextCursor: string | null }` - `export interface EveryPage

{ first: P; last: P; items: P['items'][number][]; complete: boolean; pages: number }` - `export async function readEveryPage

(fetchPage: (cursor: string | undefined) => Promise

, options: { maxPages: number }): Promise>` Behaviour: - **Required bound (amended).** `maxPages` has no default and must be an integer >= 1, otherwise it throws RangeError. Each caller names its own bound: the statement here, the sellable-stock readers in DOS-074/097. - **Loop.** Calls `fetchPage(undefined)`, then `fetchPage(prev.nextCursor)` one after another, joining items in server order. - **complete=true** when a page returns `nextCursor === null`. - **complete=false** when `maxPages` pages were read and a cursor is still pending, or when the returned cursor equals the one just sent. A cursor that does not advance ends the read instead of looping. - **Failure.** Any rejected page rejects the whole read, with no partial result. QueryCache records the error and `` shows ErrorState. - **Header comment.** Cites DOS-095 and scale rule 3 (docs/20:9). Says the helper is for server-bounded windows only, never for draining an unbounded register.
Export `readEveryPage`, `type CursorPage` and `type EveryPage` from './pages.js', next to the QueryCache exports.

Vitest spec in the style of src/react/reads.test.ts. Written first; it fails before pages.ts exists.

The fake pager is built from 54 synthetic statement rows, each with `refId` and a running `balancePaise`. Every page carries the whole-window `openingPaise` and `closingPaise`, as `retailerLedger` does.

Cases:
1. **Page size 50.** Exactly 2 calls: the first with cursor undefined, the second with page 1's cursor. Returns 54 items in order, `complete === true`, `pages === 2`, `first.openingPaise` kept, and the last item's `balancePaise === last.closingPaise`.
2. **Page size 10, maxPages 5.** 5 calls, 50 items, `complete === false`.
3. **Cursor that does not advance.** The read stops after 2 calls with `complete === false`.
4. **Page 2 rejects.** The promise rejects with that error.
5. **`maxPages: 0`.** Throws RangeError before any call.

Add one line to the documented surface (hand-written README, not generated): `readEveryPage(fetchPage, { maxPages })` follows `nextCursor` inside a window the server already bounds, reports `complete`, and rejects if any page fails. Do not touch the stale test count, which is unrelated.

**Import.** `readEveryPage` from '@dos/api-client'. A runtime root import is already used by retailer-app/src/api.ts:9; frontend/libs/config/eslint/app.js bans only react-native and react-dom.

**Constants.**
- `const STATEMENT_PAGE = 200`: the contract max, receivables.ts:64.
- `const STATEMENT_MAX_PAGES = 5`: 1,000 entries. Amended from the planner's default of 25 x 200 = 5,000; the reason is in reviewNotes.

**Lines 37-46.**
- Key: `['ledger', retailerId, rangeId, 'every']`. The trailing element keeps a fast-refresh cache that holds the old one-page shape from being read as the new shape. Prefix invalidation on ['ledger'] is unchanged, and no other retailer-app key uses 'ledger'.
- Run: `readEveryPage((cursor) => api.api.receivables.ledger.get({ retailerId: retailerId ?? '', from: range.from, to: range.to, limit: STATEMENT_PAGE, ...(cursor === undefined ? {} : { cursor }) }), { maxPages: STATEMENT_MAX_PAGES })`. The spread keeps exactOptionalPropertyTypes happy.

**Rendering.**
- Line 47: `const rows = ledger.data?.items ?? []`.
- Line 71: `ledger.data?.first.openingPaise ?? null`.
- Line 146: `ledger.data?.complete === true ? ledger.data.last.closingPaise : null`. `Money` renders null as an em dash (frontend/libs/ui/src/types.ts:88).
- Inside the r6-closing panel, when `ledger.data?.complete === false`, render `<Txt field="label" desk="meta" color={colors.text.secondary} testID="r6-partial">{t('r6.partial')}</Txt>`.
- The row rendering (Stack map, :86-136) and the row key are unchanged.

**Doc comment, line 7.** Replace 'come with the page' with: every page of the window is read before the closing balance is printed, and a capped read prints no closing figure (DOS-095).

Add after line 261: `'r6.partial': 'This period has more entries than one statement can show. Pick a shorter period.'` The namespace is English-only and `as const` (strings.ts:1-16, :435), with no locale siblings, so this one key is enough. It is shown only on a capped read.

Guard spec placed after 'serves the same closing balance to the desk and to the shop' (:830-845), which reads at limit 100 and never pages.

**Type.** Extend `LedgerReply` (:74-78) with `nextCursor: string | null` and with `refId: string` on items. Both are missing today, and the new spec compares refIds.

**Test.** As shopA on `/receivables/ledger/${shop.a}`, from day(-200) to day(0):
- Read the window once at limit 200.
- Read it again at limit 2, following `nextCursor` until null.
- Assert that the paged refId and balancePaise sequences equal the single read's.
- Assert that the last paged balancePaise === closingPaise.
- Assert that more than one page was fetched.

**Fixture.** shop.a has invoices a1-a3 dated day(-40), day(-25) and day(-10), receipts at :373, :393 and :623, plus a contra reversal row, so limit 2 really pages. All keys are unique on the document path.

This pins the contract the app now relies on. It passes before the fix; it is a guard, not the failing test.

Low. One screen changes, plus a new pure helper and a guard spec. There is no contract, permission or schema change.

- **Bounded reads.** One request per 200 entries, each under its own 20 s deadline (frontend/libs/api-client/src/link.ts:12). At most 5 requests, because STATEMENT_MAX_PAGES is 5. Each page re-runs the opening, prior and closing sums over the shop's document union, so the server cost is about 5 x 4 aggregates at worst.
- **Rendering.** The rows still render in a non-virtualised Stack, which scale rule 17 would not accept for an unbounded list. The 1,000-entry cap limits that to a size the 50-row read never reached. A heavy shop's 'This year' on the Pixel 7 is unmeasured, because dos_qa has at most 58 entries.
- **Capped read.** The screen shows the rows it read, no closing figure, and a sentence asking for a shorter period. It never shows a closing figure over part of a statement.
- **Consistency between pages.** A receipt posted mid-read sorts after the cursor, so it lands on the last page and inside that page's closing. A back-dated document landing between two page reads could make the running balance jump once at a page boundary until the next revalidation. This is negligible and not guarded.
- **Distributor switch mid-read.** The cache drops the old generation's result. At most one extra page request goes out under the new token and is discarded.
- **Cache shape.** The cache is in memory only, and the key gains a trailing 'every', so no old value can be read as the new shape. Prefix invalidation on ['ledger'] still hits it.
- **Other callers untouched.** manager-app/app/shops/index.tsx:95 (12-row preview, no closing figure) does not change.
plans.reviewNotes:
**What I changed**

1. **Page cap: 5,000 entries became 1,000.** `maxPages` is now required, and the statement passes 5 (1,000 entries) instead of the default 25 (5,000).
   - The rows render in a non-virtualised Stack (statement.tsx:86-136).
   - The kit's `<List>` is not a drop-in replacement: the web version clips rows to a fixed `itemHeight` (frontend/libs/ui/src/web/layout.tsx:250-256), and a statement row's height varies.
   - Scale rule 17 (docs/20) requires virtualised lists. 5,000 non-virtualised rows would be a new ANR risk on the Pixel 7 that the 50-row read never had.

plans.rootCause:
The screen is at fault. The server is correct. One cause, three symptoms.

1. The only entry is whole cases.
- frontend/manager-app/app/billing/credit-notes.tsx:384-392 draws every bill line with the order-entry <QtyStepper> and passes caseSize={line.caseSize ?? 1}.
- Its + and − call stepByCase(pieces, ±1, caseSize) (frontend/libs/ui/src/qty.ts:67-70). The "Pieces" button is drawn only when onOpenPieces is passed (web/money.tsx:448-466, native/money.tsx:452-470), and this screen never passes it.
- So Sunbake (case 120, billed 40) can only reach 0, 120, 240 and so on. This is wider than lines under one case: any partial credit that is not a whole-case multiple is impossible, e.g. 5 of Konkan Farsan's 40 pc at case 20. In dos_qa, 1,530 of 6,202 lines on issued, partly paid or paid bills hold less than one case, so nothing on them can be credited at all.
- stepByCase has no maximum, although its JSDoc (qty.ts:66) says "never above a hard cap".
- UX-00 §6.4 defines overAvailable as accepted, not blocked, so nothing stopped the 120-piece POST.

2. Order-entry words on a credit note, on every platform.
- At zero, qtyState returns atZero (qty.ts:87), which prints "Not ordered" (web/money.tsx:468-471, native/money.tsx:474-476, kit strings.ts:44).
- availablePieces is documented as sellable_stock (types.ts:146), but the screen passes billed pieces into it (credit-notes.tsx:388). availableLine floors 40/120 to "0 cs available" (qty.ts:98-105), and overAvailable adds "Only 0 cs available — rest short-supplied" (kit strings.ts:48).
- The line meta at credit-notes.tsx:381-383 prints only qtyPcs, so free goods are invisible, yet the server lets them be credited.

3. The server rule the screen must mirror.
- CreditNotesService.draft() (backend/libs/core/src/modules/billing/credit-notes.service.ts:308-313) computes remaining = qtyPcs + freeQtyPcs − credited.
- creditedByLine (:525-543) sums every note on the bill except cancelled ones, so drafts count.
- Anything above remaining gets BAD_REQUEST "only N pcs of X are left to credit on INV/…", with data {invoiceLineId, remaining, requested}.
- billing.spec.ts:783 (6 pc at the invoiced rate) and :837 (cumulative cap) already prove this path.

4. The refusal is rendered, but out of sight.
- useMutation stores the ApiError (frontend/libs/api-client/src/react/index.tsx, catch block in mutateAsync), and toApiError keeps the server's sentence (errors.ts:135-151).
- credit-notes.tsx:417-421 prints it, but AFTER the Draft button, at the end of the panel.
- On desk the panel is 360 px wide, full height, with overflowY:auto inside a fixed backdrop (web/feedback.tsx:199-214, web/css.ts:109). On phone it is a bottom sheet capped at 80vh.
- QA/evidence/phase1/manager/13e-credit-note-400.png shows the sentence clipped at y≈790-800 below "Draft a credit note", and 13e-credit-note-400.txt ends with it.
- The error is never cleared when another bill is picked or the sheet closes.

Data, checked read-only in dos_qa (Tarsun, tenant 01a0947d-7a79-75d2-bfff-97e499a58d49):
- INV/0634 (paid, no notes): Sunbake Glucose 55 g 40 pc, case 120, rate 748. Campa Lemon 48 + 2 free, case 24. Godavari Cow Ghee 20, case 24. Konkan Farsan 40, case 20. Annapurna 9, case 12.
- INV/0546: Campa Cola 288 + 12 free, 6 credited on CN/0028 (issued).
- INV/0619: Godavari Dahi 60, 30 credited on CN/0056 (issued).
- INV/9002: cancelled. It is still returned by invoices.list q-search (no state filter), and the server refuses it with 409 because CREDITABLE_INVOICE_STATES at :88 excludes cancelled.

changes.what:
Pure, dependency-free home for the credit cap, so the device and the server use one rule. This follows the priceOrder() pattern: one engine in @dos/domain used by both the API and the apps.
- `piecesLeftToCredit(line: { qtyPcs: number; freeQtyPcs: number }, creditedPcs: number): number` returns `line.qtyPcs + line.freeQtyPcs - creditedPcs`. It is NOT clamped, so the server message stays byte-identical. The screen clamps for display.
- `creditedPiecesByLine(notes: readonly { state: string; lines: readonly { invoiceLineId: string; qtyPcs: number }[] }[]): Map<string, number>` sums qtyPcs per invoiceLineId over notes whose state !== 'cancelled'. Its JSDoc names it the device mirror of CreditNotesService.creditedByLine (credit-notes.service.ts:525-543): drafts count, cancelled notes do not.
- `state` is a plain string because the domain library cannot import contracts.
Add `export * from './credit-notes.js'`.
The two DOS-021 domain-unit specs listed under tests. They fail before the fix because the module does not exist.

One line, no behaviour change. At :308 replace `source.qtyPcs + source.freeQtyPcs - (credited.get(source.id) ?? 0)` with `piecesLeftToCredit(source, credited.get(source.id) ?? 0)`, imported from '@dos/domain'.
- The refusal message, its data {invoiceLineId, remaining, requested} and creditedByLine's SQL are untouched.
- billing.spec.ts:783 and :837 must pass unmodified.
- Do not touch rate handling (:316-324) or anything else.

Add `export type PiecesParseResult = { readonly ok: true; readonly pieces: number } | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: 'empty' | 'unparseable' }` and `export function parsePieces(text: string): PiecesParseResult`, modelled on parseRupees (money.ts:54-74).
- Trim. An empty field returns 'empty'.
- Strip commas and whitespace, so 1,200 is accepted.
- Require /^\d+$/ and Number.isSafeInteger, else 'unparseable'. This refuses 1.5, -3, 5abc and 1e3 and never truncates the way Number.parseInt does (stock/index.tsx:366/:428 truncates today; leave those screens alone).
- It reaches screens through shared.ts (`export * from './qty.js'`), so parity.test.ts is unaffected.
- QtyStepper, stepByCase and the kit strings stay unchanged: they are order-entry controls.
Add the two DOS-021 parsePieces specs listed under tests. Before the fix the named import is undefined, so each spec throws and fails while the existing qty specs keep passing.

Drafting Sheet only.
(a) Drop the QtyStepper import (:24). Import `billLineQty` and `parsePieces` from '@dos/ui', and `piecesLeftToCredit` and `creditedPiecesByLine` from '@dos/domain' (the screen already imports uuidv7 from there).
(b) `returning` becomes Record<string, string>: the typed text per line. It is still reset on bill pick (:343-346), on close (:312-316) and on success.
(c) Read earlier credits.
- `priorIds` = `bill.data.item.creditNotes`, state !== 'cancelled', mapped to id.
- `const prior = useQuery(['creditNotes','onBill', billId ?? 'none', ...priorIds], () => Promise.all(priorIds.map((id) => api.api.billing.creditNotes.get({ id }).then((r) => r.item))), { enabled: billId !== null && bill.data !== undefined })`.
- The query returns the JSON-safe note details, never a Map (the query cache repaints from stored values). The screen derives `credited = creditedPiecesByLine(prior.data ?? [])` in render.
- A bill with no notes makes no network call. The existing ['creditNotes'] and ['invoices'] invalidations on create, issue and cancel refresh it.
- Wrap the lines in `<Async state={[bill, prior]}>`. A disabled query is 'idle', so this never shows an endless skeleton.
(d) For each line:
- `left = Math.max(0, piecesLeftToCredit(line, credited.get(line.id) ?? 0))`.
- Replace the meta Txt at :381-383 (`${qtyPcs} pcs`, which hides free goods) with `billLineQty(line)`. That is the existing kit pattern already used at manager billing/index.tsx:472, and it prints the free-goods clause.
- Render `<TextInput label={t('m8.piecesToCredit')} keyboard="decimal" maxLength={7} value={returning[line.id] ?? ''} onChange={…} state={left === 0 ? 'disabled' : undefined} helper={left > 0 ? t('m8.leftToCredit', { left: formatCount(left) }) : t('m8.nothingLeft')} error={unparseable ? t('m8.wholePieces') : pieces > left ? t('m8.overLeft', { left: formatCount(left) }) : undefined} testID={`return-${line.id}`} />`.
- Never clamp silently: UX-00 §6.3 forbids silent clamping and §6.2 defines the error line.
(e) `draftLines` keeps only lines whose text parses with 0 < pieces ≤ left. `invalid` is true when any non-empty entry is unparseable or over its cap. The Draft button gets `disabled={draftLines.length === 0 || invalid}` and `disabledReason={invalid ? t('m8.fixPieces') : t('app.nothingChanged')}`.
(f) Move the `create.error` Txt (:417-421) to directly ABOVE the Draft button in the same Stack. Call `create.reset()` in the bill ListRow onPress and in the Sheet onClose, so one bill's refusal never shows against another. If DOS-029 lands a shared mutation-error surface first, use it at this position.
Unchanged: the reason chips, `saleable: reason !== 'return_damaged'`, `ratePaise: line.ratePaise`, the per-line `uuidv7()` in the mutation run (:135), the payload and its invalidations. See reviewNotes for the defects those leave.

Add to the m8 block (:431-447):
- 'm8.piecesToCredit': 'Pieces to credit'
- 'm8.leftToCredit': '{left} pc left to credit'
- 'm8.nothingLeft': 'Already credited in full'
- 'm8.overLeft': 'Only {left} pc left to credit on this line'
- 'm8.wholePieces': 'Type whole pieces, like 5 or 40'
- 'm8.fixPieces': 'Fix the pieces marked in red first'
The planner's 'm8.billedLeft' is dropped. It labelled qtyPcs + freeQtyPcs as "billed", which is false for free goods, and billLineQty already prints the billed and free quantities.

plans.reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED
1. Test coverage of the cap. The plan's only tests covered parsePieces. The part most likely to be wrong, the cap (free pieces included, drafts counted, cancelled notes excluded), was inline arithmetic in a screen with no test runner, so nothing pinned it and the plan itself listed "device hint drifts" as a risk. I moved the rule into backend/libs/domain/src/credit-notes.ts:
   - piecesLeftToCredit, used by BOTH the screen and credit-notes.service.ts:308;
   - creditedPiecesByLine, the device mirror of creditedByLine;
   - two DOS-021 domain-unit specs.
   This is the existing priceOrder() pattern: one dependency-free rule in @dos/domain shared by the server and the Expo apps. The server message and data are unchanged.
2. False copy for free goods. The plan's helper "{billed} pc billed" used billed = qtyPcs + freeQtyPcs, so Campa Lemon would read "50 pc billed" when 48 were billed and 2 were free. It also left the old meta line (:381-383, qtyPcs only), which duplicated the figure and hid free goods. Replaced with kit billLineQty(line), the existing pattern at manager billing/index.tsx:472 that prints the free-goods clause, plus a helper that says only "{left} pc left to credit". 'm8.billedLeft' became 'm8.leftToCredit'.
3. Fully credited lines. A line with nothing left now renders its field with state='disabled' instead of an editable field that turns red on any keystroke. Added maxLength 7.
4. Query shape. The prior-credits query returns the JSON-safe note details, never a Map, and credited is derived in render. The api-client cache repaints from stored values, and a Map does not survive JSON.
5. Citations. UX-00 §6.2 is TextInput (label above, reserved helper, business-language error). The no-silent-clamping rule and "desk is a text field with inputMode=decimal" are in §6.3 (RupeeInput). §6.4 is where "Not ordered"/"available" are defined as QtyStepper copy.
6. Verify.
   - Added a tenant filter to the DB query.
   - Added the Android keypad check on the last line (no KeyboardAvoidingView anywhere in frontend/libs/ui/src/native).
   - Added a close-and-reopen check that the error clears.
   - Added the domain and core test commands against a dos_batch1_template copy.
7. Size S → M. Three workspaces are touched (domain, core, frontend kit and app), with four new specs and desk, phone and Android verification. Added 'api' to platforms because of the server swap.

CONFIRMED BY READING CODE, DATA AND EVIDENCE
- Every cited line in the root cause, including native/money.tsx:474-480 carrying the same "Not ordered"/"available" copy (so Android and iOS are equally affected).
- The desk panel scrolls (overflowY:auto) and the sentence is clipped below the button in 13e-credit-note-400.png.
- useMutation.reset() exists.
- The invoice detail returns cancelled notes too, so the client filter is required.
- invoices.list q-search returns cancelled INV/9002.
- CREDIT_NOTE_RAISERS includes manager and accountant.
- The owner app never calls creditNotes.create.
- 1,530 of 6,202 lines are below one case.
- CN/0028 = 6 pc and CN/0056 = 30 pc.
- No existing credit_note_line exceeds its invoice line's qty_pcs.

COULD NOT CONFIRM
- The DOS-029 plan's shape: it is not in the repo, and another session's task output mentions DOS-029 only in passing. If DOS-029 adds a shared mutation-error surface, this screen must use it at the position set here (above the Draft button); land DOS-029 first or in the same cluster.
- The exact words of the kit string qty.freeGoods.
- Native keypad behaviour inside the Modal sheet (read-only session, no emulator).
- I made no API calls: sign-in is a POST that writes a session. Everything else was established from code, SQL and the evidence files.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS THIS FIX MAKES EASIER TO REACH (not fixed here; propose new findings, do not widen DOS-021)
(a) Discounted lines are credited at the gross rate. The screen sends ratePaise: line.ratePaise, and the server caps only rate ≤ invoiced gross rate (credit-notes.service.ts:316-321). On 1,881 of 6,202 lines taxable = rate×qty − discount, so every credit on those lines over-credits. Existing CN/0004 credited 6 × 2263 against a net of about 2218 per piece.
(b) Free goods are credited at the full rate (lineTaxable = rate × qtyPcs, :324). Crediting all 50 Campa Lemon credits 50 × 2275 against a line billed at 48 × 2275. The UI mirrors the server's cap (qty + free), as the finding's suggested fix implies, so the valuation question stays the server's.
(c) Retry after a lost reply. The screen generates each line's uuidv7() inside the mutation run (credit-notes.tsx:135), and runIdempotent hashes the whole input (core/src/platform/idempotency.ts:55-71). So a same-intent retry whose first attempt committed gets 409 "idempotencyKey was already used with a different request", a machine sentence that this fix will now display above the button.

plans.title: Demo seed writes owner_summary.detail key 'ageingB90Plus', but the owner/manager dashboard reads 'ageingB90plus', so Today shows 90+ = ₹0.00 until the worker's next rollup
plans.rootCause:
The frontend is not the cause, so the finding's suggested fix is wrong. Owner Today reads `d?.ageing.b90plus` (frontend/owner-app/app/index.tsx:206). Money → Outstanding reads `totals?.buckets.b90plus` (frontend/owner-app/app/money/index.tsx:231) into the same `<AgeingBuckets>` component. Manager/accountant Today reads `d?.ageing.b90plus` (frontend/manager-app/app/index.tsx:379) from the same endpoint (manager-app/app/index.tsx:62-66).

The defect is a key-spelling mismatch in the untyped jsonb column `owner_summary.detail`, declared as `detail: jsonb('detail')` (backend/libs/database/src/schema/reporting.ts:262). It has one reader and two writers in different packages:
- **Reader.** `ReportingService.dashboardOwner()` casts `detail` to `Record<string, unknown>` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/reporting/reporting.service.ts:228). `fromDetail(key: string)` returns 0 for a missing key (:229-232), and 90+ is `fromDetail('ageingB90plus')` (:239).
- **Worker writer, correct.** `refreshOwnerSummary` writes `ageingB90plus: n(dues?.b90plus)` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/reporting/rollup.ts:581). It gets the live row, whose SQL alias is `b90plus` (rollup.ts:197), via rollup.ts:267.
- **Seed writer, wrong.** `seedReportingClose` writes `ageingB90Plus: n(dues?.b90_plus)` (backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/reporting.ts:964, capital P). Its own SQL alias is `b90_plus` (:924). The other six keys match (reporting.ts:958-963 vs rollup.ts:575-580), and the value is right.

Why every seeded tenant gets the bad key on every seed run:
- `seedReportingClose` is the last write of every `seedDemo` run (backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/index.ts:342).
- `seedExtraTenants` runs `seedDemo` for each extra distributor (seed-demo/tenants.ts:539, :610).
- `seedDemo` has no early return on a re-run: `resolveDemoToday` only picks the anchor (index.ts:170-218).

How long the bad row lives: the worker's `scheduleRollups` fans out a rollup for every active tenant (backend/worker/src/jobs/reporting.ts:55-66) on `*/15` (:96). So the bad row lasts until the next tick, or indefinitely while the worker is down (QA/ENV.md:133 records it dying once during the walk).

Ruled out as contributing causes:
- No offline/sync path: owner_summary is not in sync-tables.
- No trigger or RLS effect: policy `owner_summary_back_office` admits owner/manager/accountant/system, so both writers and the reader see the row.
- The kit component is not at fault: Money → Outstanding uses the same component on the same platform and shows 35,144.

Test gap that let this through:
- reporting.spec.ts:430 inserts `ageingB90plus: 200_000`, but the only dashboard test (:917-923) asserts `cashInTransitPaise` and `ageing.b0_7` and never `b90plus`.
- No test covers the seed's owner_summary row.

The evidence timeline confirms this, and explains why the finding's API capture contradicts its screenshot:
- **Seed time.** dos_qa tenants were created at 12:50:46, 12:50:55 and 12:51:01 IST. The seed's `asOf: occurred(atIstTime(TODAY,18,0))` is clamped to the wall clock (seed-demo/util.ts:109-113).
- **Owner Today, seed-written row.** QA/evidence/phase1/owner/01-home-desk.txt (mtime 12:58:24) shows "as of 12 Sep, 12:50 pm" and 90+ 0.00.
- **Money screen, live data.** 10-money.txt (12:59:11) shows 35,144.00.
- **Network capture, worker-written row.** net-home/05-GET-…dashboard_owner.json (13:03:57) has asOf 2026-09-12T07:30:29Z (13:00:29 IST), detail keys in the worker's spelling, and b90plus 3514400.
- **Manager Today, worker-written row.** manager/01-home-desk.txt (13:48:43) shows "as of 1:45 pm" and 90+ 35,144.00. So the manager walkthrough's note "DOS-001 is owner-app only" (QA/findings/02-walkthrough-manager.md:421) is a timing artefact: the manager app has the same defect on a seed-written row.
- **Current dos_qa.** The latest as_of is 22:15 IST for all six tenants. Every row is worker-written, carries no `ageingB90Plus` key, and `detail->>'ageingB90plus'` equals `sum(bucket_90_plus_paise)` (tarsun 2596200 = 2596200).

plans.risk:
Low, with one deploy-window edge the original plan missed.

Idempotent replays can return 500 for 24 hours after the restart
- `runIdempotent` returns the STORED reply as-is on a replay (backend/libs/core/src/platform/idempotency.ts:61-73).
- oRPC validates every handler output against the contract (`validateOutput` in @orpc/server dist shared/server.DEBcqOjg.mjs:178-191 throws INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR "Output validation failed").
- So once the services run the new contract, replaying any order-returning mutation stored before the restart answers 500 instead of the stored reply. That means the same idempotencyKey with the same payload, for orders create/setLines/repeatLast/submit/confirm/cancel, orders.approvals.decide, ai.drafts.confirm or delivery.vanSales.create.
- It lasts until `idempotency_keys` retention removes the row: 24 h, and only while the worker runs (backend/worker/src/jobs/retention.ts:9,28).
- dos_qa holds 24 such stored replies right now, all under 24 h old.
- Real exposure: the api-client reuses a key for an unchanged input, so a user retrying the same intent across the restart can hit it. `pnpm smoke` keys non-run-scoped mutations by IST date, so use a fresh `--run-tag`.
- Accepted as a local, pre-deployment window. Making the field optional would weaken the contract, and re-deriving replies in `idempotent()` is a platform change outside DOS-003.

Other risks
- Persisted query cache: a pre-fix cached `orders.get` repaints with an empty name row until the background revalidation lands (api-client cache.ts, client.hydrate). It is transient.
- Cost: one extra indexed query per OrderDetail reply (a PK `IN` on product_variants plus the unique `(tenant_id, variant_id)` listing index; the largest dos_qa order has 12 lines). It runs on every reply listed under contractChange, not on sync uploads.
- Build-order trap: services and apps read `@dos/contracts` and `@dos/core` from dist. Skipping the rebuild leaves the running API without the field and fails the frontend typecheck on `line.variantName`.
- `pnpm docs:readme` must run or CI `docs:readme:check` fails; six service READMEs change.
- Behaviour: a tenant `local_alias` shows on the order panel, which matches the bill (billing.internals.ts:197) and the retailer app (shop.ts:85). The warehouse picking sheet prints the global name (warehouse.internals.ts:101-104), so for an aliased item the order panel and picking sheet would differ. No dos_qa listing has an alias today.
- Manager wording: 'Inner' becomes 'inner', the bill panel's wording.
- Merge conflicts are likely with the batch findings listed in dependsOn.

plans.title: Link each bargain gate to the bargain request it waits on, so one decision closes both and each queue shows one named row per bargain
plans.rootCause:
The server and all three decision screens are both wrong.

(1) Nothing links the two records.
- Owner Approvals merges `orders.approvals.list` (frontend/owner-app/app/approvals.tsx:60-62, mapped :68-79) with `pricing.bargains.list` (:63-65, mapped :80-91) and never pairs them.
- The owner home `waiting` list (frontend/owner-app/app/index.tsx:62-67, :100-113) does the same.
- So does the manager's "Waiting for a decision" (frontend/manager-app/app/orders/index.tsx:136-141, :268-283). The manager walk recorded the same pair there: an unnamed "Bargain / —" card (approval 29e03a4b) next to "Om Sai Provision Store — Asked rate ₹39.58" (bargain 011d0c51), QA/findings/02-walkthrough-manager.md:402.
- The approval row has no `payload.orderNo`, so "What" falls back to `row.entityType` and reads "bargain_request" (approvals.tsx:72, index.tsx:104).

Seeded approvals name their bargain; product-created gates do not.
- The seed writes `approvals(kind='bargain', entity_type='bargain_request', entity_id=<bargain id>, order_id null)` for every requested bargain (backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/reporting.ts:479-497).
- Product gates lose the link. `approvalFlags` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.internals.ts:140-156) sets 'bargain' when `hasPendingBargain` (:158-175) finds any requested bargain for the order's retailer and variants (order_id null or this order).
- `submitInTx` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts:288-300) then inserts the gate with `entityType 'sales_order'` and `entityId` = order id. The bargain is never named, so no screen can pair the rows.
- `hasPendingBargain` is also a documented cross-module read of pricing's table (comment at :158).
- The sales app sends the draft's orderId with a bargain request (frontend/sales-app/app/orders/new.tsx:640-648), so the normal flow (ask a rate, then submit) creates the pair. The retailer app asks without an orderId (frontend/retailer-app/app/order.tsx:273-282), which gates every later order of that shop for that variant.

(2) A decision on one record never reaches the other.
- `ApprovalsService.decide` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/approvals.service.ts:84-95) updates only `approvals`.
- It returns at :97 when there is no order, and otherwise only cancels or confirms the order (:99-112). `bargain_requests` stays `requested` with decided_by null (finding: 1221ccf5 still requested while 4ffb552c is rejected).
- The bargain stays approvable through `BargainsService.decide` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/pricing/bargains.service.ts:144-179).
- The reverse is open too: `BargainsService.decide` never touches the gate, and pricing sits upstream of orders, so it cannot import orders.

Current dos_qa state (read-only SELECTs, 2026-09-12). This corrects the original plan's "every requested bargain has a pending approval":
- tarsun has 3 requested bargains:
  - 011d0c51 (Om Sai), approval 29e03a4b pending.
  - 1221ccf5 (Mahalaxmi), approval 4ffb552c already rejected in the walk, so it now shows once, as a Rate request.
  - 01a0958e, no approval; its order_id points at a draft that was never uploaded (DOS-090).
- kalyan-agencies and sai-distributors each have 2 seeded pending pairs.
- No pending bargain approval anywhere uses the old 'sales_order' shape.

The finding's alternative, "the approval row should not exist for bargains", is wrong. The gate is what holds the order at `submitted` (approvals.service.ts:109-112). The fix makes the gate name the bargain (the seed's shape) and has the gate's decision decide the bargain in the same transaction.

RLS stays compatible:
- `approvals_retailer_insert` (migration 0012:250) only checks `order_id` ownership. Gate rows keep `orderId`, so a shop's own submit can still insert them.
- `bargain_requests_decide` (0012:188) admits owner and manager, the same actors `orders.approvals.decide` admits (permissions.ts:527).

changes.what:
Two additions.

1. Public `decideInTx(tx, ctx, { id, decision, approvedRatePaise?, note? }, opts?: { ifStillRequested?: boolean }): Promise<Bargain | null>`, holding the current body of `decide` (lines 150-176): load, NOT_FOUND, 409 unless `requested`, approved rate <= list rate, and the update of status, approvedRatePaise, decidedBy, decidedAt, `note ?? existing.note` and updatedAt.
   - Make the write a compare-and-set: `.where(and(eq(bargainRequests.id, existing.id), eq(bargainRequests.status, 'requested')))`. With no row returned, answer null when `ifStillRequested`, otherwise the same 409 `Bargain is already …`.
   - Why: today neither path locks the bargain row, so an approval decision and a Rate-request decision in two transactions could both pass the status check and overwrite each other.
   - `decide` becomes `requireRole(MANAGEMENT)` → `withTenant` → `idempotent` → `decideInTx` with no opts, so `pricing.bargains.decide` answers exactly as today (200/400/404/409).

2. A plain exported function (no DI) `pendingBargainsForOrder(tx, { retailerId, orderId, variantIds }): Promise<string[]>`.
   - Body: the WHERE of `hasPendingBargain` verbatim (retailer, status requested, variant in variantIds, order_id null OR = orderId), ordered by id, no limit, `[]` when variantIds is empty.
   - Why a plain function: this is the pattern orders already uses for receivables (`checkCredit` / `loadRetailerCredit` imported at orders.internals.ts:42). It keeps `OrdersService`'s constructor unchanged.
Add `pendingBargainsForOrder` to the `./bargains.service.js` export line (line 5).

- `approvalFlags(tx, order, lines)` (lines 140-156) keeps its signature and returns `{ flags, bargainIds }`.
- `bargainIds = await pendingBargainsForOrder(tx, { retailerId: order.retailerId, orderId: order.id, variantIds: [...new Set(lines.map((l) => l.variantId))] })`, imported from '../pricing/index.js'.
- 'bargain' is pushed when `bargainIds.length > 0`. The credit and below_floor logic is untouched.
- Delete `hasPendingBargain` (:158-175) and the `bargainRequests` import (:33). Drop `inArray` / `isNull` / `or` only if nothing else in the file uses them.
- Update the docblock (:134-139): the bargain gate lists the requests it waits on.

In `submitInTx` only; NO constructor change:
- Line 266 becomes `const { flags, bargainIds } = await approvalFlags(tx, order, lines)`. `approvalFlags: flags` on the order and the returned `flags` stay the same, so vansales.service.ts:88-93 and ai/drafts.service.ts:167 are unaffected.
- Lines 288-300: non-'bargain' kinds insert exactly as today.
- For 'bargain', insert one row per id in `bargainIds`: `entityType: 'bargain_request'`, `entityId: bargainId`, `orderId: next.id`, `payload: { orderNo: next.orderNo, totalPaise: next.totalPaise, flag: 'bargain' }`, everything else as today.
- `stillPending` (approvals.service.ts:118-131) already confirms the order only when every gate is cleared.

Not touched: `backend/libs/core/src/modules/billing/worker-services.ts:35` builds `new OrdersService(db, new QuoteService(db), inventory)` by hand. The original plan's injection of `BargainsService` into `OrdersService` would have failed `pnpm typecheck` there.

- Inject `BargainsService` from '../pricing/index.js' in the constructor (lines 39-42). DI-only: `git grep 'new ApprovalsService('` finds no hand-built copy. OrdersModule already imports PricingModule (orders.module.ts:22), which exports BargainsService (pricing.module.ts:30).
- In `decide`, right after the approval update (:85-95) and before `if (!approval.orderId)` (:97): when `approval.kind === 'bargain' && approval.entityType === 'bargain_request'`, call `await this.bargains.decideInTx(tx, ctx, { id: approval.entityId, decision: input.decision, ...(input.note ? { note: input.note } : {}) }, { ifStillRequested: true })`.
- Approve takes the asked rate. A bargain already decided elsewhere keeps its outcome. A missing bargain is a 404, which rolls the whole decision back.
- This runs inside the existing `withTenant` + `idempotent()`. No second transaction and no nested `idempotent`, so a replay returns the stored reply without deciding twice.
- Update the class docblock (:32-36).

Pair the two streams on the queue.

1. Add `gates = useQuery(['approvals', 'pending', 'bargain'], () => api.api.orders.approvals.list({ status: 'pending', kind: 'bargain', limit: 200 }))`. It makes pairing independent of the 100-row page. The `['approvals']` invalidation already covers it by prefix.

plans.reviewNotes:
What I changed from the original plan:

1. Build break fixed. The original injected `BargainsService` into `OrdersService`'s constructor, but `backend/libs/core/src/modules/billing/worker-services.ts:35` hand-builds `new OrdersService(db, new QuoteService(db), inventory)` for the worker, so `pnpm typecheck` would fail. The lookup is now a plain exported function `pendingBargainsForOrder` in pricing, following the receivables `checkCredit` / `loadRetailerCredit` pattern orders already imports (orders.internals.ts:42). `approvalFlags` keeps its parameters and `OrdersService`'s constructor is untouched. Only `ApprovalsService` gets DI, and it is never hand-built.

2. Race closed. `decideInTx` now writes with a compare-and-set (`where id and status = 'requested'`). Neither path locks the bargain row, so an approval decision and a Rate-request decision in parallel transactions could both pass the status check. The non-race behaviour of `pricing.bargains.decide` is identical.

3. Frontend regression removed.
   - The original only filtered the bargain row on the manager and home lists. There the surviving approval row is the unnamed "Bargain / —" or "bargain_request" card, so the manager would lose the named "Om Sai — Asked rate ₹39.58" card recorded at 02-walkthrough-manager.md:402. All three screens now take the kept row's shop and rate from the bargain.
   - On owner Approvals, a gated bargain would have vanished from the Rate requests segment. That segment now also lists approval rows of kind 'bargain'.

4. Page-size pairing made sound where decisions happen. `approvals.list` sorts newest first and `bargains.list` oldest first, so within 100/100 (owner) and 20/20 (manager) pages a gated bargain can appear without its gate. There the manager's buttons would call `pricing.bargains.decide` and leave the gate pending. Both decision screens now add `orders.approvals.list({ status: 'pending', kind: 'bargain', limit: 200 })` to know every gate and show it. The display-only home list pairs within its page, which is correct for display.

5. Spec 1 now asks for the bargain through POST /pricing/bargains with orderId, the path the sales app uses, instead of a raw insert. Spec 3 was added for the new per-bargain gate count and the stillPending interplay, with a cleanup cancel. All specs sit at the end of the describe.

1. The request half works; nothing picks up the hand-off.
- `ReceivablesService.sendStatements` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/receivables/receivables.service.ts:1264-1304) writes one `StatementRequested` row per shop via `emitEvent` (:1292).
- Payload: {jobId, retailerId, from, to, channel, includeUpiQr}, no figures. Answer: {jobId, queued} (contracts receivables.ts:631-650, route :890-898).
- Its JSDoc (:1260-1263) says "the worker renders and sends them", which is untrue.

2. No consumer exists.
- The worker registers relay handlers for `DocumentRenderRequested` (backend/worker/src/main.ts:35), the docint, integrations, notifications, reporting, incentives and ai jobs, and nothing else.
- Notifications registers only `NOTIFICATION_EVENT_TYPES` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/notifications/events.ts:37-45: OrderConfirmed, OrderCancelled, OrderSubmitted, InvoiceIssued, DeliveryRecorded, ReceiptRecorded, retailer.identity_linked), in the loop at backend/worker/src/jobs/notifications.ts:162-169, plus `TripDeparted` (:170-173).
- The relay claims only rows whose type has a handler: doc comment at backend/worker/src/jobs/outbox-relay.ts:20-21, claim filter `event_type in (registered types)` at :138-141. So the row waits forever.
- dos_qa confirms it (read today): outbox_events 01a09495-c809-7650-a307-921e525dd3dd is the only StatementRequested row, published_at null, attempts 0, dead_lettered_at null. Prerna's newest messages row is order_confirmed on 2026-09-11.
- No statement template exists anywhere:
  - dos_qa holds 21 platform templates and none has key 'statement';
  - `PLATFORM_TEMPLATES` (backend/libs/database/src/seed-demo/notifications.ts:70-197) and `PLATFORM_TEMPLATE_KEYS` (backend/libs/contracts/src/notifications.ts:183-194) have none;
  - platform templates come only from the demo seed (no migration inserts any; grep of migrations/ for 'order_confirmed' finds nothing).
- History: the planned `receivables.statement_render` job (docs/plans/receivables.md:241) died with the PDF deferral (docs/plans/00-coordination.md §3.4), and docs/23-app-screens-and-api-gaps.md:196 records "statements (O10, renderer deferred)".

3. The owner app hides the outcome, at BOTH owner entry points to this call.
- Shops panel: frontend/owner-app/app/shops/index.tsx:119-132 builds the mutation; :370 does `statement.mutateAsync(current.id).then(done, done)`.
- Money O10: frontend/owner-app/app/money/index.tsx:106-118 builds the same call; :428-431 `.then(done, done)`.
- Success and refusal both just close the dialog. 'o6.statementSent' (frontend/owner-app/src/strings.ts:203) is never used.
- No owner-app screen uses a Toast. approvals.tsx:132's comment says the error is "rendered under the dialog", but no Dialog prop or render does it. The only working precedent is the delivery app's `Toast` with `error.message` (delivery-app/app/stop/[id]/index.tsx:127-130). `useMutation().mutateAsync` rejects with `ApiError extends Error` (frontend/libs/api-client/src/react/index.tsx:307, 397-400; errors.ts:41).
- The manager app's M14 (frontend/manager-app/app/shops/index.tsx:447) has the same swallow; DOS-029 covers that app.

No second backend cause:
- RLS lets the system actor read journal_lines (back-office policy includes system) and write messages.
- The outbox row is well formed; channel 'whatsapp' is what all three callers send.

plans.risk:
- **Real sends:** with Meta/MSG91 credentials, shops now actually receive statements. A 200-shop O10 run queues up to 200 rows, drained by the relay (100 × 10 per tick) and dispatch (≤ 200 per tick). Locally the stub provider is used.
- **Meta approval:** real WhatsApp needs an approved `statement_en` template in Meta. Until then the Meta provider fails, dispatch backs off 1m/5m/30m/2h/12h and dead-letters at five, and the row shows Failed in Settings → Messages. That is honest, but it isn't a send.
- **Empty variables:** when there is no VPA, dues ≤ 0 or includeUpiQr=false, the body reads "Pay by UPI:  — Tarsun Enterprise". invoice_issued already does the same. Meta may reject an empty text parameter; this is pre-existing and not widened here.
- **Load:** per event, two indexed aggregates on one shop's AR lines (journal_lines_party_idx), one rollup row read, one template resolve and one insert, off the request path, on separate connections like the other translators.
- **Missing templates:** a database whose templates were not re-seeded skips every statement as 'template_not_found' (logged; the outbox row is published). Production platform templates exist only through the demo seed, a pre-existing gap.
- **Stale guard:** a StatementRequested row older than 48 h (for example, the worker was down two days) is published and not sent, the same as the other translators.
- **pdf refusal:** 'pdf' moves from 200 to 501. No app sends it.
- **Refactor:** moving opening/closing into `ledgerBalances` and moving the constant touch the ledger.get path; the closing-balance spec (receivables.spec.ts:831-846) and the new DOS-007 equality test guard it.
- **Replay:** the api-client keys the idempotency key on the input (react/index.tsx:377-389). Pressing Send statement twice for the same shop on the same day replays job 1 (no second message) and still shows "queued". That is intended, not spam.
- **Merge overlap:** DOS-095, if its fix moves server-side into retailerLedger, and DOS-094 in the same receivables.service.ts.
